title: A Cup You Can Eat
paragraphs: Every day, the shop at Green Hill High School sells hundreds of cold drinks. The cups are used once and then thrown away, and many of them [[remain|L3-0716]] in the ground for years. The science club did not like this [[situation|L3-0800]]. They wanted to [[reduce|L3-0707]] the waste, so they decided to [[invent|L3-0442]] a new kind of cup.

The club [[explored|L3-0301]] [[various|L3-0954]] ideas. Online, they found useful [[information|L3-0433]] about seaweed, a natural [[resource|L3-0726]] that grows fast in the sea. The [[process|L3-0673]] of making the cups was not easy. The students boiled the seaweed, mixed it with water, and dried it into the shape of a cup. Many of their first cups broke, but they did not give up.

Two months later, they finally made a [[unique|L3-0946]] [[product|L3-0675]]: a soft green cup that you can eat after you finish your drink. If it is thrown away, it breaks down in the soil within weeks. The club put up [[ads|L3-0011]] around the school, and the new cups soon [[attracted|L3-0043]] many students. Their teacher, Ms. Lin, was [[amazed|L3-0021]]. "We cannot get [[rid|L3-0732]] of all the waste at once," she said, "but you have shown that one small idea can make a difference."
zh: 綠丘高中的福利社每天賣出好幾百杯冷飲。這些杯子用過一次就被丟掉，其中很多會在土裡留存好幾年。科學社不喜歡這種情況。他們想減少垃圾，於是決定發明一種新的杯子。
社員們探索了各種想法。他們在網路上找到關於海藻的實用資訊；海藻是一種在海裡長得很快的天然資源。做杯子的過程並不容易。學生們把海藻煮過，加水混合，再把它乾燥成杯子的形狀。他們最初做的杯子很多都破掉了，但他們沒有放棄。
兩個月後，他們終於做出一項獨特的產品：一個柔軟的綠色杯子，喝完飲料後可以直接吃掉。就算被丟掉，它也會在幾週內於土壤中分解。社團在校園各處張貼廣告，新杯子很快就吸引了許多學生。他們的老師林老師感到很驚奇。她說：「我們沒辦法一下子擺脫所有的垃圾，但你們證明了一個小點子就能帶來改變。」

questions.stem: Why did the science club decide to make a new kind of cup?
options: The school shop wanted cups that cost less.
They wanted to cut down on the waste from used cups.
Their teacher asked them to enter a science contest.
Students said the old cups were too small.
questions.explain: 第一段說社員不喜歡杯子用一次就丟、留在土裡多年的情況，所以「想減少垃圾」而決定發明新杯子，故選 (B)。文中沒有提到福利社想省錢，(A) 是無中生有。
questions.evidence: They wanted to reduce the waste, so they decided to invent a new kind of cup.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, how did the students make the cups?
options: They grew seaweed on the land near the school.
They mixed paper with sugar and baked it.
They boiled seaweed, mixed it with water, and dried it into a cup shape.
questions.explain: 第二段明確寫出步驟：把海藻煮過、加水混合、再乾燥成杯子形狀，故選 (D)。(A) 只抓到 online 這個字，但他們是在網路上「找資料」，不是買杯子。
questions.evidence: The students boiled the seaweed, mixed it with water, and dried it into the shape of a cup.

questions.stem: The word "unique" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: unique 指「獨特的、與眾不同的」，可以吃的杯子正是一般杯子沒有的特色，與 special 最接近，故選 (C)。文中並沒說這杯子有名，(D) famous 不合。
questions.evidence: Two months later, they finally made a unique product: a soft green cup that you can eat after you finish your drink.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a group of students made a cup that people can eat
How seaweed grows fast in the sea
Why students at the school buy so many cold drinks
How a teacher helped her students win a prize
questions.explain: 全文從發現問題、研究海藻、反覆試做，到做出可食用杯子，主軸是學生發明可吃的杯子，故選 (A)。(B) 海藻長得快只是第二段的一個細節，不是全文重點。
questions.evidence: They wanted to reduce the waste, so they decided to invent a new kind of cup.

vocab.stem: Turning off the lights when you leave a room can ______ the amount of energy you use.
vocab.explain: 離開房間時關燈可以「減少」用電量，reduce the amount of energy 意思最通順，故選 reduce。attract（吸引）、invent（發明）、suffer（受苦）都無法和「能源用量」搭配。

vocab.stem: The new art show has ______ thousands of visitors since it opened last month.
vocab.explain: 新展覽開幕以來「吸引」了數千名參觀者，attract visitors 是常見搭配，故選 attracted。warned（警告）不合語意，展覽不會去警告參觀者。

title: Why Do Chameleons Change Color?
paragraphs: Many people believe that chameleons change color to hide from their enemies. The idea has a strong [[appeal|L3-0031]], and you can find it in many cartoons. However, [[scientists|L3-0767]] who [[observe|L3-0578]] these animals in nature tell a different story.

Many chameleons live in warm, [[tropical|L3-0932]] forests, and their [[normal|L3-0574]] colors, such as green and brown, already help them hide among the leaves. Scientists have found that color change is more important for two other reasons. First, it helps a chameleon control its body heat. On a cool morning, it may turn dark so that its body can take in more heat from the sun. Second, color is a way to share [[information|L3-0433]] with other chameleons.

When a male chameleon [[recognizes|L3-0704]] the [[presence|L3-0668]] of another male, he may [[react|L3-0699]] by turning bright colors to show that this [[location|L3-0501]] belongs to him. Often the weaker one turns dark and walks away, which helps [[prevent|L3-0670]] a fight. The colors [[vary|L3-0955]] from one kind of chameleon to another, and each kind has its own [[specific|L3-0819]] way of using them. So the [[variety|L3-0953]] of colors you see is not just a trick. It is a [[unique|L3-0946]] language.
zh: 許多人相信變色龍變色是為了躲避敵人。這個說法很有吸引力，在許多卡通裡都看得到。然而，在大自然中觀察這些動物的科學家，看到的卻是另一回事。
許多變色龍住在溫暖的熱帶森林裡，牠們平常的顏色，例如綠色和褐色，本來就能幫助牠們藏身在樹葉之間。科學家發現，變色其實另有兩個更重要的原因。第一，變色能幫助變色龍控制體溫。在涼爽的早晨，牠可能會變成深色，好讓身體從陽光中吸收更多熱。第二，顏色是牠和其他變色龍分享訊息的一種方式。
當一隻雄變色龍察覺到另一隻雄性出現時，牠可能會變成鮮豔的顏色作為回應，表示這個地方是屬於牠的。通常較弱的一方會轉成深色然後走開，這有助於避免一場打鬥。顏色會因變色龍的種類而有所不同，每一種都有自己特定的用色方式。所以你看到的各種顏色不只是一種把戲，而是一種獨特的語言。

questions.stem: According to the passage, why might a chameleon turn dark on a cool morning?
options: To take in more heat from the sun
To show that it is angry
To find food among the leaves
questions.explain: 第二段說涼爽早晨變色龍會變深色，「好讓身體從陽光中吸收更多熱」，故選 (B)。(A) 正是第一段提到的一般人誤解，不是文中給的理由。
questions.evidence: On a cool morning, it may turn dark so that its body can take in more heat from the sun.

questions.stem: What often happens when two male chameleons meet?
options: They both hide among the leaves at once.
They change into the same color.
One of them turns dark and walks away, so they do not fight.
They both turn green and brown.
questions.explain: 第三段說較弱的一方常會轉成深色並走開，因此能避免打鬥，故選 (C)。(B) 說兩隻變成同色，文中並未提到；牠們反而是用不同顏色表達強弱。
questions.evidence: Often the weaker one turns dark and walks away, which helps prevent a fight.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3, what does "him" in "this location belongs to him" refer to?
options: The male chameleon that notices another male
questions.explain: 句子主詞是「察覺另一隻雄性出現的那隻雄變色龍」，牠變鮮豔是為了宣示這地方屬於自己，所以 him 指牠本身，選 (A)。(B) 是被宣示的對象，不是地方的主人。
questions.evidence: When a male chameleon recognizes the presence of another male, he may react by turning bright colors to show that this location belongs to him.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Chameleons change color only to hide from their enemies.
Most chameleons live in cold forests.
Cartoons always teach us true facts about animals.
Chameleons change color more to control body heat and share information than to hide.
questions.explain: 文章先提出「變色是為了躲藏」的常見說法，再用科學家的發現說明變色更重要的是調節體溫與傳遞訊息，故選 (D)。(A) 正是作者要修正的說法，與主旨相反。
questions.evidence: Scientists have found that color change is more important for two other reasons.

vocab.stem: Students were asked to ______ the moon every night for a month and write down how its shape changed.
vocab.explain: 連續一個月每晚「觀察」月亮並記錄形狀變化，observe 最合語意，故選 observe。prevent（預防）、unite（聯合）、react（反應）都無法接 the moon 表達觀察。

vocab.stem: Washing your hands often can help ______ the spread of disease.
vocab.explain: 常洗手可以幫助「預防」疾病傳播，prevent the spread of disease 是固定常見說法，故選 prevent。observe 是「觀察」，觀察疾病傳播不需要靠洗手，語意不合。

title: Ocean Night at the Sea Life Museum
paragraphs: Dear students, the Science Club has [[organized|L3-0591]] a special night at the Sea Life Museum on Friday, May 16. This is a rare [[opportunity|L3-0586]] to [[observe|L3-0578]] what sea [[creatures|L3-0202]] do after the lights go out.

We will meet at the school gate at 6 p.m. and take a bus to the museum. After it closes to the public, a guide will lead us through the dark halls. You will watch jellyfish [[float|L3-0328]] in the water and see a [[variety|L3-0953]] of fish that are [[awake|L3-0049]] only at night. Then we will sleep next to a huge glass wall, with sharks swimming on the other side. In the morning, a museum worker will talk about the [[protection|L3-0682]] of sea life and how our daily choices [[connect|L3-0183]] us to the ocean.

For your [[comfort|L3-0170]], bring a sleeping bag and a warm jacket. We [[advise|L3-0012]] you to eat dinner first, as no food is allowed inside. Do not [[wander|L3-0974]] away from the group or knock on the glass, since loud noises can scare the animals.
Only 40 places are available. To join, give the form to Ms. Lin by May 9. We will [[confirm|L3-0181]] your place by email. For more [[information|L3-0433]], visit Room 201.
zh: 各位同學好：科學社籌辦了 5 月 16 日（星期五）在海洋生物博物館的特別夜間活動。這是一個難得的機會，可以觀察海洋生物在熄燈後都在做些什麼。
我們晚上 6 點在校門口集合，搭巴士前往博物館。閉館之後，導覽員會帶我們走過漆黑的展廳。你會看到水母在水中漂浮，也能看到各式各樣只在夜間醒著的魚。接著我們會睡在一面巨大的玻璃牆旁，牆的另一邊就有鯊魚游來游去。隔天早上，博物館人員會談談海洋生物的保育，以及我們日常的選擇如何把自己和海洋連結在一起。
為了讓你舒適，請帶睡袋和保暖外套。我們建議你先吃過晚餐再來，因為館內禁止飲食。請勿脫隊亂逛，也不要敲玻璃，因為很大的聲響會嚇到動物。
名額只有 40 個。想參加的同學，請在 5 月 9 日前把報名表交給林老師。我們會用電子郵件確認你的名額。想知道更多資訊，請到 201 教室詢問。

questions.stem: By when must students give the form to Ms. Lin?
questions.explain: 最後一段寫明報名表要在 5 月 9 日前交給林老師，故選 (C)。5 月 16 日是活動當天，(A)、(B) 把活動日期誤當成報名期限。
questions.evidence: To join, give the form to Ms. Lin by May 9.

questions.stem: Which of the following are students asked NOT to do?
questions.explain: 第三段要求學生不要脫隊、不要敲玻璃，以免聲響嚇到動物，故選 (B)。(C) 先吃晚餐正是公告「建議」要做的事，不是禁止事項。
questions.evidence: Do not wander away from the group or knock on the glass, since loud noises can scare the animals.

questions.stem: What does "it" in "After it closes to the public" in paragraph 2 refer to?
questions.explain: 前一句說搭巴士到博物館，接著說「它閉館後」導覽員帶大家參觀，會對外關閉的是博物館，故選 (D)。(A) 巴士雖然在前一句出現，但巴士不會「對大眾關閉」。
questions.evidence: After it closes to the public, a guide will lead us through the dark halls.

questions.stem: What can we infer from the notice?
options: Students can buy food inside the museum.
Not every student who wants to go may get a place.
The trip will last for two nights.
The museum is open to the public all night.
questions.explain: 名額只有 40 個，而且要等電子郵件確認，可推知想去的人不一定都能參加，故選 (B)。(A) 與公告「館內禁止飲食」矛盾。
questions.evidence: Only 40 places are available.

vocab.stem: Our class plans to ______ a party at the end of the school year.
vocab.explain: 在學期末「籌辦」一場派對，organize a party 是常見搭配，故選 organize。confirm 是「確認」，要先有派對安排才能確認，放在這裡語意不完整。

vocab.stem: Before you leave for the airport, call the airline to ______ that your flight is still on time.
vocab.explain: 出發前打給航空公司「確認」班機是否準時，confirm that... 表示確認某事，故選 confirm。represent（代表）、connect（連接）、organize（籌辦）都不能接 that 子句表示確認某事。

title: The Hardest Player to Beat
paragraphs: Amy loved badminton and dreamed of a [[career|L3-0125]] as a player. She practiced hard every day. However, whenever she lost a game, she would [[complain|L3-0176]] about the noise, the light, or the wind in the gym. Her [[constant|L3-0186]] complaining made the other players on her team upset.

One evening, after Amy lost an important match by two points, her teacher, Mr. Chen, asked to speak with her. "You [[tend|L3-0898]] to [[rush|L3-0749]] when you fall behind," he said. "You hit too hard and too fast. Right now, your [[attitude|L3-0042]] is a bigger [[threat|L3-0907]] to you than any other player." He [[advised|L3-0012]] her to watch videos of her own games and see how she [[reacted|L3-0699]] when things went wrong.

The videos made a [[significant|L3-0793]] difference. Amy saw herself making angry [[gestures|L3-0356]] after every mistake. She decided to change her [[strategy|L3-0852]]: instead of trying to win every point at once, she would stay calm and wait for the right [[opportunity|L3-0586]]. When she [[competed|L3-0175]] in the city contest a month later, she [[barely|L3-0065]] won her first match, but she smiled at the end. For Amy, the win was [[proof|L3-0680]] that she could [[achieve|L3-0005]] more by controlling her feelings.
zh: 艾咪熱愛羽球，夢想成為職業選手。她每天都很努力練習。可是只要輸了比賽，她就會抱怨體育館裡的噪音、燈光或是風。她不停的抱怨讓隊上其他選手很不開心。
某天傍晚，艾咪在一場重要比賽中以兩分之差落敗，她的老師陳老師找她談話。他說：「你一落後就容易急躁。你打得太用力、也太快了。現在對你來說，你的態度比任何對手都更具威脅。」他建議她看自己比賽的影片，看看事情不順時自己是怎麼反應的。
這些影片帶來了顯著的改變。艾咪看到自己每次失誤後都做出生氣的手勢。她決定改變策略：不再急著每一分都拿下，而是保持冷靜，等待對的時機。一個月後她參加市賽時，第一場比賽贏得驚險，但她在比賽結束時露出了笑容。對艾咪來說，這場勝利證明了只要控制好情緒，她就能有更多成就。

questions.stem: What did Amy often do after she lost a game?
options: She complained about things around her, such as the noise.
She practiced alone in the gym all night.
She watched videos of her own games.
She asked Mr. Chen for help at once.
questions.explain: 第一段說艾咪一輸球就抱怨噪音、燈光或風，故選 (A)。(C) 看比賽影片是後來陳老師建議她做的，並不是她原本輸球後的習慣。
questions.evidence: However, whenever she lost a game, she would complain about the noise, the light, or the wind in the gym.

questions.stem: What did Mr. Chen advise Amy to do?
options: Watch videos of her own games
questions.explain: 第二段寫陳老師建議她看自己比賽的影片，觀察自己出錯時的反應，故選 (C)。(B) 正好相反，老師說她就是「打得太用力、太快」。
questions.evidence: He advised her to watch videos of her own games and see how she reacted when things went wrong.

questions.stem: The word "rush" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 陳老師接著解釋「你打得太用力、也太快」，可知 rush 指落後時急躁、動作太快，故選 (D)。(B) stay calm 正是她後來學會的做法，意思和 rush 相反。
questions.evidence: You hit too hard and too fast.

questions.stem: What can we learn about Amy from the passage?
options: She stopped playing badminton after the city contest.
She learned that controlling her feelings helped her play better.
She thought Mr. Chen's advice was not helpful.
She won her first match in the city contest by many points.
questions.explain: 最後一句說這場勝利證明她只要控制情緒就能有更多成就，可見她學到管理情緒有助於表現，故選 (B)。(D) 錯在「大比分獲勝」，文中用 barely 表示她是「勉強、驚險地」贏。
questions.evidence: For Amy, the win was proof that she could achieve more by controlling her feelings.

vocab.stem: Many students ______ to stay up late before exams, but sleep is important too.
vocab.explain: tend to + 原形動詞表示「往往會、容易會」，許多學生考前容易熬夜，故選 tend。complain 後面接 about 或 that 子句，不接 to stay up。

vocab.stem: Ten teams from different schools will ______ for the top prize in the dance contest.
vocab.explain: compete for the prize 表示「爭奪獎項」，十隊競爭冠軍最合語意，故選 compete。rush for 雖然有「衝向」的意思，但用在比賽爭奪獎項並不自然。

title: The Power of a Short Nap
paragraphs: In many high schools in Taiwan, students take a [[nap|L3-0564]] at their desks after lunch. Some people think this is a waste of time, but [[scientists|L3-0767]] have found that it brings real [[benefits|L3-0075]].

During the day, the brain gets more and more tired. A nap of [[roughly|L3-0745]] twenty minutes gives it a chance to rest. After a short nap, people [[tend|L3-0898]] to feel more [[awake|L3-0049]], and their [[mental|L3-0532]] skills, such as memory and attention, often improve. They also [[perform|L3-0629]] better on tasks that need quick [[responses|L3-0727]]. In other words, a short nap makes the brain more [[efficient|L3-0276]].

However, a longer nap is not always better. If a nap lasts longer than about thirty minutes, you may fall into deep sleep and wake up feeling heavy and slow. A late nap can also make it hard to fall asleep at night.

Some companies now [[reserve|L3-0724]] quiet rooms for workers who need a nap, and in some countries, [[airline|L3-0017]] [[pilots|L3-0638]] may take turns napping on long flights. Scientists still have not solved every [[mystery|L3-0562]] of sleep, but one thing is clear: when your body sends a [[signal|L3-0792]] that it is tired, a short nap may be the answer.
zh: 在台灣許多高中，學生午餐後會趴在桌上午睡。有些人認為這是浪費時間，但科學家發現，午睡能帶來實實在在的好處。
白天裡，大腦會越來越疲倦。大約二十分鐘的小睡能讓大腦有機會休息。短暫小睡後，人們往往會覺得比較清醒，記憶力和專注力等心智能力也常會提升。在需要快速反應的任務上，他們的表現也會比較好。換句話說，短暫小睡能讓大腦運作得更有效率。
不過，睡得越久不一定越好。如果小睡超過大約三十分鐘，你可能會進入深層睡眠，醒來時覺得昏沉、遲鈍。太晚睡午覺，也可能讓你晚上難以入睡。
現在有些公司會為需要小睡的員工保留安靜的房間；在某些國家，航空公司的機師在長程飛行時可以輪流小睡。科學家至今仍未解開睡眠的所有謎團，但有一件事很清楚：當身體發出疲倦的訊號時，短暫小睡或許就是解答。

questions.stem: According to the passage, how long should a good short nap be?
questions.explain: 第二段說大約二十分鐘的小睡能讓大腦休息，故選 (C)。(A) 超過一小時反而太長，第三段提醒睡超過約三十分鐘就可能醒來昏沉。
questions.evidence: A nap of roughly twenty minutes gives it a chance to rest.

questions.stem: What may happen if a nap is too long?
options: You may wake up feeling heavy and slow.
Your memory will get much better.
questions.explain: 第三段說小睡超過約三十分鐘可能進入深層睡眠，醒來感覺昏沉遲鈍，故選 (A)。(B) 記憶力提升是「短暫」小睡的好處，不是睡太久的結果。
questions.evidence: If a nap lasts longer than about thirty minutes, you may fall into deep sleep and wake up feeling heavy and slow.

questions.stem: The word "efficient" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 前文說小睡後人更清醒、反應更快，所以「讓大腦更 efficient」指大腦運作得好又不浪費時間，也就是「有效率的」，故選 (D)。(A) very tired 是小睡前大腦的狀態，意思相反。
questions.evidence: In other words, a short nap makes the brain more efficient.

questions.stem: What is the writer's main point?
options: Students should sleep in every class.
A short nap can be good for you, but a long one may not be.
Pilots should never sleep on long flights.
Scientists already know everything about sleep.
questions.explain: 全文先說短暫小睡的好處，再提醒小睡太久的壞處，重點是「短睡有益、長睡未必」，故選 (B)。(D) 與最後一段「科學家仍未解開睡眠所有謎團」矛盾。
questions.evidence: However, a longer nap is not always better.

vocab.stem: The band will ______ five songs at the school festival tonight.
vocab.explain: 樂團今晚在校慶「表演」五首歌，perform songs 是常見搭配，故選 perform。promote 是「宣傳、推廣」，可以宣傳新歌，但「在晚會上演出歌曲」要用 perform。

vocab.stem: We should ______ a table at the restaurant, because it is always crowded on weekends.
vocab.explain: 餐廳週末總是客滿，所以要先「預訂」位子，reserve a table 是訂位的固定說法，故選 reserve。signal 是「打信號」，不能表示訂位。

title: From Royal Treat to Lucky Cake
paragraphs: Today, the [[pineapple|L3-0640]] is a [[familiar|L3-0311]] fruit. You can buy it at almost any market, and its sweet and sour [[flavor|L3-0326]] is loved around the world. Yet [[roughly|L3-0745]] five hundred years ago, most people in Europe had never seen one.

The pineapple first grew in the [[tropical|L3-0932]] areas of South America. When European sailors tasted it in the late 1400s, they were [[amazed|L3-0021]] by its [[unique|L3-0946]] shape and sweet taste. They tried to bring the fruit home, but [[transporting|L3-0925]] it across the ocean was hard. The trip took weeks, and most pineapples went bad on the way. Later, rich people in Europe tried to grow them in warm glass houses, which cost a great deal of money.

Because the fruit was so rare, it came to [[represent|L3-0720]] wealth. A pineapple on the dinner table showed that the host was rich and important. Some stories even say that people who could not pay for one would rent a pineapple for a special [[occasion|L3-0579]], show it to their guests, and then return it. Part of the fruit's [[charm|L3-0135]] was its look: its top of green leaves, known as the [[crown|L3-0209]], made it look like a little king.

Today, the pineapple has become a [[global|L3-0358]] [[product|L3-0675]]. It is grown in [[various|L3-0954]] warm places, including Taiwan, where it has [[significant|L3-0793]] meaning. In Taiwanese, its name sounds like "good luck is coming," so pineapple cakes are popular gifts. From a rare treat to a lucky snack, the pineapple shows how the meaning of a food can change over time.
zh: 如今，鳳梨是一種大家很熟悉的水果。幾乎在任何市場都買得到，它酸酸甜甜的風味也受到世界各地的人喜愛。然而大約五百年前，大多數歐洲人連看都沒看過鳳梨。
鳳梨最早生長在南美洲的熱帶地區。十五世紀末，歐洲水手第一次嚐到鳳梨時，對它獨特的外形和香甜的滋味大感驚奇。他們想把這種水果帶回家鄉，但要跨越大海運送卻很困難。航程長達好幾週，大部分的鳳梨在途中就壞掉了。後來，歐洲的有錢人試著在溫暖的玻璃溫室裡種鳳梨，這得花上一大筆錢。
由於這種水果非常稀有，它逐漸成為財富的象徵。餐桌上擺著一顆鳳梨，就表示主人有錢又有地位。有些說法甚至提到，買不起鳳梨的人會在特殊場合租一顆來，展示給客人看，之後再歸還。鳳梨的魅力有一部分來自它的外觀：頂端那叢綠葉被稱為「冠芽」，讓它看起來就像一位小國王。
今天，鳳梨已成為全球性的產品，在各個溫暖的地方都有種植，包括台灣；而鳳梨在台灣還有重要的意義。鳳梨的台語念起來像「旺來」，象徵好運到來，所以鳳梨酥是很受歡迎的伴手禮。從稀有的珍品到討吉利的點心，鳳梨讓我們看到，一種食物的意義會如何隨著時間改變。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to grow pineapples in glass houses
How the pineapple changed from a rare treat into a common fruit with special meaning
Why European sailors did not like the taste of pineapples
How pineapple cakes are made in Taiwan
questions.explain: 文章依時間順序，從鳳梨在歐洲是稀有的財富象徵，寫到今日成為全球產品並在台灣有吉祥意義，最後一句點出「食物意義會隨時間改變」，故選 (B)。(A) 玻璃溫室只是第二段的一個細節，不足以涵蓋全文。
questions.evidence: From a rare treat to a lucky snack, the pineapple shows how the meaning of a food can change over time.

questions.stem: Why was it hard for people in Europe to get fresh pineapples at first?
options: Pineapples could only grow in glass houses.
The sailors did not want to bring the fruit home.
Kings did not allow common people to eat the fruit.
Most of the fruit went bad during the long trip across the ocean.
questions.explain: 第二段說航程長達數週，大部分鳳梨在途中就壞了，所以難以運回歐洲，故選 (D)。(B) 與文意相反，水手其實很想把鳳梨帶回家。
questions.evidence: The trip took weeks, and most pineapples went bad on the way.

questions.stem: Why would some people rent a pineapple for a special occasion?
options: They wanted their guests to think they were rich.
They planned to eat the fruit with their guests.
They wanted to grow their own pineapples later.
They did not like the flavor of the fruit.
questions.explain: 第三段說桌上有鳳梨代表主人有錢有地位，而租來的鳳梨只拿給客人看、之後還要歸還，可推知租鳳梨是為了讓客人覺得自己富有，故選 (A)。(B) 不對，因為鳳梨最後要歸還，不能吃掉。
questions.evidence: A pineapple on the dinner table showed that the host was rich and important.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3, what does the word "crown" refer to?
options: The green leaves on top of a pineapple
A gift for a special guest
questions.explain: 原句說鳳梨「頂端那叢綠葉被稱為 crown」，因此 crown 指鳳梨頂上的綠葉（冠芽），故選 (C)。(B) 是被 little king 誤導，crown 本身並不是指國王。
questions.evidence: Part of the fruit's charm was its look: its top of green leaves, known as the crown, made it look like a little king.

vocab.stem: Trucks are used to ______ fresh fruit from farms to markets all over the country.
vocab.explain: 用卡車把水果從農場「運送」到各地市場，transport A from B to C 是典型用法，故選 transport。reserve 是「預訂、保留」，無法表達把貨物送到某地。

vocab.stem: The ______ of the old bridge was so strong that it stood for over a hundred years.
vocab.explain: 橋能屹立百年，是因為它的「結構」很堅固，故選 structure。talent 是「天分」，指人的才能，不能用來形容橋。

title: Beads from the River
paragraphs: Lisa's [[hometown|L3-0407]] is a small town beside a river. Many years ago, several factories were built in an [[industrial|L3-0430]] area next to the water. They [[polluted|L3-0654]] the river, and people also threw [[plastic|L3-0645]] bottles into it. The dirty water [[destroyed|L3-0234]] the homes of many fish, and the birds that used to build [[nests|L3-0572]] along the river flew away.

Last summer, Lisa decided to do something. She asked her classmates to [[engage|L3-0290]] in a clean-up day, and more than forty [[citizens|L3-0150]] from the town joined them. Together, they picked up bags of trash. Then Lisa had an idea: why not turn the bottles into something beautiful? With help from her art teacher, she cut the plastic into thin [[strips|L3-0855]] and rolled them into small [[beads|L3-0070]]. The [[process|L3-0673]] was slow, but the beads came out bright and pretty.

Lisa made the beads into [[jewelry|L3-0456]] and sold it at the night market, along with [[cotton|L3-0191]] bags and [[bamboo|L3-0061]] cups. Few people could [[resist|L3-0725]] the bright colors. She set [[aside|L3-0037]] half of the money to [[hire|L3-0400]] a small boat for the next clean-up. The river is still far from [[pure|L3-0687]], but some birds have come back.
zh: 麗莎的家鄉是河邊的一個小鎮。許多年前，河岸旁的工業區蓋了好幾間工廠。工廠污染了河水，人們也把塑膠瓶丟進河裡。髒水毀了許多魚的棲身之處，以前在河邊築巢的鳥兒也都飛走了。
去年夏天，麗莎決定做點什麼。她邀同學參與一場淨河日活動，結果鎮上有四十多位居民也一起加入。大家一起撿了好幾袋垃圾。接著麗莎想到一個點子：何不把這些瓶子變成美麗的東西呢？在美術老師的幫忙下，她把塑膠剪成細長條，再捲成一顆顆小珠子。這個過程很慢，但做出來的珠子明亮又漂亮。
麗莎把珠子做成飾品，拿到夜市去賣，同時也賣棉布袋和竹杯。很少人抗拒得了那些鮮豔的顏色。她把一半的收入存起來，準備在下次淨河時租一艘小船。這條河離「純淨」還很遠，但已經有一些鳥兒回來了。

questions.stem: Why did the birds leave the river?
options: Lisa's town built a new night market there.
Too many people came to watch them.
The river became dirty, and their homes were damaged.
The weather near the river became too cold.
questions.explain: 第一段說工廠污染河水、人們亂丟塑膠瓶，髒水毀了魚的棲地，原本在河邊築巢的鳥就飛走了，故選 (C)。文中沒有提到天氣變冷，(D) 是無中生有。
questions.evidence: The dirty water destroyed the homes of many fish, and the birds that used to build nests along the river flew away.

questions.stem: What did Lisa do with half of the money she made?
options: She kept it to rent a boat for the next clean-up.
She gave it to her art teacher.
She used it to open a jewelry shop.
questions.explain: 第三段說她把一半的錢存起來，用來在下次淨河時租一艘小船，hire a boat 就是 rent a boat，故選 (A)。(D) 只抓到 jewelry 這個字，文中她是在夜市擺攤，並沒有開店。
questions.evidence: She set aside half of the money to hire a small boat for the next clean-up.

questions.stem: The word "resist" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: Few people could resist the bright colors 意思是「很少人能抗拒鮮豔的顏色」，也就是大家都忍不住想買；resist 在這裡是「抗拒、忍住不要」，最接近 say no to，故選 (B)。(C) pay for 是買下來，剛好是「抗拒不了」之後的結果，意思不同。
questions.evidence: Few people could resist the bright colors.

questions.stem: What can we infer about Lisa?
options: She wants to work in a factory in the future.
She only cares about making money.
She thinks the river is already clean enough.
She hopes to keep working to make the river clean again.
questions.explain: 她把賣飾品的一半收入留下來，準備租船繼續淨河，可推知她打算持續為河川努力，故選 (D)。最後一句說河水離純淨還很遠，所以 (C) 與文意相反。
questions.evidence: She set aside half of the money to hire a small boat for the next clean-up.

vocab.stem: The strong storm ______ most of the fruit trees on the farm, so the farmer had to plant new ones.
vocab.explain: 強烈暴風雨「摧毀」了農場上大部分的果樹，所以農夫只好重種，故選 destroyed。polluted（污染）通常用在水、空氣，不會說暴風雨污染了果樹；hired（雇用）、resisted（抵抗）也都不合語意。

vocab.stem: The restaurant is getting busier, so the owner plans to ______ two more cooks.
vocab.explain: 餐廳越來越忙，老闆打算再「雇用」兩位廚師，hire cooks 是常見搭配，故選 hire。melt（融化）、resist（抵抗）、destroy（摧毀）都不合語意。

title: Hidden Corners Photo Contest
paragraphs: To all students: The Photo Club is happy to [[announce|L3-0026]] our first [[monthly|L3-0551]] photo contest! This month's topic is "Hidden Corners." We want you to [[capture|L3-0124]] places that most people walk past without looking, such as a quiet [[alley|L3-0018]] near school or a forgotten corner of our [[campus|L3-0120]].

Rules: Each student may send in up to three photos. You may use a phone or a camera, but please do not climb walls or enter places where you are not [[permitted|L3-0632]] to go. Safety comes first! Also, do not [[assume|L3-0040]] that you need an expensive camera. A [[creative|L3-0200]] idea matters more.

[[Awards|L3-0051]]: Three winners will be chosen by our teachers. Their photos will be shown in a [[temporary|L3-0897]] show in the library for two weeks, and they may also appear on the town's travel page to [[attract|L3-0043]] [[tourists|L3-0919]]. After the contest, a short [[survey|L3-0872]] will ask what you think of it.

How to join: Email your photos to the club by May 31. Under each photo, please write its [[location|L3-0501]] and a few words about why you chose it. For more [[information|L3-0433]], visit the club room. Missed this month? Don't [[panic|L3-0609]]. A new contest comes every month!
zh: 全體同學請注意：攝影社很高興宣布，我們第一次的每月攝影比賽開始了！本月主題是「隱藏的角落」。我們希望你捕捉那些大多數人走過卻不會多看一眼的地方，例如學校附近一條安靜的小巷，或是校園裡一個被遺忘的角落。
比賽規則：每位同學最多可以投稿三張照片。可以用手機或相機拍攝，但請不要爬牆，也不要進入不被允許進入的地方。安全第一！另外，別以為一定要有昂貴的相機才行。有創意的點子更重要。
獎項：由老師選出三位得獎者。得獎作品將在圖書館為期兩週的臨時展覽中展出，也可能刊登在本鎮的旅遊頁面上，用來吸引觀光客。比賽結束後，會有一份簡短的問卷調查，詢問大家對這次比賽的想法。
參加方式：請在 5 月 31 日前把照片用電子郵件寄給社團。請在每張照片下方寫上拍攝地點，並用幾句話說明你為什麼選這個地方。想知道更多資訊，請到社團教室詢問。錯過了這個月嗎？別慌張，每個月都會有新的比賽！

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of this notice?
options: To ask students to clean up the corners of the campus
To invite students to take part in a photo contest
To teach students how to use an expensive camera
To tell tourists about a new show in the library
questions.explain: 公告一開頭就宣布攝影社舉辦每月攝影比賽，接著說明規則、獎項和參加方式，目的是邀請同學參賽，故選 (B)。(D) 圖書館展覽只是給得獎者的獎勵之一，而且公告的對象是學生，不是觀光客。
questions.evidence: The Photo Club is happy to announce our first monthly photo contest!

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT allowed in the contest?
options: Climbing a wall to get a better photo
Taking a photo of an alley near school
questions.explain: 規則中明確寫著請不要爬牆、不要進入不被允許的地方，故選 (C)。用手機拍攝、投稿兩張（上限三張）、拍學校附近的小巷都是公告允許或舉例的內容。
questions.evidence: You may use a phone or a camera, but please do not climb walls or enter places where you are not permitted to go.

questions.stem: The word "capture" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 在攝影比賽的情境中，capture places 指「把地方拍下來」，也就是 take a picture of，故選 (A)。(D) walk past 是原句中「一般人只是走過」的動作，並不是 capture 的意思。
questions.evidence: We want you to capture places that most people walk past without looking, such as a quiet alley near school or a forgotten corner of our campus.

questions.stem: What should students write under each photo?
options: The kind of camera they used
Where the photo was taken and why they chose the place
questions.explain: 參加方式提到每張照片下要寫上拍攝地點（location），並用幾句話說明為什麼選這個地方，故選 (D)。公告特別說不需要昂貴相機，並沒有要求寫出相機種類，(B) 不對。
questions.evidence: Under each photo, please write its location and a few words about why you chose it.

vocab.stem: My father had an ______ on his knee last month, and the doctor told him to rest for six weeks.
vocab.explain: 父親的膝蓋動了「手術」，醫生要他休息六週，have an operation 是「動手術」的固定說法，故選 operation。survey（調查）、tribe（部落）、substance（物質）都無法用在膝蓋上表示醫療行為。

vocab.stem: After carrying the heavy boxes all morning, my arms began to ______.
vocab.explain: 搬了一早上的重箱子，手臂開始「痠痛」，ache 是不及物動詞，可以直接放在 began to 後面，故選 ache。bury（埋）、spray（噴灑）、permit（允許）後面通常要接受詞，而且語意也不合。

title: Playing On in the Rain
paragraphs: Every year, Sunny Hill High School's sports day begins with the school band [[marching|L3-0519]] around the field. This year, Ben, a first-year student, was chosen to play the [[horn|L3-0411]]. He was [[eager|L3-0270]] to do well, but he could also feel the weight of everyone's [[expectations|L3-0298]]. The band had won a gold [[medal|L3-0527]] in a city contest the year before, and it was a great [[honor|L3-0409]] to [[perform|L3-0629]] with them.

On the morning of the event, the weather turned [[extreme|L3-0304]]. First it was very hot, and then a heavy rain suddenly fell. Some teachers were [[doubtful|L3-0255]] about letting the band go on. [[Meanwhile|L3-0526]], the [[audience|L3-0045]] waited under the roof, and some [[elderly|L3-0278]] grandparents who had come to watch put on raincoats.

In this [[situation|L3-0800]], the band leader made an [[immediate|L3-0425]] decision: they would play. As the water slowly [[drained|L3-0260]] off the field, Ben lifted his horn and played as loudly as he could. The crowd stood up and cheered, and the [[joyful|L3-0458]] music [[impressed|L3-0427]] everyone. "I'll remember this day for [[decades|L3-0220]]," Ben said later with a big smile.
zh: 每年，陽光丘高中的運動會都由學校樂隊繞著操場行進揭開序幕。今年，一年級的班（Ben）被選上吹奏號角。他很渴望表現好，但也感受到大家期望所帶來的壓力。樂隊前一年才在市級比賽中拿下金牌，能和他們一起演出是莫大的榮譽。
活動當天早上，天氣變得很極端。一開始非常炎熱，接著突然下起大雨。有些老師對於是否讓樂隊照常演出感到懷疑。與此同時，觀眾在屋簷下等待，一些前來觀看的年長爺爺奶奶穿上了雨衣。
在這種情況下，樂隊隊長當機立斷：他們要照常演奏。隨著雨水慢慢從操場排掉，班舉起號角，用盡全力大聲吹奏。群眾站起來歡呼，歡樂的音樂讓每個人都印象深刻。班後來滿臉笑容地說：「這一天我會記上好幾十年。」

questions.stem: Why did Ben feel the weight of everyone's expectations?
options: He had never played the horn before.
The band had done very well in a contest the year before.
His grandparents asked him to win a medal.
The teachers told him he was the band leader.
questions.explain: 第一段說樂隊前一年在市級比賽拿下金牌，能和他們一起演出是莫大的榮譽，所以班感受到大家期待的壓力，故選 (B)。文中的隊長是 band leader，不是班，(D) 錯誤。
questions.evidence: The band had won a gold medal in a city contest the year before, and it was a great honor to perform with them.

questions.stem: What happened on the morning of sports day?
options: It was hot at first, and then it rained heavily.
The band leader got sick and went home.
The sports day was moved to another day.
Ben forgot to bring his horn.
questions.explain: 第二段說天氣一開始很熱，接著突然下起大雨，故選 (A)。文中有老師懷疑是否該照常演出，但隊長最後決定演奏，並沒有改期，(C) 不對。
questions.evidence: First it was very hot, and then a heavy rain suddenly fell.

questions.stem: The word "doubtful" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 下大雨時，有些老師對樂隊是否應繼續演出感到 doubtful，也就是「懷疑、不確定」，最接近 not sure，故選 (D)。(B) sure 是「確定的」，意思正好相反。
questions.evidence: Some teachers were doubtful about letting the band go on.

questions.stem: What can we infer from the last paragraph?
options: Ben was sorry that he had joined the band.
The audience left because of the rain.
The band's decision to play turned out to be a good one.
The teachers stopped the show after a few minutes.
questions.explain: 最後一段說群眾站起來歡呼、音樂讓每個人印象深刻，班還說會記住這天好幾十年，可推知在雨中照常演奏是個好決定，故選 (C)。(B) 與「群眾站起來歡呼」不符。
questions.evidence: The crowd stood up and cheered, and the joyful music impressed everyone.

vocab.stem: The number of students who walk to school has ______ because more parents now drive their children.
vocab.explain: 越來越多家長開車接送，所以走路上學的人數「減少」了，decrease 可以當不及物動詞，主詞是 the number，故選 decreased。impressed、detected、honored 通常需要受詞，語意也不通。

vocab.stem: This small machine can ______ smoke in the kitchen and will make a loud sound to warn you.
vocab.explain: 這台小機器能「偵測」到廚房裡的煙，並發出響聲警告你，也就是煙霧偵測器，故選 detect。desire（渴望）、impress（使印象深刻）不能用在機器和煙之間；decrease smoke（減少煙）也和「發出響聲警告」的功能不符。

title: The Story Behind a Cup of Tea
paragraphs: In Taiwan, tea is part of daily life. For many families, making a pot of tea after dinner is a [[routine|L3-0746]] that helps them [[relax|L3-0710]]. But few people think about the work that goes into the leaves before they reach the cup.

Many of Taiwan's best teas come from farms in [[remote|L3-0718]] mountain areas. Small farms are [[scattered|L3-0763]] across the hills, where cool air and [[plenty|L3-0647]] of rain help the tea plants grow slowly. Most tea [[producers|L3-0674]] there are family businesses. They [[rely|L3-0715]] more on skill and hard work than on big machines, and the leaves are often picked by hand.

After picking, the leaves are dried, rolled, and sometimes [[roasted|L3-0736]]. Roasting changes the [[original|L3-0592]] taste of the leaves and gives oolong tea a deeper [[flavor|L3-0326]]. Each family has its own methods, and many are not written down. Instead, they are passed on through [[oral|L3-0589]] teaching from parents to children.

Growing tea does not always bring a big [[profit|L3-0677]]. A single typhoon can [[destroy|L3-0234]] a whole season's [[crop|L3-0208]]. Still, many farmers love what they do. So the next time you [[pour|L3-0662]] a cup of tea, enjoy it slowly. Its taste may [[reveal|L3-0730]] the many hours of work behind it.
zh: 在台灣，茶是日常生活的一部分。對許多家庭來說，晚餐後泡一壺茶是幫助大家放鬆的例行公事。但很少人會想到，茶葉在進到杯子之前，背後花了多少功夫。
台灣許多最好的茶來自偏遠山區的茶園。小小的茶園散布在山坡上，涼爽的空氣和充足的雨水讓茶樹慢慢生長。那裡大多數的製茶業者都是家族經營，他們靠的是技術和辛勤工作，而不是大型機器，茶葉也常常是用手採的。
採收後，茶葉要經過乾燥、揉捻，有時還要烘焙。烘焙會改變茶葉原本的味道，讓烏龍茶的風味更加濃厚。每個家族都有自己的方法，而且很多並沒有寫下來，而是由父母口頭傳授給孩子。
種茶不一定能帶來豐厚的利潤。一個颱風就可能毀掉整季的收成。儘管如此，許多茶農仍然熱愛自己的工作。所以下次你倒一杯茶時，慢慢品嚐吧。它的滋味也許正透露出背後許多小時的辛勞。

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, why do tea plants in the mountains grow slowly?
options: Farmers do not give them enough water.
The farms are too small for big machines.
The air there is cool, and there is a lot of rain.
questions.explain: 第二段說山坡上涼爽的空氣和充足的雨水讓茶樹慢慢生長，故選 (D)。(B) 雖然文中提到茶農不靠大型機器，但那不是茶樹生長慢的原因。
questions.evidence: Small farms are scattered across the hills, where cool air and plenty of rain help the tea plants grow slowly.

questions.stem: What does roasting do to the tea leaves?
options: It gives the tea a deeper flavor.
It makes the leaves grow faster.
It keeps the leaves green and fresh.
It helps farmers pick the leaves by hand.
questions.explain: 第三段說烘焙會改變茶葉原本的味道，讓烏龍茶的風味更濃厚，故選 (A)。烘焙是採收之後的步驟，和茶葉生長或採摘都無關，(B)、(D) 不對。
questions.evidence: Roasting changes the original taste of the leaves and gives oolong tea a deeper flavor.

questions.stem: The word "oral" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 原句先說這些方法「沒有寫下來」，接著用 Instead 轉折，說是靠 oral teaching 從父母傳給孩子，可知 oral 是「口頭的、用說的」，最接近 spoken，故選 (B)。(A) written in books 正好是前一句否定的方式。
questions.evidence: Instead, they are passed on through oral teaching from parents to children.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to make tea at home after dinner
Why typhoons are dangerous for farmers
The hard work and care behind Taiwan's tea
Why oolong tea is better than other teas
questions.explain: 文章從喝茶的日常習慣談起，接著介紹山區茶園、手工採茶、烘焙技術與種茶的風險，最後請讀者體會茶背後的辛勞，主旨是台灣茶背後的心血，故選 (C)。(B) 颱風只是第四段的一個細節。
questions.evidence: Its taste may reveal the many hours of work behind it.

vocab.stem: Students must ask for ______ before they use the computer room after school.
vocab.explain: 放學後要使用電腦教室，必須先取得「許可」，ask for permission 是固定搭配，故選 permission。pollution（污染）、semesters（學期）、passengers（乘客）都無法放在 ask for 後面表達合理的意思。

vocab.stem: Before the plane took off, all the ______ were asked to turn off their phones.
vocab.explain: 飛機起飛前，所有「乘客」都被要求關掉手機，只有人才會被要求關手機，故選 passengers。profits（利潤）、semesters（學期）、routines（例行公事）都不是人，不能當這個動作的對象。

title: Turn Down the Lights
paragraphs: Do you often lie [[awake|L3-0049]] in bed at night? You are not alone. One [[trend|L3-0928]] among teenagers today is using phones late into the night, and many of them do not get [[sufficient|L3-0865]] sleep.

The [[underlying|L3-0943]] problem is light. When it gets dark, the body makes a [[substance|L3-0860]] that tells us it is time to rest. Bright screens can slow this down. That is why doctors [[advise|L3-0012]] us to [[dim|L3-0238]] the lights and put our phones away an hour before bed.

Too little sleep can hurt both our body and our [[mental|L3-0532]] health. Tired students may find it hard to focus in class, and they may [[snap|L3-0812]] at their friends over small things. Their faces may look pale, without the healthy pink in their [[cheeks|L3-0137]].

Luckily, a few simple [[techniques|L3-0894]] can help. First, exercise during the day. A good [[sweat|L3-0878]] in the afternoon can help you sleep better, but avoid hard exercise just before bed. Second, try counting slowly in the dark. As your mind calms down, your worries may [[vanish|L3-0952]], and you may soon [[sink|L3-0798]] into a deep sleep. To [[sum|L3-0867]] up, if you want a [[solid|L3-0813]] night's sleep, less light and more exercise are the keys.
zh: 你晚上常常躺在床上睡不著嗎？你不是唯一一個。現在青少年之間有個趨勢，就是滑手機滑到深夜，而他們當中很多人睡眠不足。
根本的問題在於光線。天色變暗時，身體會製造一種物質，告訴我們該休息了。明亮的螢幕會讓這個過程變慢。這就是為什麼醫生建議我們在睡前一小時把燈光調暗、把手機收起來。
睡太少會傷害我們的身體和心理健康。疲倦的學生上課可能很難專心，也可能為了小事就對朋友發脾氣。他們的臉色可能看起來蒼白，臉頰少了健康的紅潤。
幸好，有幾個簡單的技巧可以幫忙。第一，白天要運動。下午好好流一身汗，可以幫助你睡得更好，但睡前要避免激烈運動。第二，試著在黑暗中慢慢數數。當你的心靜下來，煩惱可能就會消失，你也許很快就能沉沉入睡。總而言之，想要一夜好眠，少一點光、多一點運動就是關鍵。

questions.stem: Why do bright screens make it harder to fall asleep?
options: They slow down the making of a substance that tells the body to rest.
They make the room too hot.
They make our cheeks turn pink.
questions.explain: 第二段說天黑時身體會製造一種告訴我們該休息的物質，而明亮的螢幕會讓這個過程變慢，故選 (B)。文中沒有提到眼睛痛或房間變熱，(A)、(C) 是無中生有。
questions.evidence: When it gets dark, the body makes a substance that tells us it is time to rest. Bright screens can slow this down.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT given as a sign of too little sleep?
options: Getting angry at friends over small things
questions.explain: 第三段列出睡眠不足的表現：上課難專心、為小事對朋友發脾氣、臉色蒼白；文中沒有提到「一直覺得餓」，故選 (C)。
questions.evidence: Tired students may find it hard to focus in class, and they may snap at their friends over small things.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3, the phrase "snap at" is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 疲倦的學生可能為了小事就 snap at 朋友，這裡的 snap at 是「對……厲聲說話、發脾氣」，最接近 speak angrily to，故選 (B)。snap 也有「拍照」的口語用法，但和 at friends over small things 的語境不合，(A) 是陷阱。
questions.evidence: Tired students may find it hard to focus in class, and they may snap at their friends over small things.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Teenagers should stop using phones forever.
Exercise is the only way to fall asleep.
Doctors do not understand why people cannot sleep.
Light, exercise, and a calm mind all affect how well we sleep.
questions.explain: 文章先說明光線是失眠的根本原因，再談睡眠不足的影響，最後提供運動與放鬆的技巧，結論是少一點光、多一點運動就能睡得好，故選 (D)。(B) only 太絕對，文中也提到數數等其他方法。
questions.evidence: To sum up, if you want a solid night's sleep, less light and more exercise are the keys.

vocab.stem: The little boy covered his eyes during the ______ movie because it was too scary for him.
vocab.explain: 小男孩看電影時遮住眼睛，因為太可怕了，可知是「恐怖」片，horror movie 是固定說法，故選 horror。fortune（財富）、lightning（閃電）、technique（技巧）放在 movie 前都不合語意。

vocab.stem: At the airport, you need to show your ______ before you can get on a plane to another country.
vocab.explain: 搭飛機出國前，在機場要出示「護照」，故選 passport。pigeon（鴿子）、lightning（閃電）、horror（恐懼）都不是登機時需要出示的東西。

title: The Bird That Always Finds Its Way
paragraphs: In many city parks, [[pigeons|L3-0635]] are so [[familiar|L3-0311]] that most people hardly notice them. Yet these common birds have a special skill: many of them can find their way home from hundreds of miles away. Some have even flown home after being taken to places they had never seen before. For thousands of years, people have [[relied|L3-0715]] on this skill.

Long before phones and the Internet, pigeons were used to carry messages. A small piece of paper was tied to a bird's leg, and the bird was [[released|L3-0711]] far from home. It would then fly straight back, often faster than a horse could run. In the 1800s, some [[traders|L3-0923]] used pigeons to get news about prices before others did. Getting such news even a few hours early could be worth a [[fortune|L3-0338]]. Because the birds were cheap, fast, and [[reliable|L3-0712]], this [[technique|L3-0894]] was used for a long time.

How do pigeons do it? For many years, this was a complete [[mystery|L3-0562]]. [[Scientists|L3-0767]] have now [[observed|L3-0578]] that the birds seem to use [[various|L3-0954]] clues. They may follow the sun, and they may [[recognize|L3-0704]] roads, rivers, and other things they see from the sky. Some scientists believe pigeons can also [[detect|L3-0235]] the earth's magnetic field, which may work like a map inside their heads. However, there is not yet [[sufficient|L3-0865]] [[proof|L3-0680]] to explain everything, and the question is still being studied.

Today, few people send messages by pigeon, and some people even think of them as dirty city birds. Still, these birds show us that even the most ordinary [[creatures|L3-0202]] may hide [[amazing|L3-0021]] abilities.
zh: 在許多城市公園裡，鴿子太常見了，大多數人幾乎不會注意到牠們。然而，這些普通的鳥兒有一項特殊的本領：牠們當中有許多能從數百英里外找到回家的路。有些鴿子甚至被帶到從未去過的地方後，仍能飛回家。數千年來，人類一直仰賴這項本領。
早在有電話和網路之前，人們就用鴿子來傳遞訊息。把一小張紙綁在鳥的腳上，然後在離家很遠的地方把牠放飛。牠就會直接飛回家，速度常常比馬跑得還快。十九世紀時，有些商人利用鴿子比別人更早得知價格消息。就算只早幾個小時得到這類消息，也可能價值一大筆財富。由於鴿子便宜、快速又可靠，這種方法沿用了很長一段時間。
鴿子是怎麼辦到的？多年來，這一直是個徹底的謎。現在，科學家已觀察到這些鳥似乎會運用各種線索。牠們可能會跟著太陽走，也可能認得從空中看到的道路、河流和其他東西。有些科學家認為鴿子還能偵測到地球的磁場，而磁場可能就像牠們腦中的一張地圖。不過，目前還沒有足夠的證據能解釋一切，這個問題仍在研究中。
如今已經很少人用鴿子傳遞訊息了，有些人甚至把牠們看成骯髒的城市鳥類。儘管如此，這些鳥讓我們看到，即使是最平凡的生物，也可能藏著驚人的能力。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why pigeons are no longer seen in city parks
How traders became rich in the 1800s
How pigeons find their way home and how people have used this skill
Why scientists think pigeons are smarter than horses
questions.explain: 文章先介紹鴿子能從遠方找到回家的路，第二段談人類如何利用鴿子傳遞訊息，第三段談科學家對鴿子認路方式的研究，主旨是鴿子的歸巢能力及人類的運用，故選 (C)。(B) 商人只是第二段的一個例子。
questions.evidence: Yet these common birds have a special skill: many of them can find their way home from hundreds of miles away.

questions.stem: Why did some traders in the 1800s use pigeons?
options: To send gifts to their families
To get news about prices earlier than others
To find out about the weather
To sell the birds at a high price
questions.explain: 第二段說十九世紀有些商人用鴿子比別人更早得到價格消息，故選 (B)。文中說鴿子便宜，並沒有說商人拿鴿子高價出售，(D) 不對。
questions.evidence: In the 1800s, some traders used pigeons to get news about prices before others did.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from paragraph 3?
options: Scientists do not yet fully understand how pigeons find their way.
Pigeons can only fly when the sun is out.
Scientists have proved that pigeons use a map inside their heads.
Pigeons get lost when they fly over rivers.
questions.explain: 第三段最後說目前還沒有足夠證據解釋一切，問題仍在研究中，可推知科學家尚未完全了解鴿子認路的方式，故選 (A)。(C) 錯在 proved：磁場像腦中地圖只是部分科學家的看法，並未被證實。
questions.evidence: However, there is not yet sufficient proof to explain everything, and the question is still being studied.

questions.stem: The word "reliable" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 原句說鴿子便宜、快速又 reliable，所以被使用很久；能被長期用來送重要消息，表示鴿子「可靠的、值得信賴的」，最接近 able to be trusted，故選 (D)。(A) expensive 與同一句的 cheap 互相矛盾。
questions.evidence: Because the birds were cheap, fast, and reliable, this technique was used for a long time.

vocab.stem: When the man waved his hand over the coin, it seemed to ______ into thin air.
vocab.explain: 男子在硬幣上方揮手，硬幣好像憑空「消失」了，vanish into thin air 是常見說法，故選 vanish。twist（扭轉）、sweat（流汗）、snap（啪地折斷）都不能和 into thin air 搭配表示不見。

vocab.stem: The soup tastes too plain. Let's add a little ______ to give it more flavor.
vocab.explain: 湯太淡了，加一點「香料」讓它更有味道，故選 spice。sweat（汗水）、cheek（臉頰）、mosquito（蚊子）都不是能加進湯裡調味的東西。

title: The Quiet Girl Who Rode Around Taiwan
paragraphs: Mia grew up in a quiet [[neighborhood|L3-0571]] near a small fishing [[harbor|L3-0382]]. As a child, she was not an [[athlete|L3-0041]] at all. She was shy, and loud ball games often [[frightened|L3-0345]] her. What she loved most was sitting by the sea and watching the [[tide|L3-0910]] come in.

Things changed when she was fifteen. Her high school started a cycling club, and Mr. Wu, the [[coach|L3-0161]], asked her to join. At first, Mia could [[barely|L3-0065]] keep up. On her first ride up a mountain [[trail|L3-0924]], the [[gap|L3-0352]] between her and the others grew bigger and bigger. "I'm not [[capable|L3-0122]] of this," she thought. But Mr. Wu told her that the most important thing was the [[inner|L3-0436]] voice that says, "Don't stop."

Slowly, her [[attitude|L3-0042]] changed. [[Besides|L3-0077]] riding after school, she ran every morning. Two years later, she became the club's [[captain|L3-0123]]. That summer, she led ten members on a ten-day [[adventure|L3-0010]] around Taiwan. Wearing [[helmets|L3-0397]], they rode past rice fields and along the east coast, stopping to drink fresh [[coconut|L3-0164]] water under the hot [[tropical|L3-0932]] sun.
Now Mia often tells younger students, "Being shy is fine. Even a quiet person can [[achieve|L3-0005]] big goals."
zh: 米亞在小漁港附近一個安靜的社區長大。小時候，她完全不是運動型的人。她很害羞，吵鬧的球類比賽常常讓她害怕。她最喜歡的是坐在海邊，看著潮水湧上來。
十五歲那年，事情有了改變。她的高中成立了自行車社，吳教練邀她加入。一開始，米亞幾乎跟不上。第一次騎上山路時，她和其他人的差距越拉越大。她心想：「我沒有能力做到。」但吳教練告訴她，最重要的是內心那個說著「別停下來」的聲音。
慢慢地，她的態度改變了。除了放學後騎車，她每天早上還去跑步。兩年後，她成了社團的隊長。那年夏天，她帶著十名社員展開為期十天的環島冒險。他們戴著安全帽，騎過稻田、沿著東海岸前進，途中停下來在炎熱的熱帶陽光下喝新鮮的椰子水。
現在，米亞常對學弟妹說：「害羞沒有關係。即使是安靜的人，也能達成遠大的目標。」

questions.stem: What did Mia like to do as a child?
options: Watch the sea and the tide
Play ball games with her friends
Ride her bike in the mountains
questions.explain: 第一段說她小時候最喜歡坐在海邊看潮水湧上來，故選 (A)。(B) 正好相反，吵鬧的球類比賽會讓她害怕；(D) 每天早上跑步是她加入自行車社之後才養成的習慣。
questions.evidence: What she loved most was sitting by the sea and watching the tide come in.

questions.stem: What happened on Mia's first ride up a mountain trail?
options: She rode faster than everyone else.
She fell and hurt her leg.
She fell further and further behind the others.
She decided to leave the club.
questions.explain: 第二段說第一次騎上山路時，她和其他人之間的差距越來越大，也就是越落越後面，故選 (C)。文中沒有提到她跌倒受傷或退社，(B)、(D) 都是無中生有。
questions.evidence: On her first ride up a mountain trail, the gap between her and the others grew bigger and bigger.

questions.stem: The word "capable" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 「I'm not capable of this」是她跟不上別人時心裡的想法，意思是「我沒有能力做到」，capable of 等於 able to do，故選 (D)。(A) afraid 雖然符合她的心情，但不是 capable 的字義。
questions.evidence: "I'm not capable of this," she thought.

questions.stem: What can we learn from Mia's story?
options: Shy people should not join sports clubs.
With hard work, a person can change and grow.
Only strong athletes can ride around Taiwan.
A good coach always does the work for students.
questions.explain: 米亞原本害羞、不擅運動，靠著每天練習和內心的堅持，最後當上隊長並帶隊環島，最後一句也說安靜的人也能達成遠大目標，可知努力能讓人改變成長，故選 (B)。(A) 與她的經歷相反。
questions.evidence: Even a quiet person can achieve big goals.

vocab.stem: The students helped ______ the classroom with paper flowers and bright lights for the party.
vocab.explain: 學生用紙花和燈光「布置、裝飾」教室來辦派對，decorate A with B 是常見用法，故選 decorate。frighten（使害怕）、coach（指導）、tune（調音）都不能和「用紙花布置教室」搭配。

vocab.stem: The old coin turned out to be ______. It was made only last year, not two hundred years ago.
vocab.explain: 那枚「古」錢幣其實去年才做的，不是兩百年前的，可知是「假的」，故選 fake。bitter（苦的）、inner（內部的）、capable（有能力的）都不能用來形容一枚被揭穿的仿造錢幣。

title: A Receipt in Your Pocket
paragraphs: In Taiwan, a shopping [[receipt|L3-0702]] is more than a piece of paper. Every two months, the government draws winning numbers, and a receipt with the right number can win money. Because of this, many people keep their receipts.

In [[theory|L3-0904]], keeping paper receipts is easy, but in real life it is not. They are easy to lose, and if you [[spill|L3-0821]] a drink on one or leave it in a hot car, the numbers may [[fade|L3-0305]]. Printing them also uses [[plenty|L3-0647]] of paper.

So more and more people now choose [[electronic|L3-0282]] receipts. Instead of taking a paper copy, people show a barcode on their phone for the store to scan. The receipt is then saved, and with a few [[taps|L3-0890]], they can check the winning numbers. This [[enables|L3-0288]] people to keep every receipt without any paper.

Ms. Lin, a teacher, turned this into an [[educational|L3-0275]] [[experiment|L3-0299]]. For one [[semester|L3-0775]], half of her class kept paper receipts, and the other half used their phones. In the end, the paper group lost many receipts, but the phone group lost none. "It was a [[tough|L3-0917]] lesson," she laughed, "but it showed the [[strength|L3-0854]] of technology: it can [[reduce|L3-0707]] waste and make life easier."
zh: 在台灣，購物發票不只是一張紙。政府每兩個月會開出中獎號碼，號碼對中的發票就能贏得獎金。因此，許多人會把發票保存起來。
理論上，保存紙本發票很簡單，但實際上卻不然。發票很容易弄丟，如果把飲料灑在上面，或把它留在很熱的車裡，上面的號碼可能會褪色。印發票也要用掉大量的紙。
所以越來越多人改用電子發票。購物時不拿紙本，而是出示手機上的條碼讓店家掃描。發票就這樣存好了，只要在手機上點幾下，就能對中獎號碼。這讓人們不需要任何紙張，就能保存每一張發票。
有位林老師把這件事變成一場有教育意義的實驗。在一個學期裡，班上一半的學生保存紙本發票，另一半用手機。到了學期末，紙本組弄丟了許多發票，手機組卻一張也沒丟。她笑著說：「這是很難熬的一課，但它展現了科技的力量：科技可以減少浪費，讓生活更輕鬆。」

questions.stem: Why do many people in Taiwan keep their receipts?
options: They need them to return things to stores.
A receipt with the right number can win money.
Their teachers ask them to collect receipts.
They use the paper to make art.
questions.explain: 第一段說政府每兩個月開出中獎號碼，號碼對中的發票能贏得獎金，所以很多人會保存發票，故選 (B)。(C) 林老師的實驗只是第四段的一個班級活動，並不是大家保存發票的原因。
questions.evidence: Every two months, the government draws winning numbers, and a receipt with the right number can win money.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, which is a problem with paper receipts?
options: They cannot be printed in color.
They are too heavy to carry.
The numbers on them may fade.
They cost a lot of money to buy.
questions.explain: 第二段說紙本發票容易遺失，如果灑到飲料或放在很熱的車裡，上面的號碼可能會褪色，故選 (C)。文中沒有提到重量或價格，(B)、(D) 是無中生有。
questions.evidence: They are easy to lose, and if you spill a drink on one or leave it in a hot car, the numbers may fade.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3, what does the word "This" in "This enables people to keep every receipt" refer to?
questions.explain: This 指的是前一句所說的事：發票存進手機，點幾下就能對獎。正因為發票存在手機裡，人們才能不帶紙就保存每一張發票，故選 (A)。(C) 印更多紙本發票正好和電子發票的做法相反。
questions.evidence: The receipt is then saved, and with a few taps, they can check the winning numbers.

questions.stem: What can we infer about Ms. Lin's experiment?
options: The paper group did better than the phone group.
Ms. Lin thinks students should stop shopping.
The students did not learn anything from it.
It showed that electronic receipts are easier to keep.
questions.explain: 實驗結果是紙本組弄丟許多發票，手機組一張也沒丟，林老師也說科技能減少浪費、讓生活更輕鬆，可推知實驗顯示電子發票比較好保存，故選 (D)。(A) 與實驗結果相反。
questions.evidence: In the end, the paper group lost many receipts, but the phone group lost none.

vocab.stem: In very cold winters, the lake ______, and people can even walk on it.
vocab.explain: 嚴冬時湖面「結冰」，人甚至可以在上面走，故選 freezes。spills（溢出）、taps（輕敲）、rusts（生鏽）都不會讓人能在湖面上行走。

vocab.stem: The river is so ______ here that you can see the stones at the bottom.
vocab.explain: 河水「淺」到可以看見河底的石頭，故選 shallow。tight（緊的）、native（本土的）、tough（堅韌的、困難的）都不是用來形容河水深淺的字。

title: The Hidden Life in the Soil
paragraphs: When Mia joined the gardening club, her teacher, Mr. Chen, handed her a cup of soil. "Tell me what you [[observe|L3-0578]]," he said. "It's just soil," Mia answered. "Look again," Mr. Chen said. "[[Beneath|L3-0074]] your feet, there is a whole world."

Healthy soil, he explained, is full of tiny living things, including millions of [[bacteria|L3-0057]]. Many of them turn dead leaves into food for plants. Roots also need air to [[breathe|L3-0096]], so plants grow [[badly|L3-0058]] in hard soil. Once Mia became [[aware|L3-0052]] of this, she stopped pressing the soil down.

The club had a small [[budget|L3-0105]], so the students made their own plant food. They mixed old leaves and fruit skins with soil in a box. At first, it gave off an [[awful|L3-0053]] smell, but they kept the [[moisture|L3-0548]] right and turned it every week. The [[process|L3-0673]] took two months, and the mix became dark, rich soil. Soon they started an [[additional|L3-0006]] box.

Mia became Mr. Chen's [[assistant|L3-0039]]. She kept [[accurate|L3-0003]] notes on the plants and used soft string to [[bind|L3-0079]] the tall tomato plants to sticks. Their [[experiment|L3-0299]] worked: plants in the new soil looked bigger and more [[attractive|L3-0044]]. "Good [[agriculture|L3-0016]] starts with the tiny life in the soil," Mr. Chen said.
zh: 米亞加入園藝社時，指導老師陳老師遞給她一杯泥土。「說說看你觀察到什麼。」他說。「這就只是土啊。」米亞回答。「再看一次，」陳老師說，「在你的腳底下，有一整個世界。」
他解釋說，健康的土壤裡充滿了微小的生物，其中包括數以百萬計的細菌。許多細菌會把枯葉變成植物的養分。植物的根也需要空氣才能呼吸，所以在硬邦邦的土裡，植物會長得很差。米亞知道這件事以後，就不再把土壓緊了。
社團的預算不多，所以學生們自己做肥料。他們把落葉和果皮跟泥土一起混在箱子裡。一開始，箱子散發出可怕的臭味，但他們把濕度控制得剛剛好，而且每週翻攪一次。整個過程花了兩個月，混合物變成了黑色、肥沃的土壤。不久，他們又多做了一箱。
米亞當上了陳老師的助手。她準確地記錄植物的生長情形，並用軟繩把長高的番茄綁在支架上。他們的實驗成功了：用新土種的植物長得比較大，看起來也更漂亮。「好的農業，是從土壤裡的微小生命開始的。」陳老師說。

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, why do plants grow badly in hard soil?
options: There are too many dead leaves in it.
It is too cold for the bacteria.
The roots cannot get enough air.
The plants cannot get enough light.
questions.explain: 第二段說植物的根也需要空氣才能呼吸，所以在硬土裡長不好，也就是根得不到足夠的空氣，故選 (C)。(A) 枯葉在文中是被細菌分解成養分的好東西，並不是植物長不好的原因。
questions.evidence: Roots also need air to breathe, so plants grow badly in hard soil.

questions.stem: What did the club do because it had a small budget?
options: It made its own plant food from leaves, fruit skins, and soil.
It asked the school for more money.
It sold tomatoes to buy plant food.
It stopped growing plants for two months.
questions.explain: 第三段說社團預算不多，所以學生用落葉、果皮和泥土自己做肥料，故選 (A)。(D) 的 two months 是做土所花的時間，並不是停止種植。
questions.evidence: The club had a small budget, so the students made their own plant food.

questions.stem: The word "bind" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 米亞用軟繩把番茄「綁」在支架上，bind 在此就是「綁、捆」的意思，與 tie 最接近，故選 (B)。用繩子不可能「澆水」或「剪」植物，(A)、(C) 都不合。
questions.evidence: used soft string to bind the tall tomato plants to sticks

questions.stem: What is Mr. Chen's main point in the passage?
options: Students should not join a club with a small budget.
Tomatoes are the easiest plants to grow at school.
Bad smells mean that the soil is bad for plants.
Healthy soil full of tiny life is the key to growing good plants.
questions.explain: 陳老師從「腳下有一整個世界」講到細菌、自製土壤，最後總結「好的農業是從土壤裡的微小生命開始的」，故選 (D)。(C) 與文意不符，臭味只是做土初期的現象，最後還是做出了肥沃的土。
questions.evidence: "Good agriculture starts with the tiny life in the soil," Mr. Chen said.

vocab.stem: The weather was so ______ last weekend that we stayed home and watched movies.
vocab.explain: 天氣「糟透了」所以待在家看電影，awful 最合語意，故選 awful。accurate（準確的）、additional（額外的）、aware（察覺的）都不能用來形容天氣。

vocab.stem: The doctor told Ben to sit down and ______ slowly to calm himself.
vocab.explain: 醫生要 Ben 坐下來慢慢「呼吸」好讓自己冷靜，breathe slowly 是自然的搭配，故選 breathe。arrest（逮捕）、weave（編織）、bind（綁）都不能單獨接 slowly 表達冷靜下來。

title: From Hello to Best Friend
paragraphs: On a [[chilly|L3-0142]] morning in her first week at a new school, Lisa sat alone in the classroom. She wanted to make friends, but she did not [[dare|L3-0214]] to start a conversation. "What if I say something silly?" she thought.

[[Scientists|L3-0767]] who study friendship have reached an interesting [[conclusion|L3-0179]]: close friendships rarely start with one big moment. They grow from many small ones. One study found that it takes about 50 hours together to turn a stranger into a [[casual|L3-0131]] friend, and over 200 hours to become close friends. Much of that time is spent in simple [[chats|L3-0136]] about homework or lunch.

These small chats give us [[clues|L3-0160]] about each other. When we [[communicate|L3-0173]] often, we learn who likes the same music and who always shares her [[crispy|L3-0207]] snacks. Strangers become [[familiar|L3-0311]] faces, we [[relax|L3-0710]], and our talks slowly [[deepen|L3-0225]] into trust. So do not feel [[confused|L3-0182]] if a friendship grows slowly. There is no fast way.

Saying hello is not [[costly|L3-0190]], and every lunch break is an [[opportunity|L3-0586]]. The next week, Lisa asked the girl next to her about her [[collection|L3-0166]] of cute pencils. By the end of the [[semester|L3-0775]], the two were eating lunch together every day.
zh: 在新學校第一週一個涼颼颼的早上，麗莎獨自坐在教室裡。她很想交朋友，卻不敢開口聊天。「萬一我說了什麼蠢話怎麼辦？」她心想。
研究友誼的科學家得出一個有趣的結論：親密的友誼很少是從某個重大時刻開始的，而是由許多小時刻累積而成。有一項研究發現，把一個陌生人變成普通朋友，大約需要相處 50 個小時；要成為親密好友，則需要超過 200 個小時。這些時間大多花在簡單的閒聊上，像是聊作業或午餐。
這些閒聊能讓我們得到關於彼此的線索。經常溝通，我們就會知道誰喜歡同樣的音樂，誰總是會分享她的酥脆零食。陌生人變成熟悉的面孔，我們也放鬆下來，對話就慢慢加深成信任。所以，如果友誼成長得很慢，也不必感到困惑。這件事沒有捷徑。
打聲招呼不需要付出什麼代價，而每一次午餐時間都是一個機會。隔週，麗莎向坐在旁邊的女生問起她收藏的可愛鉛筆。到了學期末，兩個人每天都一起吃午餐。

questions.stem: Why did Lisa sit alone in the classroom at first?
options: She did not want to make any friends.
She was busy with her homework.
She was afraid of saying something silly.
Her classmates did not speak to her.
questions.explain: 第一段說麗莎想交朋友卻不敢開口，因為怕自己說出蠢話，故選 (C)。(A) 與文意相反，她其實很想交朋友。
questions.evidence: She wanted to make friends, but she did not dare to start a conversation. "What if I say something silly?" she thought.

questions.stem: According to the scientists, how are close friendships usually built?
options: Through many small moments over a long time
Through one big and exciting moment
questions.explain: 第二段說親密的友誼很少從一個重大時刻開始，而是由許多小時刻累積而成，故選 (A)。(B) 正是文章否定的說法。
questions.evidence: close friendships rarely start with one big moment. They grow from many small ones.

questions.stem: The word "deepen" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: deepen 是「加深」，句子說對話慢慢加深成信任，也就是關係「變得更堅固」，故選 (D)。(B) 方向相反，文中的友誼是越來越深，不是越來越淺短。
questions.evidence: our talks slowly deepen into trust

questions.stem: What can we infer about Lisa at the end of the passage?
options: She decided to change schools again.
A small first step helped her make a friend.
She still did not dare to speak to anyone.
She started her own pencil collection.
questions.explain: 最後一段說她主動問隔壁同學的鉛筆收藏，到學期末兩人每天一起吃午餐，可推知一個小小的開頭讓她交到了朋友，故選 (B)。(D) 只抓到 collection 這個字，文中收藏鉛筆的是那位同學，不是麗莎。
questions.evidence: By the end of the semester, the two were eating lunch together every day.

vocab.stem: The baby began to ______ across the floor toward her favorite toy.
vocab.explain: 嬰兒在地板上「爬」向最喜歡的玩具，crawl across the floor 是常見搭配，故選 crawl。dare（敢）、deposit（存放）、confuse（使困惑）都不能接 across the floor 表示移動。

vocab.stem: The school sports ______ decided to hold the event in November this year.
vocab.explain: 能「做決定」的必須是人組成的團體，sports committee 是「運動會委員會」，故選 committee。cupboard（櫥櫃）、column（柱子；專欄）、cradle（搖籃）都不會做決定。

title: Paper Folding Club: Join Us!
paragraphs: Do you have a piece of paper? Then you are ready. No screens, no [[electricity|L3-0281]], and no [[costly|L3-0190]] tools—just your two hands and your [[imagination|L3-0424]].

What We Do: Every week, members learn to [[fold|L3-0334]] something new. Beginners start with boats and birds. Later, you can try a [[dinosaur|L3-0241]] with a long tail or a [[crown|L3-0209]] fit for an [[emperor|L3-0287]]. The size of your paper will [[determine|L3-0236]] how big your work can be. Our members are happy to give [[guidance|L3-0373]] to anyone who is new, so don't be [[fearful|L3-0317]] if your first try looks [[awful|L3-0053]]. Everyone's does!

Why Join? Folding is an [[enjoyable|L3-0291]] way to [[relax|L3-0710]] after class. Some of our members' works are so [[expressive|L3-0303]] that they seem to have feelings, like a sad fox or a proud horse. Last year, our [[dramatic|L3-0261]] paper dragon won first place at the school art show, and its photos brought our club page hundreds of new [[followers|L3-0335]].

When and Where: Fridays, 4:10–5:30 p.m., Room 502. Take the [[elevator|L3-0284]] to the fifth floor and turn left at the water [[fountain|L3-0339]]. Members get a 10% [[discount|L3-0244]] on paper at the school bookstore. Come once, and you may love folding [[forever|L3-0337]]!
zh: 你手邊有一張紙嗎？那你已經準備好了。不用螢幕、不用電，也不需要昂貴的工具——只要你的雙手和想像力。
社團活動：每週，社員都會學摺一樣新東西。初學者從小船和小鳥開始。之後，你可以挑戰一隻長尾巴的恐龍，或是一頂適合皇帝戴的王冠。紙張的大小會決定你的作品能做多大。社員們很樂意指導每一位新朋友，所以如果你第一次摺得很醜，也別害怕。每個人第一次都是這樣！
為什麼要加入？摺紙是下課後放鬆的愉快方式。有些社員的作品非常傳神，好像有感情一樣，例如一隻難過的狐狸或一匹驕傲的馬。去年，我們那隻氣勢驚人的紙龍在校內美展拿下第一名，它的照片也為社團專頁帶來好幾百位新追蹤者。
時間地點：每週五下午 4:10–5:30，502 教室。搭電梯到五樓，在飲水機左轉。社員在學校書店買紙可享九折優惠。來一次，你可能就會永遠愛上摺紙！

questions.stem: Where does the club meet?
options: Next to the water fountain on the first floor
In Room 502 on the fifth floor
questions.explain: 最後一段寫明每週五在 502 教室，要搭電梯到五樓，故選 (C)。(B) 是混淆選項，飲水機只是在五樓指路用的地標，而且不是一樓。
questions.evidence: Fridays, 4:10–5:30 p.m., Room 502. Take the elevator to the fifth floor

questions.stem: What happened to the club's paper dragon last year?
options: It won first place at the school art show.
It was sold at the school bookstore.
It was folded by a new member.
It was too big to fit in the room.
questions.explain: 第三段說紙龍在校內美展拿下第一名，故選 (A)。文中沒有說紙龍被賣掉或是由新社員摺的，(B)、(C) 皆無根據。
questions.evidence: Last year, our dramatic paper dragon won first place at the school art show

questions.stem: The word "expressive" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: expressive 是「富有表情的、傳神的」，後面說作品好像有感情，例如難過的狐狸、驕傲的馬，所以是 full of feeling，故選 (B)。(C) 難摺與文意無關。
questions.evidence: Some of our members' works are so expressive that they seem to have feelings

questions.stem: What can we infer from the poster?
options: Only students who are good at art can join.
Members must buy costly tools before the first class.
The club meets every day after class.
Students with no folding experience are welcome.
questions.explain: 海報說社員樂意指導新人、初學者從小船小鳥開始，第一次摺得醜也沒關係，可推知沒有經驗也歡迎加入，故選 (D)。(B) 與第一段「不需要昂貴的工具」相反。
questions.evidence: Our members are happy to give guidance to anyone who is new

vocab.stem: The taxi ______ from the airport to the city center is about 1,000 dollars.
vocab.explain: 計程車從機場到市中心的「車資」約一千元，fare 專指交通工具的費用，故選 fare。fountain（噴泉）、faucet（水龍頭）、follower（追隨者）都不是搭車要付的費用。

vocab.stem: Use the other end of your pencil to ______ the wrong answer and try again.
vocab.explain: 用鉛筆的另一端（橡皮擦）把錯的答案「擦掉」再試一次，故選 erase。dine（用餐）、elbow（用手肘推擠）不合語意；dump（傾倒、丟棄）是倒垃圾之類的動作，不能用在擦掉答案。

title: When the Sea Steps Back
paragraphs: If you stay on a beach all day, you will notice something [[dramatic|L3-0261]]. In the morning, the water may reach the rocks [[beneath|L3-0074]] a path by the sea. By afternoon, it may have moved back hundreds of meters, leaving wet sand and small pools behind. Then, slowly, it returns. This rise and fall of the sea is called the [[tide|L3-0910]].

People once found tides [[confusing|L3-0182]]. Over time, [[scientists|L3-0767]] reached a clear [[conclusion|L3-0179]]: the moon is the main cause. It pulls on the earth, and this pull is strongest on the side nearest to it. The ocean on that side rises toward the moon, and the ocean on the far side rises, too. As the earth turns, many places pass through two high tides and two low tides about every day. The sun plays a part as well: when the sun and the moon are in a line, the tides become even higher and lower.

Tides are not only a [[theory|L3-0904]] in science books; they shape daily life. Before leaving the [[harbor|L3-0382]], people who fish check tide tables, because a boat can get stuck in [[shallow|L3-0782]] water. On some coasts, low tide opens a [[trail|L3-0924]] across the sand to a small island, and tide tables [[enable|L3-0288]] visitors to plan their walks.

Low tide is also a good time for [[adventure|L3-0010]]. In the pools left behind, you may see crabs [[crawl|L3-0199]] over the rocks. Visitors should stay [[aware|L3-0052]] of the time, though, because the water can come back faster than they expect. Before you go, check an [[accurate|L3-0003]] tide table and [[determine|L3-0236]] when you must return. With a little care, the sea's daily movement can be one of nature's most [[enjoyable|L3-0291]] shows.
zh: 如果你在海灘上待一整天，就會注意到一個驚人的變化。早上，海水可能會漫到海邊小路下方的岩石；到了下午，海水可能已經退後好幾百公尺，留下濕漉漉的沙灘和一個個小水窪。接著，海水又慢慢回來。海水這樣一漲一退，就叫做潮汐。
人們曾經對潮汐感到困惑。隨著時間過去，科學家得出明確的結論：月球是主要的成因。月球會拉引地球，而這股引力在最靠近月球的那一側最強。那一側的海水會朝月球升高，而另一側遠端的海水也會升高。隨著地球自轉，許多地方大約每天會經歷兩次漲潮和兩次退潮。太陽也有影響：當太陽和月球排成一直線時，漲潮會更高，退潮會更低。
潮汐不只是科學書裡的理論，它也影響著日常生活。捕魚的人在離開港口前會先查潮汐表，因為船可能會在淺水處擱淺。在某些海岸，退潮時會在沙灘上露出一條通往小島的步道，潮汐表能讓遊客規劃步行的時間。
退潮也是探險的好時機。在留下來的水窪裡，你可能會看到螃蟹在岩石上爬行。不過，遊客一定要留意時間，因為海水回來的速度可能比想像中還快。出發前，請先查看準確的潮汐表，確定自己必須在什麼時候折返。只要稍加小心，大海每天的漲退就能成為大自然最令人愉快的表演之一。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How people catch fish in shallow water
What tides are, what causes them, and how they affect people
Why the moon looks bigger on some nights
How to build a path across the sand to an island
questions.explain: 第一段介紹潮汐現象，第二段說明成因（月球與太陽的引力），第三、四段談潮汐對捕魚、遊客與探險的影響，故選 (B)。(A) 捕魚只是第三段的一個例子，不足以涵蓋全文。
questions.evidence: This rise and fall of the sea is called the tide.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, when do the tides become even higher and lower?
options: When the sun and the moon are in a line
When many boats leave the harbor
When many visitors walk on the beach
questions.explain: 第二段最後一句說，當太陽和月球排成一直線時，漲潮會更高、退潮會更低，故選 (A)。(B) 只是把第三段的 harbor 拿來混淆，船隻出港並不會影響潮汐。
questions.evidence: when the sun and the moon are in a line, the tides become even higher and lower

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the trail to the small island in paragraph 3?
options: It was built by people who fish.
It can only be used at night.
It is under water when the tide is high.
It is the safest path on the coast.
questions.explain: 第三段說步道是「退潮時」才會露出來，而且需要靠潮汐表規劃步行時間，可推知漲潮時步道會被海水淹沒，故選 (C)。(D) 文中沒有提到這條路最安全，反而第四段提醒要注意海水回來的時間。
questions.evidence: low tide opens a trail across the sand to a small island, and tide tables enable visitors to plan their walks

questions.stem: In paragraph 2, what does "it" in "the side nearest to it" refer to?
questions.explain: 前一句說月球是主要成因，接著說「它」拉引地球，這股引力在「最靠近它」的那一側最強，這裡的 it 指的是施力的月球，下一句「朝月球升高」也可佐證，故選 (D)。(A) 不對，side 本身就是地球的一側，不會說地球最靠近地球。
questions.evidence: It pulls on the earth, and this pull is strongest on the side nearest to it.

vocab.stem: My grandparents like to ______ at a quiet restaurant by the river on weekends.
vocab.explain: 爺爺奶奶週末喜歡到河邊安靜的餐廳「用餐」，dine at a restaurant 是固定搭配，故選 dine。dump（傾倒）、fold（摺疊）、erase（擦掉）都不能接 at a restaurant。

vocab.stem: Thank you for being ______ with me. I needed to hear the truth, even though it hurt.
vocab.explain: 對方願意說出真話、即使聽了會難過，表示對方很「坦白」，be frank with someone 是常見用法，故選 frank。fearful（害怕的）、enjoyable（令人愉快的）、dramatic（戲劇性的）都與「說真話」不符。

title: Two Weeks on a Duck Farm
paragraphs: Last summer, Ben spent two weeks as a volunteer on a small farm in eastern Taiwan. Getting there was a long [[journey|L3-0457]]: three hours by train and another hour by bus. He stayed at a small [[inn|L3-0435]] near the farm.

The work was hard. The air was hot and [[humid|L3-0418]], and by eight his shirt was wet with [[sweat|L3-0878]]. He carried [[hay|L3-0389]] to the cows and climbed a [[ladder|L3-0476]] to pick fruit for the summer [[harvest|L3-0385]]. Once, he took a [[hasty|L3-0386]] step and fell. Luckily, the [[injury|L3-0434]] was small, and the farmer, Mrs. Lin, handed him a first-aid [[kit|L3-0469]].

Mrs. Lin grew rice without [[harmful|L3-0384]] chemicals. Instead, she kept ducks in the fields to eat insects. Each morning, Ben helped her [[inspect|L3-0438]] the rice for insects, and the hard work soon became a [[routine|L3-0746]]. The ducks were very [[intelligent|L3-0440]]. Within days, they knew his voice and came running when he called.

Near the end of his stay, Ben watched some baby ducks [[hatch|L3-0387]]. As they broke out of their shells, he felt [[hopeful|L3-0410]] about his own future. Before he left, Mrs. Lin [[informed|L3-0432]] him that the farm would need [[additional|L3-0006]] help next summer. Ben had already decided to come back.
zh: 去年暑假，班（Ben）在台灣東部一座小農場當了兩個星期的志工。到那裡是一段漫長的旅程：搭三小時的火車，再轉一小時的公車。他住在農場附近的一間小旅店。
這份工作很辛苦。空氣又熱又潮濕，不到八點，他的襯衫就被汗水浸濕了。他要把乾草搬去餵牛，還要爬梯子摘水果，準備夏季的收成。有一次，他腳步太匆忙而跌倒了。幸好傷勢不重，農場主人林太太遞給他一個急救包。
林太太種稻不用有害的化學藥劑，而是在田裡養鴨子吃蟲。每天早上，班都會幫她檢查稻子有沒有蟲，這些辛苦的工作很快就成了例行公事。鴨子非常聰明：才幾天，牠們就認得他的聲音，他一叫就跑過來。
在農場的日子快結束時，班看到幾隻小鴨子孵化。看著牠們破殼而出，他對自己的未來充滿了希望。離開前，林太太告訴他，農場明年夏天還需要更多人手。班早就決定要回來了。

questions.stem: How did Ben get to the farm?
options: He drove a car for four hours.
He took a plane and then a taxi.
He walked from a small inn.
He took a train and then a bus.
questions.explain: 第一段說去農場要搭三小時火車，再轉一小時公車，故選 (D)。(C) 的 inn 是他到了之後住的地方，不是交通方式。
questions.evidence: three hours by train and another hour by bus

questions.stem: Why did Mrs. Lin keep ducks in her fields?
options: To sell their eggs at the market
To eat the insects instead of using chemicals
To carry hay to the cows
To wake Ben up in the morning
questions.explain: 第三段說林太太種稻不用有害的化學藥劑，而是養鴨子在田裡吃蟲，故選 (B)。文中沒有提到賣鴨蛋，(A) 是無中生有。
questions.evidence: Mrs. Lin grew rice without harmful chemicals. Instead, she kept ducks in the fields to eat insects.

questions.stem: The word "hasty" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: hasty 是「匆忙的、草率的」，他因為腳步太急而跌倒，與 too quick 最接近，故選 (A)。(B) 意思正好相反，小心慢走就不容易跌倒。
questions.evidence: Once, he took a hasty step and fell.

questions.stem: What can we infer about Ben from the last paragraph?
options: He was glad that the hard work was finally over.
He wanted to buy some ducks for his family.
He enjoyed the experience and wanted to help again.
He did not like Mrs. Lin's way of farming.
questions.explain: 最後一段說林太太提到明年還需要人手，而班「早就決定要回來」，可推知他很喜歡這次經驗、想再來幫忙，故選 (C)。(A) 與文意相反，他並不是慶幸工作結束。
questions.evidence: Ben had already decided to come back.

vocab.stem: Amy is so ______ that she finished the difficult math test in only twenty minutes.
vocab.explain: 能在二十分鐘內寫完很難的數學考試，表示她很「聰明」，故選 intelligent。holy（神聖的）、humid（潮濕的）不能形容人的能力；inferior（較差的）則與快速寫完考卷的語意矛盾。

vocab.stem: Taiwan ______ most of its wheat from other countries.
vocab.explain: 台灣的小麥大多「從其他國家進口」，import A from B 是固定用法，故選 imports。inspects（檢查）、informs（通知）、hatches（孵化）都不能和 from other countries 搭配表示來源。

title: The Little Train into the Clouds
paragraphs: Amy and her grandmother had planned the trip for months: a ride on a small train up into the mountains of central Taiwan. At the station, Amy checked her [[luggage|L3-0509]] twice. Warm clothes were a [[necessity|L3-0569]], her grandmother had said, because it could be cold in the mountains even in summer.

The train was old and slow. An [[elderly|L3-0278]] couple sat [[opposite|L3-0587]] them, and the other [[passengers|L3-0615]] talked quietly. As the train climbed, the air outside became cool and [[moist|L3-0547]], and soon a thick [[mist|L3-0544]] covered the hills. Amy could see only the dark [[outline|L3-0596]] of the trees. It felt [[magical|L3-0511]], as if they were riding into the clouds.

Then something [[odd|L3-0580]] happened. Amy reached for her [[mobile|L3-0546]] phone to take a picture, but it was [[missing|L3-0542]]. She began to [[panic|L3-0609]]. The old man across from her smiled and pointed under her seat. There it was! Everyone broke into [[laughter|L3-0478]].

At the top, the mist cleared, and a [[marvelous|L3-0521]] view appeared: [[mighty|L3-0537]] mountains, one behind another, under a blue sky. Later, however, Amy told her friends that the view was not the best part of the trip. The best part was laughing with strangers on a slow little train.
zh: 艾咪和奶奶計畫這趟旅行好幾個月了：搭一列小火車，一路開上台灣中部的山區。在車站，艾咪把行李檢查了兩遍。奶奶說過，保暖的衣服是必需品，因為山上即使在夏天也可能很冷。
火車又老又慢。一對年長的夫婦坐在她們對面，其他乘客則輕聲聊天。隨著火車往上爬，窗外的空氣變得涼爽又濕潤，不久，一片濃霧籠罩了山丘。艾咪只看得見樹木黑黑的輪廓。那感覺好神奇，彷彿她們正搭著火車駛進雲裡。
接著發生了一件怪事。艾咪伸手拿手機想拍照，手機卻不見了。她開始慌了起來。坐在對面的老先生笑了笑，指了指她的座位底下。手機就在那裡！大家都笑了出來。
到了山頂，霧氣散去，眼前出現了壯麗的景色：雄偉的群山一座接著一座，矗立在藍天下。不過後來她告訴朋友，這趟旅程最棒的部分並不是風景，而是在一列慢吞吞的小火車上，和陌生人一起開懷大笑。

questions.stem: Why did Amy's grandmother tell her to bring warm clothes?
options: It could be cold in the mountains even in summer.
They planned to stay in the mountains for months.
Amy had caught a cold before the trip.
questions.explain: 第一段說奶奶提醒保暖衣物是必需品，因為山上即使夏天也可能很冷，故選 (B)。(C) 的 months 是她們「計畫」這趟旅行的時間，不是待在山上的時間。
questions.evidence: Warm clothes were a necessity, her grandmother had said, because it could be cold in the mountains even in summer.

questions.stem: Where did Amy's phone turn out to be?
questions.explain: 第三段說對面的老先生指了指她的座位底下，手機就在那裡，故選 (C)。(B) 老先生只是用手指出位置，手機並不在他手上。
questions.evidence: The old man across from her smiled and pointed under her seat.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3, what does "it" in "There it was!" refer to?
questions.explain: 前文說艾咪的手機不見了，老先生指向她座位底下，There it was! 意思是「它就在那裡」，it 指的是找回來的手機，故選 (A)。(D) 照片根本還沒拍，不可能是 it。
questions.evidence: Amy reached for her mobile phone to take a picture, but it was missing.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Old trains are too slow for young travelers.
Travelers should always keep their phones in their hands.
The mountains of central Taiwan are famous for their mist.
Sharing a happy moment with others can be the best part of a trip.
questions.explain: 文末艾咪說旅程最棒的不是風景，而是和陌生人一起歡笑，點出全文重點，故選 (D)。(B) 只是從手機不見的小插曲延伸出來，並非作者要表達的主旨。
questions.evidence: The best part was laughing with strangers on a slow little train.

vocab.stem: Don't forget to ______ the door when you leave the house.
vocab.explain: 出門時別忘了「鎖」門，lock the door 是固定搭配，故選 lock。owe（欠）、lick（舔）、outline（畫出輪廓）都不是出門前對門該做的事。

vocab.stem: Please write your name on the box with a black ______.
vocab.explain: 用黑色的「麥克筆」在箱子上寫名字，故選 marker。mayor（市長）、limb（四肢）、miracle（奇蹟）都不是書寫工具。

title: The Puppet Master's Hands
paragraphs: For a school report, Mia visited Mr. Chen, who has given glove [[puppet|L3-0686]] shows for over forty years. His small room was full of [[piles|L3-0636]] of [[colorful|L3-0168]] cloth and puppet heads made of wood.

Mr. Chen showed her how a glove puppet works. The [[performer|L3-0629]] puts one hand inside the puppet's body, which is like a cloth bag. One finger moves the head, two others move the arms, and the [[palm|L3-0607]] stays hidden inside. "It takes years to learn the [[technique|L3-0894]]," he said, "before you can make a puppet walk, bow, or [[pretend|L3-0669]] to cry." He even [[persuaded|L3-0633]] Mia to try, but her puppet fell over at once.

In the [[previous|L3-0671]] century, glove puppet [[performances|L3-0630]] were often held [[outdoors|L3-0593]] at temple festivals. Today, fewer young people watch them, but Mr. Chen has not lost his [[passion|L3-0616]]. Each show still takes him weeks of [[preparation|L3-0667]], and a [[professor|L3-0676]] once brought her students to learn from him.

Before Mia left, a [[photographer|L3-0634]] came to take Mr. Chen's [[portrait|L3-0658]]. He held up his favorite puppet, an old hero with a red face. Mia wrote down a sentence to [[quote|L3-0691]] in her report: "A puppet has no life of its own. It borrows mine."
zh: 為了寫學校報告，米亞拜訪了陳老師。他演布袋戲已經超過四十年。他的小房間裡堆滿了一疊疊色彩繽紛的布料，還有一個個木頭做的戲偶頭。
陳老師示範布袋戲偶是怎麼操作的。表演者把一隻手伸進戲偶那像布袋一樣的身體裡，一根手指控制頭部，另外兩根手指控制雙手，手掌則藏在裡面。「要花好幾年才能學會這門技巧，」他說，「然後你才能讓戲偶走路、鞠躬，或假裝哭泣。」他甚至說服米亞試試看，但她的戲偶馬上就倒了。
在上個世紀，布袋戲常在廟會時於戶外演出。如今看布袋戲的年輕人變少了，但陳老師並沒有失去熱情。每一場戲仍要花上他好幾週的準備時間，還曾有一位教授帶著學生來向他學習。
米亞離開前，一位攝影師來替陳老師拍肖像照。他舉起最心愛的戲偶——一位紅臉的老英雄。米亞記下一句話，準備在報告中引用：「戲偶本身沒有生命，它借用的是我的生命。」

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, how does a performer move a glove puppet's head?
questions.explain: 第二段說一根手指控制頭部，另外兩根手指控制雙手，手掌藏在裡面，故選 (A)。(B) 不對，手掌是藏在戲偶身體裡，並不是用來動頭的。
questions.evidence: One finger moves the head, two others move the arms, and the palm stays hidden inside.

questions.stem: Where were glove puppet shows often performed in the previous century?
questions.explain: 第三段說上個世紀布袋戲常在廟會時於戶外演出，故選 (D)。(B) 是混淆選項，文中只說有位教授帶學生來向陳老師學習，與過去的演出地點無關。
questions.evidence: In the previous century, glove puppet performances were often held outdoors at temple festivals

questions.stem: The word "passion" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: passion 是「熱情」，前文說看的人變少了，但陳老師每場戲仍花好幾週準備，表示他對布袋戲的熱愛沒變，與 strong love 最接近，故選 (B)。(D) fear 與文意相反。
questions.evidence: Today, fewer young people watch them, but Mr. Chen has not lost his passion.

questions.stem: What does Mr. Chen mean when he says, "It borrows mine"?
options: He often borrows puppets from other people.
His puppets are too old to use in shows.
A puppet comes alive only through the performer's skill and feeling.
He wants Mia to give the puppet back to him.
questions.explain: mine 指 my life，意思是戲偶本身沒有生命，是靠表演者的技巧和情感才「活」起來，故選 (C)。(A) 誤把 borrow 當成真的向別人借戲偶，忽略了前一句「戲偶本身沒有生命」。
questions.evidence: "A puppet has no life of its own. It borrows mine."

vocab.stem: The ______ near the river belongs to my uncle, and he plans to build a house on it.
vocab.explain: 河邊那塊「地產」屬於叔叔，他打算在上面蓋房子，property 指房地產、土地，故選 property。punch（一拳）、penguin（企鵝）、rag（破布）都不能拿來蓋房子。

vocab.stem: Our team ______ second in the national science contest last year.
vocab.explain: 我們隊在全國科展「名列」第二，rank second 表示排名第二，故選 ranked。pumped（打氣）、pretended（假裝）、persuaded（說服）都不能直接接 second 表示名次。

title: The Can Before the Can Opener
paragraphs: Today, you can open a can of corn or tomato [[sauce|L3-0755]] in seconds. Two hundred years ago, keeping food fresh was hard. Meat and fruit could [[rot|L3-0742]] within days, and in winter, meals were often [[restricted|L3-0729]] to dried or salted food.

In 1795, the French government offered a prize for a better way to keep food for its army. A French cook spent years on the problem. He [[sealed|L3-0773]] cooked food in glass bottles and heated them in boiling water. [[Somehow|L3-0815]], the food stayed good for months. The government's [[reaction|L3-0700]] was positive, and in 1810 he won the prize. Still, he never knew why his method worked. Only [[decades|L3-0220]] later did a [[scientist|L3-0767]] [[reveal|L3-0730]] that heat kills the [[bacteria|L3-0057]] that make food go bad.

Glass broke easily, so [[shortly|L3-0787]] after, people in England began using [[shiny|L3-0785]] metal cans. Early cans were very heavy, and people opened them with a hammer and a knife, which left [[rough|L3-0744]] edges. The can opener was not [[invented|L3-0442]] until almost fifty years later.
Now, cans are light and sold at a [[reasonable|L3-0701]] price. For people far from markets, cans can be a real [[relief|L3-0713]]. Not bad for an idea that once needed a hammer!
zh: 今天，你只要幾秒鐘就能打開一罐玉米或番茄醬。但在兩百年前，要讓食物保持新鮮可不容易。肉和水果可能幾天內就腐爛，到了冬天，餐點往往僅限於乾燥或鹽醃的食物。
1795 年，法國政府懸賞，徵求能為軍隊更好地保存食物的方法。一位法國廚師為這個問題花了好幾年。他把煮好的食物密封在玻璃瓶裡，再放進滾水中加熱。不知怎麼的，食物竟然能保存好幾個月。政府的反應很正面，他在 1810 年贏得了獎金。不過，他始終不知道自己的方法為什麼有效。直到幾十年後，才有一位科學家揭開答案：高溫會殺死讓食物腐壞的細菌。
玻璃很容易破，所以在那之後不久，英國人開始使用閃亮的金屬罐。這些早期的罐頭非常重，人們得用鐵鎚和刀子才能打開，還會留下粗糙的邊緣。開罐器直到將近五十年後才被發明出來。
如今，罐頭很輕，價格也合理。對住得離市場很遠的人來說，罐頭真的能讓人鬆一口氣。對一個曾經需要用鐵鎚才能打開的發明來說，這樣的成果還真不賴！

questions.stem: Why did the French government offer a prize in 1795?
options: It wanted a faster way to cook meat.
It wanted a better way to keep food for its army.
It wanted someone to invent the can opener.
It wanted to find out what bacteria were.
questions.explain: 第二段說 1795 年法國政府懸賞，徵求能為軍隊更好地保存食物的方法，故選 (B)。(C) 不對，開罐器是將近五十年後才出現，與這次懸賞無關。
questions.evidence: In 1795, the French government offered a prize for a better way to keep food for its army.

questions.stem: How did people open the early metal cans?
options: By heating them in boiling water
With a hammer and a knife
By breaking them on the floor
questions.explain: 第三段說早期罐頭得用鐵鎚和刀子才能打開，故選 (C)。(A) 是陷阱，文中特別強調開罐器要到將近五十年後才發明。
questions.evidence: people opened them with a hammer and a knife

questions.stem: The word "Somehow" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
