options: in a way that was not understood
questions.explain: somehow 是「不知怎麼地」，後文說那位廚師始終不知道方法為何有效，正是「原因不明」的意思，故選 (A)。(C) 不對，他是花了好幾年刻意研究，並非碰巧做到。
questions.evidence: Still, he never knew why his method worked.

questions.stem: What can we infer from paragraph 3?
options: Metal cans were lighter than glass bottles.
Glass bottles were safer than metal cans.
The can opener was invented by the French cook.
People used metal cans for many years before they had an easy way to open them.
questions.explain: 第三段說金屬罐在 1810 年後不久就開始使用，但開罐器將近五十年後才發明，在那之前只能用鐵鎚和刀子開，可推知人們用了很多年的罐頭才有方便的開罐工具，故選 (D)。(A) 錯，文中說早期罐頭非常重；(B) 也錯，玻璃容易破，所以才改用金屬罐。
questions.evidence: The can opener was not invented until almost fifty years later.

vocab.stem: This sweater will ______ if you wash it in hot water, so please be careful.
vocab.explain: 毛衣用熱水洗會「縮水」，shrink 指變小、收縮，故選 shrink。regret（後悔）、restrict（限制）、seal（密封）都不能當作毛衣自己發生的變化。

vocab.stem: She has put all her ______ into a bank account to pay for college.
vocab.explain: 把所有「存款」放進銀行帳戶準備念大學，savings 指積蓄，故選 savings。sauce（醬汁）、scholars（學者）、sorrow（悲傷）都不能存進銀行帳戶。

title: Mia Finds a Better Way to Lead
paragraphs: Mia's group had two weeks to make a class video to [[promote|L3-0678]] [[tourism|L3-0918]] in their [[hometown|L3-0407]], Tainan. Mia was the leader, but leading was not easy. Ben was good at [[technical|L3-0893]] [[stuff|L3-0859]] like using the camera, but he was [[stubborn|L3-0857]] and wanted to film only old temples. Lisa preferred night markets and liked to [[tease|L3-0892]] Ben, calling his ideas "boring."

Their first meeting did not go well. Ben would not listen, and in [[spite|L3-0825]] of Mia's efforts, the others [[tossed|L3-0916]] ideas around without deciding anything. That night, Mia listed everyone's ideas on her [[tablet|L3-0882]] and thought about each person's [[strengths|L3-0854]].

Next time, she came with a plan. "Ben, your camera skills are [[superior|L3-0870]] to ours, so you'll be in charge of filming," she said. "Lisa, you know the markets best, so you'll choose the places." Instead of [[squeezing|L3-0830]] the work into the last few days, they met every afternoon in the school's video [[studio|L3-0858]].

The group made [[swift|L3-0880]] progress, and the final video showed both temples and markets. Their teacher gave them a big [[thumbs|L3-0909]]-up. Mia learned that a good leader does not do everything alone; she helps every member use his or her strengths to [[achieve|L3-0005]] a shared goal.
zh: 為了一項班級作業，米雅的小組有兩週的時間拍一支短片，推廣家鄉台南的觀光。米雅是組長，但帶領大家並不容易。阿班很會操作攝影機這類技術性的東西，但他很固執，只想拍老廟。莉莎想介紹夜市，而且她喜歡取笑阿班，說他的點子「很無聊」。
他們第一次開會並不順利。阿班不聽別人的意見，儘管米雅努力協調，其他人也只是隨口丟出各種想法，什麼都沒決定。那天晚上，米雅把每個人的點子列在平板電腦上，並思考每個人的長處。
下一次開會，她帶著計畫來了。她說：「阿班，你的攝影技術比我們都好，所以由你負責拍攝。莉莎，你最了解夜市，所以由你來挑選地點。」他們沒有把工作擠到最後幾天，而是每天下午都在學校的影音工作室碰面。
小組進展得很快，最後完成的影片同時呈現了老廟和夜市。老師對他們比了個大大的讚。米雅學到，好的領導者不是什麼都自己做，而是幫助每位組員運用自己的長處，一起達成共同的目標。

questions.stem: Why did the group's first meeting not go well?
options: The video studio was too small for the whole group.
Ben did not listen, and the others could not make any decisions.
Mia forgot to bring her tablet.
Lisa refused to come to the meeting.
questions.explain: 第二段說阿班不聽別人的意見，其他人只是隨口丟出想法、什麼都沒決定，故選 (B)。(C) 平板電腦是米雅當晚用來整理大家點子的工具，並不是她忘了帶。
questions.evidence: Ben would not listen, and in spite of Mia's efforts, the others tossed ideas around without deciding anything.

questions.stem: What job did Mia give Ben?
questions.explain: 第三段米雅說阿班的攝影技術最好，所以「由你負責拍攝」，故選 (C)。(A) 挑選夜市地點是分配給莉莎的工作，不是阿班。
questions.evidence: so you'll be in charge of filming,

questions.stem: The word "stubborn" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 同一句說阿班「只想拍老廟」，第二段又說他不聽別人的意見，可知 stubborn 指「固執的、不肯改變想法的」，故選 (A)。(B) 不合文意，阿班其實很擅長使用攝影機。
questions.evidence: but he was stubborn and wanted to film only old temples.

questions.stem: What can we learn from Mia's experience?
options: A leader should do all the work by herself.
Teasing others is a good way to make a team stronger.
A team works best when it meets only once.
A good leader gives each member a job that fits his or her strengths.
questions.explain: 米雅依照每個人的長處分配工作後，小組才順利完成影片；最後一段也說好的領導者會幫助組員運用長處達成目標，故選 (D)。(A) 正好和「好的領導者不是什麼都自己做」相反。
questions.evidence: Mia learned that a good leader does not do everything alone; she helps every member use his or her strengths to achieve a shared goal.

vocab.stem: My little brother likes to ______ me about my singing, but I know he is only joking.
vocab.explain: 弟弟拿我的歌聲「開玩笑、取笑」我，後面又說他只是在開玩笑，tease sb. about sth. 是固定用法，故選 tease。toss（拋擲）、squeeze（擠壓）、suck（吸）都不能接 me about my singing。

vocab.stem: The gift shop sells T-shirts, cups, and other ______ with the city's name on them.
vocab.explain: 禮品店賣 T 恤、杯子和其他印有城市名稱的「東西」，stuff 是不可數名詞，前面接 other 不需冠詞，故選 stuff。studio、tent、stadium 都是可數名詞，單數前面不能直接接 other，語意上商店也不會賣工作室或體育場。

title: Reading with Your Fingers
paragraphs: Touch the buttons in an [[elevator|L3-0284]], and you may feel small raised dots beside the numbers. This writing, called Braille, was created by a teenager.

Louis Braille was born in France in 1809 and lost his sight as a small child. At his school for blind children, the books had large raised letters. They were heavy and [[costly|L3-0190]], so the school could not [[afford|L3-0014]] many.

Louis had a big [[ambition|L3-0023]]: he wanted blind people to read on their own. He heard about a way of writing with raised dots, and soon [[afterward|L3-0015]] he began making his own system. By fifteen, he had created a new [[alphabet|L3-0020]] in which each letter was a pattern of up to six dots.

His classmates [[admired|L3-0007]] it, and Louis later became a teacher who [[assisted|L3-0038]] younger students. However, the school did not [[approve|L3-0032]] of his system for years. Some teachers were [[anxious|L3-0027]] about writing they could not read. Louis kept teaching it [[anyhow|L3-0028]]. The school finally accepted it in 1854, two years after his death.
Today, Braille is [[recognized|L3-0704]] around the world. Printed letters must be seen, but Braille does not need to be [[visible|L3-0964]]; it only needs to be felt.
zh: 摸摸電梯裡的按鈕，你可能會在數字旁邊摸到凸起的小點。這種文字叫做「點字」，而它是由一位青少年發明的。
路易・布萊葉於 1809 年出生於法國，小時候就失明了。他就讀的盲童學校裡，書本是用大型凸起字母印成的。這些書又重又昂貴，學校買不起很多本。
路易有個遠大的志向：他希望盲人能自己讀書。他聽說有一種用凸點書寫的方法，不久之後就開始打造自己的系統。到了十五歲時，他已經創造出一套新的字母，每個字母都是由最多六個點排成的圖形。
他的同學們很欣賞這套字母，路易後來也成為老師，協助年紀較小的學生。然而，學校多年來都不認可他的系統。有些老師對於使用一種自己看不懂的文字感到不安。路易還是照樣繼續教。直到 1854 年，也就是他過世兩年後，學校才終於正式採用點字。
如今，點字已受到全世界的認可。印刷的字母必須用眼睛看，但點字不需要被看見，只需要用手去摸。

glosses.zh: 路易・布萊葉（人名；點字 Braille 即以他命名）

questions.stem: Why could Louis's school not have many books?
options: Most blind children did not want to read.
The books were heavy and cost a lot of money.
Louis's alphabet was not ready yet.
The teachers did not like reading.
questions.explain: 第二段說用大型凸起字母印的書又重又昂貴，所以學校買不起很多本，故選 (B)。(C) 時間順序不對，路易是入學之後才發明新字母的。
questions.evidence: They were heavy and costly, so the school could not afford many.

questions.stem: How old was Louis when he created his new alphabet?
questions.explain: 第三段明確寫到 By fifteen, he had created a new alphabet，也就是他十五歲時已創造出新的字母，故選 (C)。第一段雖提到點字是「青少年」發明的，但具體年紀要看第三段，其他選項文中都沒有提到。
questions.evidence: By fifteen, he had created a new alphabet

questions.stem: The word "anyhow" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 前文說學校主事者不認可、有些老師也感到不安，但路易 kept teaching it anyhow，表示「不管怎樣、還是照樣」繼續教，與 in any case 最接近，故選 (A)。其餘選項文中都沒有提到。
questions.evidence: Louis kept teaching it anyhow.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about Louis Braille?
options: He gave up his idea when the teachers did not approve of it.
He did not see his school accept his alphabet while he was alive.
He created Braille to help people use elevators.
He learned to read printed letters as a teenager.
questions.explain: 第四段說學校直到 1854 年、也就是他過世兩年後才正式採用點字，可推知他生前沒能看到學校接受他的發明，故選 (B)。(A) 與「他還是照樣繼續教」相反。
questions.evidence: The school finally accepted it in 1854, two years after his death.

vocab.stem: We can't ______ a new car this year, so we will keep driving our old one.
vocab.explain: 今年「負擔不起」新車，所以繼續開舊車，can't afford sth. 是常見搭配，故選 afford。admire（欣賞）雖然可以接 a new car，但和「所以繼續開舊車」的因果關係不合。

vocab.stem: After a long talk, my parents finally ______ of my plan to study abroad for a year.
vocab.explain: approve of sth. 表示「贊成、認可某事」，爸媽終於同意我出國讀書的計畫，故選 approved。admire、afford、assist 後面都不接 of，文法上不成立。

title: The Noise in the Basement
paragraphs: Lisa was spending the summer at her grandmother's old house by the [[bay|L3-0069]]. On her third night, she was [[awakened|L3-0050]] by a loud [[bang|L3-0062]] from the [[basement|L3-0068]]. She listened, but in the [[background|L3-0055]] she heard only the waves.
Grandma just laughed. "Old houses make strange noises," she said. But the noise came again the next night, so Lisa decided to solve the [[mystery|L3-0562]] herself.

Being a [[bold|L3-0085]] girl, she put on her [[boots|L3-0088]] and went down with a light. Books from an old [[bookcase|L3-0087]] were [[scattered|L3-0763]] across the floor, and a bag of dried fish had been torn open. Looking for [[clues|L3-0160]], she wondered, "What kind of [[beast|L3-0072]] did this? I [[bet|L3-0078]] it's a big rat."

The next night, she left some cheese as [[bait|L3-0060]] beside an empty [[barrel|L3-0067]] and waited in the dark. Around midnight, a thin gray cat jumped in through a small window, picked up a piece of dried fish, and went straight behind the barrel. There, on an old blanket, four baby cats were waiting.
Lisa smiled. The "beast" was only a mother bringing food home. The next day, Grandma put a box with a soft towel in the basement for the little family.
zh: 莉莎那年暑假住在奶奶海灣邊的老房子。第三晚，她被地下室傳來的一聲巨響吵醒。她仔細聽，但背景裡只聽得到海浪聲。
奶奶只是笑了笑，說：「老房子本來就會發出奇怪的聲音。」可是隔天晚上聲音又出現了，於是莉莎決定自己解開這個謎團。
莉莎是個大膽的女孩，她穿上靴子，拿著燈走下樓。舊書櫃上的書散落一地，一袋魚乾也被扯破了。她一邊尋找線索，一邊心想：「什麼樣的野獸會做出這種事？我敢打賭是一隻大老鼠。」
隔天晚上，她在一個空木桶旁放了一些起司當誘餌，然後在黑暗中等待。大約午夜時分，一隻瘦瘦的灰貓從一扇小窗跳進來，叼起一片魚乾，直接走到木桶後面。在那裡，一條舊毯子上，有四隻小貓正在等著。
莉莎笑了。這隻「野獸」只是一隻帶食物回家的媽媽。第二天，奶奶在地下室放了一個鋪著柔軟毛巾的箱子，給這個小家庭住。

questions.stem: What woke Lisa up on her third night at the house?
options: A loud noise from the basement
A cat crying at the window
questions.explain: 第一段說她被地下室傳來的一聲巨響（bang）吵醒，故選 (B)。(A) 海浪聲只是背景裡聽得到的聲音，並不是吵醒她的原因。
questions.evidence: she was awakened by a loud bang from the basement.

questions.stem: What did Lisa use as bait?
questions.explain: 第四段說她在空木桶旁放了一些起司當誘餌，故選 (D)。(A) 魚乾是原本放在地下室、被扯破的那一袋，後來被貓叼走，不是莉莎放的誘餌。
questions.evidence: she left some cheese as bait beside an empty barrel

questions.stem: In the last paragraph, the word "beast" refers to ______.
questions.explain: 最後一段說這隻「野獸」只是一隻帶食物回家的「媽媽」，也就是叼著魚乾回來餵小貓的灰色母貓，故選 (B)。(A) 大老鼠只是莉莎一開始的猜測，後來證明猜錯了。
questions.evidence: The "beast" was only a mother bringing food home.

questions.stem: What most likely caused the noises in the basement?
options: The waves hitting the old house
Grandma looking for her books at night
The mother cat getting food for her babies
A big rat looking for cheese
questions.explain: 地下室的書散落、魚乾袋被扯破，而莉莎親眼看到母貓從窗戶跳進來叼走魚乾、帶回給小貓，可推知夜裡的聲響是母貓找食物造成的，故選 (C)。(D) 是莉莎原本的猜測，但文中出現的是貓，不是老鼠。
questions.evidence: picked up a piece of dried fish, and went straight behind the barrel.

vocab.stem: Fishermen often use small fish as ______ to catch bigger ones.
vocab.explain: 漁夫常用小魚當「誘餌」來釣大魚，use sth. as bait 是常見說法，故選 bait。barrel（桶子）、beast（野獸）、boot（靴子）都無法用來「釣」大魚。

vocab.stem: Every morning, the birds outside my window ______ me before my alarm rings.
vocab.explain: 窗外的鳥兒在鬧鐘響之前就把我「喚醒」，awaken sb. 表示「叫醒某人」，故選 awaken。bet（打賭）、bleed（流血）、bless（祝福）放進句中都不合語意。

title: City Girl, Country Boy
paragraphs: Our school paper asked two students to write about the places where they live. Here is what they said.

Mia: I live in a tall [[brick|L3-0098]] building in Taipei, and everything I need is close by. On weekends, my family often goes out for [[brunch|L3-0101]] or a [[buffet|L3-0107]], and then we go [[bowling|L3-0090]]. When it rains, I can stay home and watch a live [[broadcast|L3-0100]] of a ball game on [[cable|L3-0118]] TV. Of course, city life has its problems. All day long, I hear [[horns|L3-0411]] and the [[brakes|L3-0091]] of cars and buses. On busy streets, it is sometimes hard to take a deep [[breath|L3-0095]].

Ben: My family lives in a small wooden [[cabin|L3-0117]] in a [[remote|L3-0718]] village. Every morning, I am woken by birds, not cars. A cool [[breeze|L3-0097]] blows almost every day, and in spring the [[bushes|L3-0115]] around our house are full of flower [[buds|L3-0104]]. In summer, the air [[buzzes|L3-0116]] with insects. But life here has its problems, too. The nearest store is ten [[kilometers|L3-0466]] away, and the bus [[bumps|L3-0111]] along a [[rough|L3-0744]] road for an hour to get there.
zh: 我們的校刊請兩位同學寫寫自己住的地方。以下是他們的分享。
米雅：我住在台北一棟高高的磚造大樓裡，需要的東西都在附近。週末時，我們家常出去吃早午餐或吃到飽自助餐，然後去打保齡球。下雨天，我可以待在家裡，用有線電視看球賽的現場轉播。當然，城市生活也有它的問題。我整天都聽得到汽車、公車的喇叭聲和煞車聲。在繁忙的街道上，有時連深呼吸都很困難。
阿班：我家住在一個偏遠村莊裡的小木屋。每天早上叫醒我的是鳥叫聲，不是車聲。這裡幾乎每天都有涼爽的微風，春天時，房子周圍的灌木叢長滿了花苞。夏天時，空氣中充滿昆蟲的嗡嗡聲。不過這裡的生活也有它的問題。最近的商店在十公里外，公車要在崎嶇不平的路上顛簸一個小時才到得了。

questions.stem: What does Mia's family often do on weekends?
options: Visit a farm in the countryside
Eat brunch or a buffet and then go bowling
Take a bus for an hour to a store
questions.explain: 米雅說週末全家常去吃早午餐或自助餐，然後去打保齡球，故選 (C)。(D) 搭一小時公車去商店是阿班在鄉下的生活，不是米雅家的週末活動。
questions.evidence: On weekends, my family often goes out for brunch or a buffet, and then we go bowling.

questions.stem: According to Ben, what is one problem with living in his village?
options: There are too many cars and buses.
The birds are too noisy at night.
It is hard to take a deep breath.
The nearest store is far away.
questions.explain: 阿班說最近的商店在十公里外，坐公車要顛簸一小時，故選 (D)。(A) 和 (C) 是米雅描述的城市生活問題，不是阿班的。
questions.evidence: The nearest store is ten kilometers away

questions.stem: The word "bumps" in Ben's part is closest in meaning to ______.
options: moves along while shaking up and down
questions.explain: 公車行駛在「崎嶇不平的路（rough road）」上，可知 bumps along 指車子「一路顛簸前進」，故選 (A)。(D) 的 smoothly（平穩地）和崎嶇的路況正好相反。
questions.evidence: the bus bumps along a rough road for an hour to get there.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why Mia wants to move to the countryside
Two students describing the good and bad sides of where they live
How to travel from the city to a village by bus
Why country life is better than city life
questions.explain: 兩位同學都先說自己住處的好處，再用 Of course, city life has its problems 和 But life here has its problems, too 帶出缺點，主旨是比較城鄉生活的優缺點，故選 (B)。(D) 文章並沒有評斷哪一種生活比較好，最後也沒有下結論。
questions.evidence: Our school paper asked two students to write about the places where they live.

vocab.stem: The driver stepped on the ______ just in time, and the car stopped at the red light.
vocab.explain: 駕駛及時踩下「煞車」，車子才在紅燈前停下，step on the brake 是固定說法，故選 brake。bush（灌木）、breath（呼吸）、bud（花苞）都不能「踩」來讓車停住。

vocab.stem: A cool ______ came in through the open window and made the hot room feel much better.
vocab.explain: 從打開的窗戶吹進來一陣涼爽的「微風」，讓悶熱的房間舒服多了，故選 breeze。cabin（小木屋）、buffet（自助餐）、brick（磚塊）都不會從窗戶「吹」進來。

title: The Clothes Clinic
paragraphs: Most of us have [[closets|L3-0157]] full of clothes we never wear. Amy, a high school student who loves fashion, decided to do something about it. Every Friday afternoon, she runs a "clothes [[clinic|L3-0155]]" in the school library.

Her [[clients|L3-0154]] are classmates who bring her old shirts, jackets, and dresses. Amy gives each piece a new life. For Ben's plain white shirt, she [[replaced|L3-0719]] the [[collar|L3-0165]] with a soft blue one and added a small pocket on the [[chest|L3-0140]].

Lisa's winter coat was too long for her. Amy made it shorter and added a high collar that reached her [[chin|L3-0144]] to keep out the [[chill|L3-0141]] of winter mornings. Then she added a [[shiny|L3-0785]] silver [[clip|L3-0156]] shaped like a star.

Amy takes photos of each piece before and after she works on it. Side by side, the [[comparison|L3-0174]] often [[amazes|L3-0021]] people. A dull gray dress becomes bright and [[cheerful|L3-0138]], and some of her designs are as [[colorful|L3-0168]] as a [[circus|L3-0149]].
Amy hopes to become a [[designer|L3-0230]] one day. "Fashion doesn't have to be new," she says. "It just has to feel like you."
zh: 我們大多數人的衣櫥裡都塞滿了從來不穿的衣服。熱愛時尚的高中生艾咪決定為此做點什麼。每週五下午，她都會在學校圖書館開設「衣服診所」。
她的客人是班上同學，大家會帶舊襯衫、外套和洋裝來找她。艾咪讓每一件衣服重獲新生。阿班有一件素面白襯衫，艾咪把它的領子換成柔軟的藍色領子，還在胸前加了一個小口袋。
莉莎的冬季大衣對她來說太長了。艾咪把它改短，再加上一個高到下巴的立領，擋住冬天早晨的寒意。接著她又別上一個星星形狀、閃閃發亮的銀色夾子。
艾咪會在每件衣服改造前後各拍一張照片。兩張照片並排時，前後的對比常常讓人驚嘆。一件黯淡的灰色洋裝變得明亮又令人愉快，而她有些設計更是像馬戲團一樣色彩繽紛。
艾咪希望有一天能成為設計師。她說：「時尚不一定要是新的，只要感覺像你自己就好。」

questions.stem: What did Amy do to Ben's shirt?
options: She gave it a new collar and added a pocket.
questions.explain: 第二段說艾咪把阿班襯衫的領子換成藍色的，並在胸前加了小口袋，故選 (B)。(A) 和 (C) 是她改造莉莎大衣時做的事。
questions.evidence: she replaced the collar with a soft blue one and added a small pocket on the chest.

questions.stem: Why did Amy add a high collar to Lisa's coat?
options: To keep Lisa warm on cold mornings
To hide a hole in the coat
questions.explain: 第三段說加上高到下巴的立領，是為了擋住冬天早晨的寒意（keep out the chill），也就是讓莉莎保暖，故選 (A)。(B) 不對，那件大衣原本就太長，艾咪是把它改短。
questions.evidence: added a high collar that reached her chin to keep out the chill of winter mornings.

questions.stem: The word "clients" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: friends who make clothes with her
people who come to her for help or service
questions.explain: 同學們帶舊衣來找艾咪改造，接受她的服務，可知 clients 指「來接受服務的客人」，故選 (D)。(C) 不對，同學只是把衣服交給艾咪，並沒有和她一起做衣服。
questions.evidence: Her clients are classmates who bring her old shirts, jackets, and dresses.

questions.stem: What does Amy most likely believe?
options: Old clothes should be thrown away.
Only expensive clothes can look good.
With a few changes, old clothes can feel new and personal.
Designers must always use new cloth.
questions.explain: 艾咪讓每件舊衣重獲新生，最後還說時尚不一定要是新的、只要像你自己就好，可推知她相信舊衣稍加改造就能煥然一新又有個人風格，故選 (C)。(A) 與「讓每件衣服重獲新生」的做法相反。
questions.evidence: Fashion doesn't have to be new

vocab.stem: Please hang your coat in the ______ next to the front door.
vocab.explain: 外套要掛在前門旁的「衣櫥」裡，hang a coat in the closet 是常見說法，故選 closet。collar（衣領）和 chin（下巴）無法用來掛外套；clinic（診所）不會設在家門旁供人掛衣服。

vocab.stem: A ______ between the two phones shows that the new one is much faster.
vocab.explain: 兩支手機之間的「比較」顯示新手機快得多，a comparison between A and B 是固定搭配，故選 comparison。chest（胸部；箱子）、client（客戶）、collar（衣領）都不能接 between the two phones 來表示比較結果。

title: Night Singers in the Grass
paragraphs: On a summer night, if you sit on the [[deck|L3-0221]] of a country house, you will probably hear "chirp, chirp, chirp" from the grass. This is the song of the [[cricket|L3-0205]], a small insect found on almost every [[continent|L3-0187]].

Crickets do not sing with their mouths. A male cricket rubs its wings together. One wing has a [[rough|L3-0744]] part like the teeth of a comb, and the other has a hard edge that runs across it to make the sound. Only males sing, and their songs are [[mostly|L3-0554]] for females. To a female, a strong, clear song is [[desirable|L3-0231]] because it may show that the male is healthy.

Crickets are always [[conscious|L3-0184]] of the sounds around them. Their ears are on their front legs! If a cricket senses danger, it stops singing at once and [[dashes|L3-0216]] away into the grass.

Not everyone loves these night singers. Some people make [[complaints|L3-0177]] when crickets keep them [[awake|L3-0049]] until [[dawn|L3-0218]]. In China, however, people have kept crickets in cages for over a thousand years to enjoy their songs, and some markets there still have cricket [[dealers|L3-0219]]. Today, [[scientists|L3-0767]] even keep a [[database|L3-0217]] of cricket songs to study different kinds.
zh: 夏天的夜晚，如果你坐在鄉間房子的露台上，大概會聽到草叢裡傳來「唧、唧、唧」的聲音。這是蟋蟀的歌聲；蟋蟀是一種小昆蟲，幾乎每一個大陸上都有牠們的蹤跡。
蟋蟀不是用嘴巴唱歌的。雄蟋蟀會摩擦兩片翅膀：其中一片翅膀上有一段像梳子齒一樣粗糙的部位，另一片則有堅硬的邊緣，邊緣劃過粗糙部位時就會發出聲音。只有雄蟋蟀會唱歌，而牠們的歌聲主要是唱給雌蟋蟀聽的。對雌蟋蟀來說，響亮又清楚的歌聲很有吸引力，因為這可能代表這隻雄蟋蟀很健康。
蟋蟀總是很留意周圍的聲音。牠們的耳朵長在前腳上！只要察覺到危險，蟋蟀就會立刻停止鳴叫，飛快地衝進草叢裡。
並不是每個人都喜歡這些夜晚的歌手。有些人會抱怨蟋蟀吵得他們一直到天亮都睡不著。然而在中國，人們一千多年來都把蟋蟀養在籠子裡欣賞牠們的叫聲，而且當地有些市場至今仍有賣蟋蟀的商人。如今，科學家甚至建立了蟋蟀叫聲的資料庫，用來研究不同種類的蟋蟀。

questions.stem: How does a male cricket make its song?
options: By opening and closing its mouth
By hitting its legs on the grass
questions.explain: 第二段說雄蟋蟀是靠摩擦兩片翅膀發出歌聲，故選 (D)。(A) 錯誤，第二段第一句就說蟋蟀不是用嘴巴唱歌。
questions.evidence: A male cricket rubs its wings together.

questions.stem: Where are a cricket's ears?
questions.explain: 第三段明確寫到蟋蟀的耳朵長在前腳上，故選 (A)。(B) 翅膀是牠們用來發聲的部位，不是耳朵所在的地方。
questions.evidence: Their ears are on their front legs!

questions.stem: The word "dashes" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 蟋蟀察覺危險時會立刻停止鳴叫，dashes away into the grass 指「飛快地衝進草叢」，故選 (C)。(A) 不對，前面才說牠會立刻停止唱歌。
questions.evidence: it stops singing at once and dashes away into the grass.

questions.stem: What can we infer from the last paragraph?
options: People in different places feel differently about crickets' songs.
Scientists want to keep crickets away from people's homes.
Crickets in cages sing louder than those in the grass.
questions.explain: 最後一段先說有些人抱怨蟋蟀吵得睡不著，再用 however 說中國人卻養蟋蟀來欣賞叫聲，可推知不同地方的人對蟋蟀叫聲感受不同，故選 (B)。(A) 不對，第一段說幾乎每個大陸都有蟋蟀。
questions.evidence: Not everyone loves these night singers.

vocab.stem: We sat on the ship's ______ and enjoyed the cool wind from the sea.
vocab.explain: 坐在船的「甲板」上吹海風，sit on the deck 是常見說法，故選 deck。dawn（黎明）、dealer（商人）、database（資料庫）都不是可以坐在上面的地方。

vocab.stem: There was a ______ amount of rain last night, and many roads were under water.
vocab.explain: 昨晚下了「相當多」的雨，所以許多道路淹水，a considerable amount of 表示「大量的」，故選 considerable。desirable（令人嚮往的）和淹水的結果矛盾；conscious（意識到的）、cruel（殘忍的）不能形容雨量。

title: Summer News from the Downtown Library
paragraphs: Dear readers, here is some important news about the [[Downtown|L3-0257]] Library this summer.

1. Reading Room Closed (July 1–14): During last month's heavy rain, water began to [[drip|L3-0262]] from the ceiling of the second-floor reading room. To fix the [[leak|L3-0481]], the room will be closed for two weeks. A [[temporary|L3-0897]] reading area will be open on the first floor.

2. Summer Programs: (a) Video Class (Saturdays, 2–4 p.m.): Learn to [[edit|L3-0272]] short videos on your phone. (b) Meet an [[Editor|L3-0273]] (July 20, 3 p.m.): Ms. Lin, an editor of a children's magazine, will explain how a magazine is made. (c) Ocean Friends Story Time (Sundays, 10 a.m., for kids aged 5–8): Children will learn how [[dolphins|L3-0252]] use [[echoes|L3-0271]] to find food. This program will [[educate|L3-0274]] young readers about sea life in a fun way.
3. Free Old [[Disks|L3-0246]]: We are getting [[rid|L3-0732]] of old music and movie disks. Each visitor may take up to five from the box near the front desk.

Please Remember: Food and drinks are not [[permitted|L3-0632]] in the reading areas, so please enjoy your [[doughnuts|L3-0256]] and [[dumplings|L3-0268]] outside. Also, please lift chairs instead of [[dragging|L3-0258]] them across the floor.
zh: 各位讀者好，以下是市中心圖書館今年夏天的重要消息。
一、閱覽室暫停開放（7 月 1 日至 14 日）：上個月下大雨期間，二樓閱覽室的天花板開始滴水。為了修理漏水，閱覽室將關閉兩週。一樓將開設臨時閱讀區。
二、暑期活動：(a) 影片課程（每週六下午 2 點至 4 點）：學習用手機剪輯短片。(b) 與編輯有約（7 月 20 日下午 3 點）：兒童雜誌編輯林小姐將說明一本雜誌是如何製作的。(c) 海洋好朋友說故事時間（每週日上午 10 點，適合 5 至 8 歲兒童）：孩子們將認識海豚如何利用回聲尋找食物。這個活動將以有趣的方式，讓小讀者認識海洋生物。
三、舊光碟免費送：我們正在清出一批舊的音樂和電影光碟。每位讀者可以從服務台旁的箱子裡拿取最多五片。
請記得：閱讀區內禁止飲食，所以請到館外享用您的甜甜圈和水餃。另外，移動椅子時請抬起來，不要在地板上拖行。

questions.stem: Why will the reading room be closed for two weeks?
options: A new floor is being put in.
Water came through the ceiling, and the leak needs to be fixed.
Too many people ate food there.
questions.explain: 公告第一項說大雨期間天花板開始滴水，為了修理漏水才要關閉閱覽室兩週，故選 (C)。(B) 是被 Downtown 這個字誤導，圖書館本來就在市中心，並沒有要搬家。
questions.evidence: To fix the leak, the room will be closed for two weeks.

questions.stem: Who can join Ocean Friends Story Time?
options: Students who want to make videos
questions.explain: 第二項 (c) 註明這個活動適合 5 至 8 歲的兒童，故選 (A)。(B) 和 (D) 是影片課程的內容，要用手機學剪輯短片。
questions.evidence: for kids aged 5–8

questions.stem: The word "dragging" in the last paragraph is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 公告請大家把椅子抬起來（lift），而不要 dragging them across the floor，兩者對比可知 dragging 指「在地上拖行」，故選 (D)。(A) lifting 正是公告希望大家做的動作，意思與 dragging 相反。
questions.evidence: please lift chairs instead of dragging them across the floor.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of this notice?
options: To ask readers to give money to the library
To tell readers about changes and events at the library this summer
To teach readers how to edit videos
To advertise a popular children's magazine
questions.explain: 公告一開頭就說要告訴讀者今年夏天的重要消息，內容包括閱覽室關閉、暑期活動、送舊光碟和提醒事項，故選 (B)。(C) 剪輯影片只是其中一項活動，不能代表整份公告的目的。
questions.evidence: here is some important news about the Downtown Library this summer.

vocab.stem: The ______ of our school paper checks every story before it is printed.
vocab.explain: 在刊登前檢查每篇文章的是校刊的「編輯」，故選 editor。disk（光碟）、dolphin（海豚）、doughnut（甜甜圈）都不會檢查文章。

vocab.stem: The old faucet kept ______ all night, and the sound kept me awake.
vocab.explain: 老舊的水龍頭整晚「滴水」，聲音吵得我睡不著，故選 dripping。editing（編輯）、educating（教育）都需要人來做；dragging（拖拉）通常要接受詞，水龍頭也不會自己拖東西。

title: Jupiter, the Mighty Giant
paragraphs: If you look up at the night sky, you may notice a bright, [[shiny|L3-0785]] point of light. It looks like a star, but it is in fact Jupiter, the largest planet that travels around our sun.

Jupiter is [[mighty|L3-0537]]: more than 1,300 Earths could fit inside it. Yet this giant is different from our home. It is made [[mostly|L3-0554]] of [[gas|L3-0354]], so it has no [[solid|L3-0813]] ground, and even if a [[rocket|L3-0740]] could reach it, there would be no place to land. Jupiter also [[spins|L3-0822]] very fast; a day there lasts only about ten hours.

The planet's most famous feature is the Great Red Spot, a huge storm that has been [[observed|L3-0578]] for more than 150 years. This [[stormy|L3-0850]] area is wider than the whole Earth, and its winds blow harder than those of any typhoon on our planet. In recent years, however, experts have noticed that the storm is [[shrinking|L3-0790]]. No one knows for sure whether it will one day disappear.

Jupiter also has many moons. In 1610, Galileo pointed a telescope at the planet and saw four small points of light moving around it: moons. In [[previous|L3-0671]] times, most people believed that everything in the sky moved around the Earth, so his discovery changed how people saw the universe.

Studying Jupiter up close is a great [[technical|L3-0893]] challenge. The planet is so far away that even a [[swift|L3-0880]] machine needs years to get there. Still, people have sent machines on these long [[journeys|L3-0457]] since the 1970s, and each has sent back new facts about this [[marvelous|L3-0521]] world. Experts are [[hopeful|L3-0410]] that future visits will help us understand how the planets around our sun were formed.
zh: 如果你仰望夜空，可能會注意到一個明亮、閃耀的光點。它看起來像一顆星星，但其實是木星──繞著太陽運行的最大行星。
木星十分龐大：裡面可以裝下超過 1,300 個地球。然而，這個巨人和我們的家園非常不同。它主要由氣體組成，所以沒有堅實的地面；就算火箭能抵達那裡，也找不到地方降落。木星的自轉也非常快，那裡的一天只有大約十個小時。
木星最有名的特徵是「大紅斑」，這是一個已被觀測超過 150 年的巨大風暴。這片狂風暴雨的區域比整個地球還寬，風力也比地球上任何颱風都還要強。不過近年來，專家注意到這個風暴正在縮小。沒有人能確定它是否有一天會消失。
木星還有許多衛星。1610 年，伽利略把望遠鏡對準木星，看見四個小光點繞著它移動──那就是衛星。在那之前，大多數人相信天上的一切都繞著地球轉，因此他的發現改變了人們看待宇宙的方式。
近距離研究木星是一項巨大的技術挑戰。木星距離非常遙遠，就算是速度很快的探測器，也要花好幾年才能抵達。儘管如此，人類從 1970 年代起就不斷派出探測器踏上這段漫長的旅程，每一架都傳回了關於這個奇妙世界的新資料。專家們滿懷希望，期待未來的探測能幫助我們了解繞著太陽的行星是如何形成的。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to find stars in the night sky without a telescope
Some interesting facts about Jupiter and how people have studied it
Why the Great Red Spot will soon disappear
How Galileo became a famous scientist
questions.explain: 文章依序介紹木星的大小與組成、大紅斑風暴、衛星的發現，以及人類派探測器研究木星，主旨是木星的特色與人類對它的研究，故選 (B)。(C) 文中只說大紅斑在縮小，並明說「沒有人能確定它是否會消失」，不能說它很快就會消失。
questions.evidence: but it is in fact Jupiter, the largest planet that travels around our sun.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the Great Red Spot?
options: It is a storm that is wider than the Earth.
It was first discovered by Galileo in 1610.
It has been growing larger in recent years.
It is a place where rockets can land.
questions.explain: 第三段說大紅斑是一個巨大風暴，範圍比整個地球還寬，故選 (A)。(C) 與文意相反，專家發現風暴正在縮小（shrinking）；(B) 伽利略 1610 年看到的是木星的衛星，不是大紅斑。
questions.evidence: This stormy area is wider than the whole Earth

questions.stem: Why was Galileo's discovery important?
options: It proved that Jupiter has no solid ground.
It showed that a day on Jupiter is very short.
It showed that not everything in the sky moves around the Earth.
It helped people send machines to Jupiter in 1610.
questions.explain: 第四段說當時大多數人相信天上一切都繞著地球轉，而伽利略卻看到四顆衛星繞著木星轉，可推知他的發現證明了並非萬物都繞地球運行，故選 (C)。(D) 不對，人類是從 1970 年代才開始派探測器前往木星。
questions.evidence: In previous times, most people believed that everything in the sky moved around the Earth

questions.stem: The word "shrinking" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 後一句接著說沒人確定它會不會「有一天消失」，可知 shrinking 指風暴「正在變小」，故選 (D)。(C) becoming stronger 與「可能會消失」的走向相反。
questions.evidence: experts have noticed that the storm is shrinking

vocab.stem: The weather was ______ all weekend, so we stayed home and played board games.
vocab.explain: 整個週末天氣「狂風暴雨」，所以只好待在家玩桌遊，故選 stormy。swift（快速的）、stubborn（固執的）、superior（較優秀的）都不能用來形容讓人無法出門的天氣。

vocab.stem: Our computer has some ______ problems, so we asked an engineer to fix it.
vocab.explain: 電腦有些「技術上的」問題，所以請工程師來修理，technical problems 是常見搭配，故選 technical。stale（不新鮮的）用在食物或空氣，不能形容電腦問題。

title: Welcoming the New Year Around the World
paragraphs: On the night of December 31, people on every [[continent|L3-0187]] wait for midnight. Yet the ways they welcome the new year [[vary|L3-0955]] a great deal, and each custom shows what people hope for.

In Spain, millions of families watch a live TV [[broadcast|L3-0100]] from a famous clock [[tower|L3-0921]] in the capital. As the clock strikes twelve, they eat one grape with each sound of the bell. Each grape [[represents|L3-0720]] good luck for one month of the year. Since eating twelve grapes in less than a minute is not easy, people [[anxious|L3-0027]] to finish in time pick the smallest grapes from the [[bunch|L3-0112]].

In Scotland, people care about who will be the first visitor to step into their home after midnight. This guest, the "first foot," is believed to [[bless|L3-0082]] the family with luck for the whole year. In the past, the first foot often brought small gifts, such as coal to keep the house warm in the winter [[chill|L3-0141]], or bread so that the family would never go hungry.

In Japan, many temples ring their bells 108 times on New Year's Eve to help people leave the old year's troubles behind. The next morning, many people get up before [[dawn|L3-0218]] to [[admire|L3-0007]] the year's first sun as it comes up.

In [[comparison|L3-0174]], the new year in Brazil arrives in the middle of summer. Many people dress in white, such as a white shirt or [[blouse|L3-0084]], and go to the beach. As a warm [[breeze|L3-0097]] blows, they jump over seven waves, making a wish with each jump.
These customs look very different, but they all come from the same [[desire|L3-0232]]: to start the year in a [[cheerful|L3-0138]] way.
zh: 12 月 31 日的夜晚，每一個大陸上的人都在等待午夜到來。然而，人們迎接新年的方式差別很大，而每一種習俗都展現出人們心中的期盼。
在西班牙，數以百萬計的家庭會收看首都一座著名鐘樓的電視現場轉播。隨著時鐘敲響十二下，他們每聽到一聲鐘響就吃一顆葡萄。每顆葡萄代表一年中某一個月的好運。由於要在不到一分鐘內吃完十二顆葡萄並不容易，急著想及時吃完的人會從整串葡萄中挑出最小的幾顆。
在蘇格蘭，人們很在意午夜過後第一位踏進家門的訪客是誰。人們相信，這位被稱為「第一腳」的客人會為這家人帶來一整年的好運。過去，「第一腳」常會帶來小禮物，例如在冬天的寒意中讓屋子保持溫暖的煤炭，或是讓全家永遠不會挨餓的麵包。
在日本，許多寺廟會在除夕夜敲鐘 108 下，幫助人們把過去一年的煩惱拋在身後。隔天早上，許多人會在黎明前起床，欣賞新年的第一次日出。
相較之下，巴西的新年是在盛夏到來。許多人會穿上白色衣服，例如白色襯衫或女用上衣，然後前往海邊。在溫暖的微風吹拂下，他們會跳過七道浪，每跳一次就許一個願。
這些習俗看起來非常不同，但它們都來自同樣的心願：以歡欣愉快的方式展開新的一年。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why people in Spain eat grapes at midnight
Why the new year comes in summer in Brazil
How to choose good gifts for New Year's Day
How different places welcome the new year and what their customs share
questions.explain: 文章先點出各地迎接新年的方式差異很大，再分別介紹西班牙、蘇格蘭、日本、巴西的習俗，最後總結它們都出自同樣的心願，故選 (D)。(A) 和 (B) 都只是其中一段的內容，無法涵蓋全文。
questions.evidence: Yet the ways they welcome the new year vary a great deal

questions.stem: According to the passage, what does each grape stand for in Spain?
options: A wish for one family member
Good luck for one month of the year
A gift for the first visitor
questions.explain: 第二段說每顆葡萄代表一年中一個月的好運，故選 (C)。(B) 鐘聲只是「吃葡萄的時機」，每響一聲吃一顆，葡萄本身代表的是好運。
questions.evidence: Each grape represents good luck for one month of the year.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the gifts that the "first foot" brought in Scotland?
options: They stood for good wishes for the family's new year.
They were used to pay for a New Year's dinner.
They were given only to young children.
They had to be returned the next day.
questions.explain: 第三段說煤炭是為了讓屋子在寒冬中保持溫暖，麵包則是希望全家永不挨餓，可推知這些禮物都象徵對這家人新一年的祝福，故選 (A)。其餘選項文中都沒有提到。
questions.evidence: such as coal to keep the house warm in the winter chill, or bread so that the family would never go hungry

questions.stem: In paragraph 5, the phrase "In comparison" is used to show that ______.
options: Brazil has more beaches than Japan
the weather in Brazil at New Year is different from that in the places described before
people in Brazil also ring bells 108 times
the customs in Brazil are older than those in Spain
questions.explain: 前面提到蘇格蘭的「冬天的寒意」，而巴西的新年卻在「盛夏」到來，In comparison（相較之下）是用來對比兩地新年時的季節與天氣，故選 (B)。(C) 敲鐘 108 下是日本的習俗，文中沒說巴西也這麼做。
questions.evidence: In comparison, the new year in Brazil arrives in the middle of summer.

vocab.stem: We got up before ______ to watch the sun come up over the sea.
vocab.explain: 要看太陽從海面升起，就得在「黎明」前起床，before dawn 是常見說法，故選 dawn。deck（甲板）、dealer（商人）、deed（行為）放在 before 後面都說不通。

vocab.stem: Asia is the largest ______ in the world.
vocab.explain: 亞洲是世界上最大的「洲」，故選 continent。cricket（蟋蟀）、complaint（抱怨）、creator（創造者）都不能用來指亞洲。

title: The Speech That Almost Didn't Happen
paragraphs: When Mia's classmates [[elected|L3-0279]] her class leader, she was happy for about five minutes. Then her teacher told her that every class leader had to give a short speech at the school art [[exhibition|L3-0297]]. Mia was a [[fairly|L3-0307]] good student, but speaking in front of a crowd was her greatest fear.

She [[envied|L3-0293]] her friend Lisa, who was always [[energetic|L3-0289]] on stage. "I'm not a [[fighter|L3-0320]] like you," Mia said. "When I see an [[audience|L3-0045]], I feel like I might [[faint|L3-0306]]." "You don't need to be a fighter," Lisa said. "You just need a plan."

So every night, Mia practiced. She learned to [[breathe|L3-0096]] slowly whenever she began to [[panic|L3-0609]]. When her hands turned into [[fists|L3-0322]], she opened them and let them rest. She even read her speech aloud to her cat, who did not seem [[impressed|L3-0427]].

On the big day, Mia stood at the [[entry|L3-0292]] to the hall. Her voice shook at first, but she kept going. Later, she felt so [[emotional|L3-0286]] that she almost cried. Her speech was not a model of [[excellence|L3-0295]], and it did not need to be. She now had [[faith|L3-0309]] in herself. She had gone [[farther|L3-0314]] than she ever thought she could.
zh: 米亞的同學選她當班長時，她大概開心了五分鐘。接著老師告訴她，每位班長都必須在學校美術展上做簡短的演講。米亞是個成績相當不錯的學生，但在一群人面前說話是她最大的恐懼。
她很羨慕朋友莉莎，莉莎在舞台上總是精力充沛。「我不像妳是個勇敢的鬥士，」米亞說。「我一看到台下的觀眾，就覺得自己快要昏倒了。」「妳不需要當鬥士，」莉莎說，「只需要一個計畫。」
於是米亞每天晚上都練習。每當她開始慌張，她就學著慢慢呼吸。當她的手握成拳頭時，她就把手張開，讓它們放鬆。她甚至把講稿大聲念給她的貓聽，不過貓看起來不怎麼佩服。
到了重要的那天，米亞站在大廳入口。一開始她的聲音發抖，但她繼續講下去。事後，她激動得差點哭出來。她的演講稱不上完美出色，但也不需要如此。她現在對自己有了信心。她走得比自己想像的還要遠。

questions.stem: Why did Mia have to give a speech?
options: She wanted to show her own art at the exhibition.
Every class leader had to give one at the exhibition.
Her friend Lisa asked her to speak for her.
She lost a bet with her classmates.
questions.explain: 第一段說老師告訴她，每位班長都要在學校美術展上做簡短演講，故選 (B)。(A) 文中沒有提到米亞要展出自己的作品。
questions.evidence: every class leader had to give a short speech at the school art exhibition

questions.stem: What did Mia do when her hands turned into fists?
options: She hid them behind her back.
She stopped practicing for the night.
She opened them and let them rest.
questions.explain: 第三段說她的手握成拳頭時，就把手張開、讓它們放鬆，故選 (C)。這是她練習控制緊張的方法之一，(B) 停止練習與文意不符。
questions.evidence: When her hands turned into fists, she opened them and let them rest.

questions.stem: In paragraph 2, when Mia says "I'm not a fighter like you," she means that she is not ______.
options: brave and strong when facing hard things
questions.explain: 這裡的 fighter 不是真的打架的人，而是指「面對困難不退縮、很勇敢的人」。米亞羨慕莉莎上台不怕，覺得自己沒那麼勇敢，故選 (A)。(C) 和人生氣與上下文無關。
questions.evidence: I'm not a fighter like you,

questions.stem: What can we infer from the last paragraph?
options: Mia gave a perfect speech and won a prize.
Mia learned that she did not have to be perfect to succeed.
Mia decided never to speak in public again.
Mia was angry that people laughed at her joke.
questions.explain: 最後一段說她的演講稱不上完美，「也不需要如此」，重要的是她對自己有了信心，可推知她體會到不必完美也能成功，故選 (B)。(A) 與「not a model of excellence」矛盾。
questions.evidence: Her speech was not a model of excellence, and it did not need to be.

vocab.stem: After a long day of hiking, the children were still ______ and wanted to play soccer.
vocab.explain: 爬了一整天山，孩子們「仍然精力充沛」還想踢足球，故選 energetic。faint 是「虛弱的；快昏倒的」，意思剛好相反，也接不上後面「還想踢球」。

vocab.stem: Our class will ______ a new leader next week, and three students want the job.
vocab.explain: 有三位同學想當，所以全班下週要「選出」新班長，elect a leader 是常見搭配，故選 elect。exchange 是「交換」，不能用來表示選人。

title: Before You Head Up the Mountain
paragraphs: Are you [[fond|L3-0336]] of hiking? Taiwan's [[geography|L3-0355]] makes it a wonderful place to hike. About two-thirds of the island is covered by mountains and hills, and many [[trails|L3-0924]] are close to big cities. But mountains can be dangerous, so always plan ahead.

First, check the weather. Mountain weather changes [[frequently|L3-0343]], and a sunny morning can turn [[foggy|L3-0333]] by afternoon. In thick fog, it is easy to get lost, especially on wide [[grassy|L3-0368]] hills where every direction looks the same. If dark clouds appear, don't [[gamble|L3-0350]] with your safety. Turn back. The mountain will still be there next week.

Second, carry a map, warm clothes, and [[plenty|L3-0647]] of water. [[Glance|L3-0357]] at your map often so that you always know where you are. On [[slippery|L3-0810]] parts of the path, take small steps and [[grasp|L3-0366]] the rope with both hands.

Finally, don't be [[greedy|L3-0369]]. People who try to climb three or four mountains in one day often end up walking in the dark. A trip should be fun, not a [[fright|L3-0344]]. Enjoy the [[grasshoppers|L3-0367]] jumping in the grass and the cool [[breeze|L3-0097]] on your face. When you get home safely, tired but [[grinning|L3-0371]], you will know that good planning made it possible.
zh: 你喜歡爬山嗎？台灣的地理環境讓它成為登山的好地方。全島大約三分之二是山地和丘陵，許多步道離大城市都很近。不過，山區也可能很危險，所以一定要事先做好計畫。
首先，要查看天氣。山上的天氣變化頻繁，晴朗的早晨到了下午就可能起霧。在濃霧中很容易迷路，尤其是在寬廣的草坡上，每個方向看起來都一樣。如果出現烏雲，別拿自己的安全冒險，就往回走吧。下週山還是會在那裡。
第二，要帶地圖、保暖衣物和充足的水。要常看一眼地圖，隨時清楚自己的位置。走到濕滑的路段時，要小步前進，並用雙手抓緊繩索。
最後，不要貪心。想在一天之內爬三、四座山的人，常常最後只能摸黑走路。旅程應該是有趣的，而不是一場驚嚇。好好欣賞草叢裡跳來跳去的蚱蜢，和拂過臉上的涼爽微風吧。當你平安到家，雖然累了卻笑得合不攏嘴時，你就會明白，這一切都要歸功於良好的計畫。

questions.stem: According to the passage, what should people do if dark clouds appear?
options: Walk faster to reach the top.
Wait under a tree until the rain stops.
Take some photos of the clouds.
Turn back and try another day.
questions.explain: 第二段說出現烏雲時，不要拿安全冒險，應該往回走，下週山還在，故選 (D)。(A) 加快腳步攻頂正是文章提醒不要做的冒險行為。
questions.evidence: If dark clouds appear, don't gamble with your safety. Turn back.

questions.stem: Why is it easy to get lost on grassy hills in thick fog?
options: The paths there are always slippery.
People often forget their maps there.
questions.explain: 第二段說在濃霧中，寬廣的草坡上每個方向看起來都一樣，所以容易迷路，故選 (A)。(B) 蚱蜢出現在第四段，是登山樂趣，與迷路無關。
questions.evidence: especially on wide grassy hills where every direction looks the same

questions.stem: The phrase "gamble with your safety" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: ask others to keep you safe
questions.explain: gamble 原意是「賭博」，這裡指看到烏雲還硬要繼續走，等於拿安全去賭，也就是「冒很大的風險」，故選 (C)。(B) 是把 gamble 誤解成真的花錢。
questions.evidence: don't gamble with your safety

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The history of hiking in Taiwan
Advice for hiking safely in the mountains
Why grasshoppers live on grassy hills
How to draw a good map
questions.explain: 第一段說山區危險、要事先計畫，接著用 First、Second、Finally 列出查天氣、帶對裝備、不要貪心三個建議，主旨是安全登山的建議，故選 (B)。(A) 文中沒有談登山的歷史。
questions.evidence: But mountains can be dangerous, so always plan ahead.

vocab.stem: My little brother is very ______ of his new puppy and plays with it every day.
vocab.explain: 弟弟每天跟小狗玩，表示他很「喜愛」牠，be fond of 是「喜歡……」的固定用法，故選 fond。greedy 是「貪心的」，不能接 of 表示喜愛。

vocab.stem: Lisa ______ at the clock and saw that she was already late for class.
vocab.explain: 莉莎「瞄了一眼」時鐘，發現自己上課已經遲到了，glance at 是「看一眼」的固定搭配，故選 glanced。grasp 是「抓緊；理解」，後面不接 at the clock 表示看時間。

title: Wanted: A Weekend Helper at a Hair Shop
paragraphs: HELP WANTED! Are you friendly and good with your hands? Green Leaf Hair Shop is looking for a weekend [[assistant|L3-0039]] to work with our [[hairdressers|L3-0375]]. No experience is needed. We will teach you everything.

What you will do: Welcome customers, wash their hair, and keep the shop clean. You will also [[fold|L3-0334]] [[heaps|L3-0393]] of towels, hang coats for our [[clients|L3-0154]] on [[hangers|L3-0381]], and sweep the [[hallway|L3-0376]]. In winter, you will turn on the [[heater|L3-0394]] before the shop opens.

Who we are looking for: Someone who is [[handy|L3-0380]] and quick to learn. [[Honesty|L3-0408]] is very important, because you will sometimes handle money. A sense of [[humor|L3-0419]] is a plus. Many customers sit with us for two hours, and a friendly [[chat|L3-0136]] makes the time pass quickly. Please wear comfortable shoes. High [[heels|L3-0395]] are a bad idea when you stand all day!

Pay and hours: Saturdays and Sundays, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. We pay NT$200 [[hourly|L3-0414]], plus a free haircut every month. Students aged 16 or older are welcome. Don't [[hesitate|L3-0398]]! Visit us at 25 Park Road, Taipei, and ask for Ms. Lin. Here's a [[hint|L3-0399]]: come with a smile.
zh: 徵人啟事！你個性友善，又有一雙巧手嗎？綠葉髮廊正在徵求一名週末助理，協助我們的美髮師。不需要任何經驗，我們會教你一切。
工作內容：招呼客人、幫客人洗頭，並保持店內整潔。你也要摺好一堆堆的毛巾、把客人的外套掛在衣架上，並打掃走廊。冬天時，你要在開店前先打開暖氣。
我們想找的人：手巧、學得快的人。誠實非常重要，因為你有時需要經手金錢。有幽默感是加分條件。許多客人一坐就是兩個小時，友善的閒聊能讓時間過得很快。請穿舒適的鞋子；整天站著工作，穿高跟鞋可不是好主意！
薪資與工時：每週六、日，上午九點到下午五點。時薪新台幣兩百元，外加每個月免費剪髮一次。歡迎十六歲以上的學生應徵。別猶豫！請到台北市公園路25號，找林小姐。給你一個小提示：帶著笑容來吧。

questions.stem: How much does the job pay?
options: Nothing, but workers get free haircuts
questions.explain: 第四段說 We pay NT$200 hourly，hourly 是「每小時」，也就是時薪兩百元，故選 (B)。(D) 免費剪髮是額外福利，不是唯一的報酬。
questions.evidence: We pay NT$200 hourly

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as part of the job?
options: Turning on the heater in winter
questions.explain: 第二段列出的工作有招呼客人、洗頭、摺毛巾、掛外套、掃走廊、冬天開暖氣，但沒有提到幫客人剪頭髮（那是美髮師的工作），故選 (C)。
questions.evidence: Welcome customers, wash their hair, and keep the shop clean.

questions.stem: The word "handy" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: good at using your hands to do things
questions.explain: 廣告開頭就問你是否 good with your hands（手巧），可知第三段的 handy 是指「手巧的、動手能力強的」，故選 (A)。(B) easy to carry 是 handy 用來形容物品「方便的」時的意思，不適合形容人。
questions.evidence: Someone who is handy and quick to learn.

questions.stem: Who would most likely get this job?
options: A 14-year-old who can only work on Monday evenings
An adult who plans to wear high heels to work
A student who does not like talking to people
A 17-year-old student who is friendly, honest, and free on weekends
questions.explain: 這份工作在週末，要十六歲以上、誠實、友善，最符合的是 (D)。(A) 年齡不到十六歲，時間也不對；(B) 廣告說穿高跟鞋不是好主意；(C) 廣告重視和客人愉快聊天。
questions.evidence: Students aged 16 or older are welcome.

vocab.stem: It is so cold in the classroom! Could someone please turn on the ______?
vocab.explain: 教室好冷，請人「打開暖氣機」，turn on the heater 是常見說法，故選 heater。hanger 是「衣架」，不能 turn on。

vocab.stem: When the teacher asked for a helper, Ben did not ______ for a second; he raised his hand right away.
vocab.explain: 後半句說他「馬上舉手」，所以前面是「一秒都沒有猶豫」，故選 hesitate。hum 是「哼歌」，和是否馬上舉手無關。

title: Living with Mochi
paragraphs: My cat, Mochi, is an [[indoor|L3-0428]] cat. She has lived [[indoors|L3-0429]] all her life. She [[investigates|L3-0444]] every bag, box, and drawer. When my grandmother [[knitted|L3-0471]] a little blanket for her, Mochi pulled it to pieces in one afternoon.

Mochi is also a little [[jealous|L3-0451]]. When I do homework on my computer, she lies down on the [[keyboard|L3-0464]]. She [[interrupts|L3-0441]] my online classes this way, too. Then she looks up at me with big, [[innocent|L3-0437]] eyes, as if she has done nothing wrong. She is [[stubborn|L3-0857]], too. Once she chooses a place to sleep, nobody can move her.

Many cats do not drink enough water, and over time this can hurt their [[kidneys|L3-0465]]. So we keep several bowls of water around the house. We also never give Mochi [[junk|L3-0462]] food, even when [[hunger|L3-0421]] makes her cry loudly. It is easy to [[spoil|L3-0827]] a pet, but the wrong food can make her sick.

Every evening, I take one treat out of a glass [[jar|L3-0448]]. Even when Mochi is fast asleep, she [[somehow|L3-0815]] hears the sound and comes running. To me, that sound means "I love you." To her, it just means "Dinner!"
zh: 我的貓麻糬是一隻室內貓。牠一輩子都住在屋裡。每個袋子、箱子和抽屜，牠都要調查一番。奶奶幫牠織了一條小毯子，結果麻糬一個下午就把它扯得亂七八糟。
麻糬也有點愛吃醋。我用電腦寫作業時，牠會直接躺在鍵盤上。牠也用這招打斷我的線上課程。接著牠會抬頭用一雙無辜的大眼睛看著我，好像什麼壞事都沒做。牠還很固執，一旦選好睡覺的地方，誰也沒辦法把牠移開。
許多貓喝水喝得不夠，時間久了可能會傷害腎臟。所以我們在家裡各處放了好幾碗水。我們也從不給麻糬吃垃圾食物，即使牠餓得大聲喵喵叫也一樣。寵物很容易被寵壞，但吃錯食物可能會讓牠生病。
每天傍晚，我會從玻璃罐裡拿出一塊零食。即使麻糬正在熟睡，牠也總能不知怎麼地聽到聲音，立刻跑過來。對我來說，那個聲音代表「我愛妳」；對牠來說，只代表「開飯了！」

questions.stem: Why does the writer's family keep several bowls of water around the house?
options: Mochi likes to play with water.
The apartment is very hot in summer.
Drinking enough water helps protect Mochi's kidneys.
Mochi is too stubborn to drink from one bowl.
questions.explain: 第三段說許多貓喝水不夠，久了會傷害腎臟，所以家裡放了好幾碗水，目的是讓麻糬多喝水、保護腎臟，故選 (C)。(D) 固執是指牠選了睡覺地點就不肯移動，與喝水無關。
questions.evidence: Many cats do not drink enough water, and over time this can hurt their kidneys.

questions.stem: What does Mochi do when the writer uses the computer?
options: She lies down on the keyboard.
She pulls the writer's blanket to pieces.
She asks for a treat from the jar.
questions.explain: 第二段說作者用電腦寫作業時，麻糬會躺在鍵盤上，故選 (A)。(C) 被扯壞的是奶奶織給麻糬的毯子，而且與用電腦無關。
questions.evidence: she lies down on the keyboard

questions.stem: The word "innocent" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: looking as if she has done nothing wrong
questions.explain: 後面緊接著 as if she has done nothing wrong（好像什麼壞事都沒做），說明 innocent eyes 是「無辜的眼神」，故選 (D)。(A) 飢餓與這段的情境無關。
questions.evidence: with big, innocent eyes, as if she has done nothing wrong

questions.stem: What can we infer about the writer?
options: The writer wants to give Mochi away.
The writer loves Mochi and cares about her health.
The writer often feeds Mochi junk food.
The writer thinks cats should live outside.
questions.explain: 作者雖然抱怨麻糬搗蛋，但很注意牠的飲水和飲食，最後還說零食的聲音對自己代表「我愛妳」，可推知作者很愛麻糬、也關心牠的健康，故選 (B)。(C) 與「從不給垃圾食物」矛盾。
questions.evidence: It is easy to spoil a pet, but the wrong food can make her sick.

vocab.stem: The police will ______ the fire to find out how it started.
vocab.explain: 警方要「調查」這場火災，查出起火原因，故選 investigate。jail 是「把人關進監獄」，受詞必須是人，不能是火災。

vocab.stem: Amy felt a little ______ when her best friend began spending all her time with a new classmate.
vocab.explain: 好朋友把時間都花在新同學身上，艾咪覺得有點「吃醋」，故選 jealous。innocent 是「無辜的」，和這種被冷落的感受不符。

title: Why Does Shaved Ice Hurt Your Head?
paragraphs: On a hot summer afternoon, you [[grab|L3-0364]] a big bowl of shaved ice with grass [[jelly|L3-0453]] and [[juicy|L3-0459]] mango on top. You eat it as fast as you can. Suddenly, a sharp pain hits the front of your head. For a few seconds, it feels [[horrible|L3-0412]]. Then, just as quickly, it is gone. If you [[frequently|L3-0343]] eat cold [[desserts|L3-0233]], you probably know this feeling well. It is called "brain [[freeze|L3-0341]]."

Why does this happen? To [[grasp|L3-0366]] the reason, we need to look inside the mouth. When something [[icy|L3-0423]] touches the roof of your mouth, the tiny blood vessels there quickly become narrower. A moment later, they open wide again to let warm blood flow back in. Your body [[reacts|L3-0699]] to this sudden change by sending pain [[signals|L3-0792]] to the brain through nerves. However, the same nerves also carry messages from your face. As a result, the brain gets [[confused|L3-0182]] and feels the pain in your forehead instead of your mouth.

[[Scientists|L3-0767]] have [[investigated|L3-0444]] brain freeze in a simple way. In one study, they asked people to drink ice water through a [[straw|L3-0853]] while machines measured the blood flow in their heads. The pain began when blood flow in the brain suddenly increased, and it stopped when the flow went back to [[normal|L3-0574]].

Although it [[interrupts|L3-0441]] your snack, brain freeze is not dangerous, and it usually lasts less than a minute. If you want to stop it quickly, here is a useful [[hint|L3-0399]]: press your tongue against the roof of your mouth to warm it up, or drink something warm. Better still, eat cold food slowly. Brain freeze may just be your body's way of saying, "Slow down!"
zh: 炎熱的夏日午後，你端起一大碗加了仙草和多汁芒果的剉冰，用最快的速度大口吃。突然，一陣刺痛襲向額頭。那幾秒鐘痛得要命，接著又一下子就消失了。如果你常吃冰涼的甜點，應該很熟悉這種感覺。這叫做「冰淇淋頭痛」（又稱「大腦凍結」）。
為什麼會這樣呢？要了解原因，我們得看看口腔裡面。當冰冷的東西碰到上顎時，那裡的細小血管會迅速收縮變窄。過一會兒，血管又會張開，讓溫暖的血液流回來。身體會對這種突然的變化產生反應，透過神經把疼痛訊號傳到大腦。然而，同一組神經也負責傳遞來自臉部的訊息，於是大腦被搞混了，以為疼痛來自額頭，而不是嘴巴。
科學家曾用簡單的方法研究冰淇淋頭痛。在一項研究中，他們請受試者用吸管喝冰水，同時用儀器測量他們頭部的血流。結果發現，當大腦的血流突然增加時，疼痛就開始了；當血流恢復正常時，疼痛就停止了。
雖然冰淇淋頭痛會打斷你享用點心，但它並不危險，通常不到一分鐘就會消失。如果想快點止痛，這裡有個實用的小訣竅：用舌頭頂住上顎讓它回溫，或喝點溫熱的東西。更好的做法是：冰的東西慢慢吃。冰淇淋頭痛或許只是身體在對你說：「慢一點！」

glosses.zh: （冰）刨成細片的；shaved ice 剉冰

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to make shaved ice with grass jelly
What brain freeze is, why it happens, and how to stop it
Why cold desserts are bad for your health
How scientists measure blood flow in the brain
questions.explain: 文章先描述吃冰時的頭痛（是什麼），再說明血管與神經的原理和科學研究（為什麼），最後提供止痛方法（怎麼辦），故選 (B)。(D) 測量血流只是第三段的研究細節，不能涵蓋全文；(C) 文中明說它並不危險。
questions.evidence: brain freeze is not dangerous, and it usually lasts less than a minute

questions.stem: According to the passage, why do people feel brain freeze in the forehead?
options: Cold food moves from the mouth up to the forehead.
The forehead has more blood than the mouth.
The nerves from the mouth also carry messages from the face, so the brain gets confused.
People often touch their forehead when they eat ice.
questions.explain: 第二段說，傳送疼痛訊號的神經也負責傳遞臉部的訊息，因此大腦搞混了，誤以為是額頭在痛，故選 (C)。(A) 冰並不會真的跑到額頭。
questions.evidence: However, the same nerves also carry messages from your face.

questions.stem: Which person is most likely to get brain freeze?
options: Amy, who drinks hot tea slowly
Ben, who eats an ice pop in small bites over ten minutes
Lisa, who eats a warm bowl of rice
Mia, who finishes a cup of ice-cold juice in a few seconds
questions.explain: 文章說冰冷的東西碰到上顎、而且吃得很快時會引起頭痛，並建議冰的東西慢慢吃。幾秒鐘就喝完一杯冰果汁的米亞最可能頭痛，故選 (D)。(B) 雖然也吃冰，但是慢慢小口吃，正是文中建議的做法。
questions.evidence: Better still, eat cold food slowly.

questions.stem: The word "grasp" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: To grasp the reason 後面接著說明頭痛的原因，可知 grasp 在這裡是「理解、掌握」，故選 (A)。(B) hold tightly 是 grasp 的字面意思「抓緊」，但「原因」無法用手抓。
questions.evidence: To grasp the reason, we need to look inside the mouth.

vocab.stem: Be careful when you walk to school today. The road is ______ after last night's snow.
vocab.explain: 昨晚下雪，今天路面「結冰」很滑，所以要小心，故選 icy。juicy 是「多汁的」，用來形容水果，不能形容路面。

vocab.stem: It is not polite to ______ people when they are speaking.
vocab.explain: 別人說話時「打斷」他們很不禮貌，故選 interrupt。investigate 是「調查」，與說話的禮貌無關。

title: Knots of Good Wishes
paragraphs: Walk into a hotel [[lobby|L3-0499]] in Taiwan during Chinese New Year, and you will probably see bright red [[knots|L3-0472]] on the walls. These Chinese knots do more than [[decorate|L3-0222]] a room. For hundreds of years, people have given them as gifts to share good wishes.

A Chinese knot is usually made from one long piece of red string. In Chinese culture, red is the color of good luck, and many knots have [[hopeful|L3-0410]] names. For example, the "double coin" knot [[represents|L3-0720]] wealth.

[[Lately|L3-0477]], this old art has become a popular [[leisure|L3-0485]] activity among young people. Amy, a student in Tainan, joined a knot class last summer. "At first, my knots were too [[loose|L3-0505]] and lost their shape," she says. "If you can tie your shoe [[laces|L3-0475]], you can start." Her teacher, who has made knots for a [[lifetime|L3-0491]], told her to keep a [[log|L3-0503]] of every knot she learned. Soon, her skills made a big [[leap|L3-0482]].

Now Amy sells knots at a weekend market. On each one, she puts a [[label|L3-0474]] that explains its meaning. The market is always [[lively|L3-0497]], and visitors often stop to watch her work. "Each knot carries a wish," she says.
zh: 農曆新年期間走進台灣的飯店大廳，你很可能會看到牆上掛著鮮紅的結。這些中國結的作用不只是裝飾房間。數百年來，人們一直把它們當作禮物，傳遞美好的祝福。
中國結通常是用一條長長的紅繩編成的。在華人文化中，紅色代表好運，許多結的名字也都寄託著美好的希望。例如「雙錢結」就象徵財富。
最近，這項古老的藝術成了年輕人熱門的休閒活動。台南的學生艾咪去年暑假參加了編結課。「一開始，我打的結太鬆，都變形了，」她說。「只要會綁鞋帶，就可以開始學。」她的老師編了一輩子的中國結，要她把學過的每一種結都記錄下來。很快地，她的技巧就突飛猛進。
現在艾咪在週末市集賣中國結。她在每個結上都貼了一張標籤，說明它的含意。市集總是熱鬧滾滾，路過的人常會停下來看她編結。「每個結都承載著一個願望，」她說。

questions.stem: According to the passage, why are most Chinese knots red?
options: Red string is cheaper than other colors.
Red knots are easy to see in a hotel lobby.
Amy's teacher only uses red string.
Red is the color of good luck in Chinese culture.
questions.explain: 第二段說在華人文化中，紅色代表好運，故選 (D)。(A) 文中沒有提到紅繩比較便宜。
questions.evidence: In Chinese culture, red is the color of good luck

questions.stem: What problem did Amy have when she first started?
options: She could not find any red string.
Her teacher did not have time for her.
Nobody wanted to buy her knots.
questions.explain: 第三段艾咪說一開始她的結太鬆，都變形了，故選 (A)。(D) 她現在在市集賣結，文中沒說沒人買。
questions.evidence: At first, my knots were too loose

questions.stem: The word "lively" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 後半句說路過的人常停下來看她編結，可見市集人很多、很熱鬧，lively 是「熱鬧的、充滿活力的」，故選 (C)。(A) 安靜冷清與文意相反。
questions.evidence: The market is always lively, and visitors often stop to watch her work.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Chinese knots are only used in hotels.
Chinese knots are an old art that young people are enjoying again.
Shoe laces are the best string for making knots.
Amy wants to work in a hotel lobby.
questions.explain: 文章先介紹中國結的傳統與意義，再以艾咪為例，說明這項古老藝術最近成了年輕人的休閒活動，故選 (B)。(A) 飯店大廳只是開頭的例子，文中說它們也被當作禮物。
questions.evidence: Lately, this old art has become a popular leisure activity among young people.

vocab.stem: Please read the ______ on the bottle before you take any medicine.
vocab.explain: 吃藥前要先讀瓶子上的「標籤」，故選 label。lobby 是「大廳」，不會出現在藥瓶上。

vocab.stem: The cat made a great ______ from the floor onto the kitchen table.
vocab.explain: 貓從地上「一躍」跳到餐桌上，make a leap 是「跳躍」，故選 leap。knot 是「結」，貓不會從地上打一個結到桌上。

title: The Magic Box in the Kitchen
paragraphs: When my little brother was four, he thought our [[microwave|L3-0536]] was a [[magician|L3-0512]]. Cold soup became hot in two minutes, with no fire or [[flame|L3-0323]]. When the machine made its low noise, he was sure a [[monster|L3-0550]] lived inside.

So how does it work? The [[majority|L3-0515]] of foods contain water. A microwave sends out waves that make the tiny parts of water move back and forth very quickly. As they move, they create heat, and this heat cooks the food. At the same time, a small [[motor|L3-0557]] turns the plate under the food so that the heat spreads more evenly.

Some parts of the food may stay cold. If you heat [[dumplings|L3-0268]] from a [[freezer|L3-0342]] at [[minus|L3-0538]] 18°C, turn them over once in the middle of cooking. Cover your food, too, or it may make a [[mess|L3-0534]]. And never cook a whole egg in its shell, because it can [[explode|L3-0300]]!

The microwave was invented by accident. In 1945, an engineer working near a machine that produced microwaves noticed that a chocolate bar in his pocket had [[melted|L3-0530]]. Since then, the number of microwaves in homes has [[multiplied|L3-0558]]. It was a small surprise, but a [[meaningful|L3-0525]] one for [[humankind|L3-0517]].
zh: 我弟弟四歲時，以為我們家的微波爐是個魔術師。冷湯兩分鐘就變熱了，沒有火，也沒有火焰。當機器發出低沉的聲音時，他就確定裡面住著一隻怪獸。
那它是怎麼運作的呢？大多數的食物都含有水分。微波爐會發出一種波，讓水的微小粒子非常快速地來回擺動。這些粒子在運動時會產生熱，而這些熱就把食物煮熟了。同時，一個小馬達會轉動盤子，讓熱分布得更平均。
食物有些部分可能還是冷的。如果你要加熱從零下18度的冷凍庫拿出來的水餃，記得在加熱到一半時把它們翻面一次。也要把食物蓋起來，否則可能會弄得一團亂。還有，千萬不要把帶殼的整顆蛋放進去加熱，因為它可能會爆炸！
微波爐是意外發明出來的。1945年，一位工程師在一台會產生微波的機器旁工作時，發現口袋裡的巧克力棒融化了。從那時起，家中的微波爐數量成倍增加。這是一個小小的意外，對人類卻很有意義。

questions.stem: According to the passage, what makes food hot in a microwave?
options: A small flame under the plate
Tiny parts of water in the food moving very quickly
questions.explain: 第二段說微波讓食物中水的微小粒子快速來回擺動，運動時產生熱，把食物煮熟，故選 (B)。(A) 第一段明說沒有火焰。
questions.evidence: As they move, they create heat, and this heat cooks the food.

questions.stem: Why does the plate inside a microwave turn?
options: To keep the food from exploding
To help the heat spread more evenly
questions.explain: 第二段說小馬達轉動盤子，是為了讓熱分布得更平均，故選 (D)。(A) 防止爆炸的方法是不要加熱帶殼的蛋，與盤子轉動無關。
questions.evidence: a small motor turns the plate under the food so that the heat spreads more evenly

questions.stem: In paragraph 2, what does "they" in "As they move" refer to?
questions.explain: 前一句說微波讓 the tiny parts of water（水的微小粒子）快速來回擺動，接著 As they move 的 they 指的就是這些在擺動的水分子，故選 (C)。(A) 食物本身並沒有在來回擺動。
questions.evidence: make the tiny parts of water move back and forth very quickly

questions.stem: What would the writer most likely tell someone who is heating dumplings from the freezer?
options: Turn them over once and cover them.
Heat them together with an egg in its shell.
Do not cover them, so they cook faster.
Put them back in the freezer first.
questions.explain: 第三段建議冷凍水餃加熱到一半時翻面，也建議把食物蓋起來以免弄髒，故選 (A)。(C) 不加蓋與作者的建議相反；(B) 作者提醒帶殼的蛋可能爆炸。
questions.evidence: turn them over once in the middle of cooking

vocab.stem: The ______ of students in our class voted for a trip to the beach, so that is where we are going.
vocab.explain: 全班「大多數」同學投票選海邊，所以就去海邊，the majority of… 是「大多數的……」，故選 majority。mess 是「混亂」，the mess of students 不合文意。

vocab.stem: If you ______ 6 by 7, you get 42.
vocab.explain: 6 和 7 相「乘」得 42，multiply A by B 是「A 乘以 B」，故選 multiply。mend 是「修補」，不能用在數字運算。

title: A Night Owl Logs Off
paragraphs: Lisa calls herself a night [[owl|L3-0600]]. Every night, she [[logs|L3-0503]] on to social [[media|L3-0528]] and posts photos under the [[nickname|L3-0573]] "Moon Cat." She has hundreds of [[followers|L3-0335]], and she often [[chats|L3-0136]] until long after midnight with a [[pal|L3-0605]] who lives [[overseas|L3-0598]].

[[Lately|L3-0477]], however, Lisa has often fallen asleep in class, and her grades have dropped. Her mother was worried. "Your life is not an [[ongoing|L3-0582]] show for strangers," her mother said. "You don't have to post every [[pancake|L3-0608]] you eat."

So Lisa made a change. She set a simple rule: no phone after 11 p.m. On weekends, she spent more time [[outdoors|L3-0594]]. When she did post something, she learned to [[omit|L3-0581]] personal details, such as the name of her school.

Her friends kept asking why she was not online, and she had to [[parrot|L3-0613]] the same answer again and again. But after a month, she was sleeping better, her desk was [[neater|L3-0568]], and she felt more [[optimistic|L3-0588]]. She even started writing a short story. "Maybe one day I will become a [[novelist|L3-0575]]," she says. She still enjoys the Internet, but now she uses it instead of letting it use her.
zh: 莉莎說自己是個夜貓子。每天晚上，她都會登入社群媒體，用「月亮貓」這個暱稱發照片。她有好幾百個追蹤者，還常和一位住在國外的朋友聊天，一聊就聊到凌晨。
然而最近，莉莎常在課堂上睡著，成績也下滑了。媽媽很擔心。「妳的人生不是一場演給陌生人看、永不停播的節目，」媽媽說。「妳不必把吃的每一塊鬆餅都放上網。」
於是莉莎做出改變。她訂了一條簡單的規則：晚上十一點以後不碰手機。週末時，她多花時間待在戶外。真的要發文時，她學會省略個人資料，像是學校的名字。
朋友們一直問她為什麼不在線上，她只好像鸚鵡一樣一遍又一遍重複同樣的回答。但一個月後，她睡得比較好了，書桌變得比較整齊，心情也更樂觀了。她甚至開始寫短篇故事。「也許有一天我會成為小說家，」她說。她仍然喜歡上網，但現在是她在使用網路，而不是讓網路使用她。

questions.stem: What rule did Lisa set for herself?
options: No more chatting with her overseas pal
questions.explain: 第三段說她訂了一條簡單的規則：晚上十一點以後不碰手機，故選 (C)。(D) 媽媽只提醒她不必把每塊鬆餅都放上網，這也不是莉莎訂的規則。
questions.evidence: She set a simple rule: no phone after 11 p.m.

questions.stem: What kind of information did Lisa learn to omit when she posted?
options: Personal details, such as her school's name
questions.explain: 第三段說她發文時學會省略個人資料，例如學校名字，故選 (A)。omit 是「省略」，表示不把這些資料放上網。
questions.evidence: she learned to omit personal details, such as the name of her school

questions.stem: The phrase "night owl" in paragraph 1 means a person who ______.
options: works as a guard at night
questions.explain: 貓頭鷹在夜間活動，night owl 用來比喻「習慣熬夜的人」；後文也說莉莎常聊到凌晨，故選 (D)。(B) 是只看 owl 字面意思的誤解。
questions.evidence: she often chats until long after midnight

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Social media is the best way to make friends.
Lisa changed her online habits, and her life got better.
Lisa's mother does not allow her to use a phone.
Lisa wants to become a famous online star.
questions.explain: 文章描述莉莎原本熬夜上網影響課業，後來訂規則、多到戶外、保護個資，一個月後睡得好、更樂觀，主旨是改變上網習慣讓生活變好，故選 (B)。(C) 規則是莉莎自己訂的，媽媽並沒有禁止她用手機。
questions.evidence: But after a month, she was sleeping better

vocab.stem: My grandfather's ______ was "Big Ox" because he was so strong.
vocab.explain: 爺爺因為力氣很大，「綽號」叫「大牛」，故選 nickname。novelist 是「小說家」，指人，不能是「大牛」這個稱呼。

vocab.stem: Even after failing the test twice, Mia stayed ______ and believed she would pass next time.
vocab.explain: 考兩次沒過，米亞仍相信下次會過，表示她保持「樂觀」，故選 optimistic。neat 是「整潔的」，和「相信自己會通過」的心態無關。

title: The Ten-Second Rule
paragraphs: Lisa used to spend every [[penny|L3-0627]] of her pocket money right away. A cute cup at the [[mall|L3-0516]], a bag of [[peanut|L3-0623]] candy, a pen with a [[playful|L3-0646]] cat on it—she wanted them all. By the end of each month, her money was gone, so she often had to [[postpone|L3-0660]] plans with friends.

[[Lately|L3-0477]], her class has been learning about money. In a [[poll|L3-0653]] about shopping habits, the [[majority|L3-0515]] of students said they often bought things they did not need. Their teacher made a [[poster|L3-0659]] with a simple rule: before you buy anything, [[pause|L3-0620]] for ten seconds and ask yourself, "Do I need this, or do I just want it?" "It is [[probable|L3-0672]] that you will forget most of these things in a week," he added.

Lisa thought the rule was silly, but when she tried it, the answer was usually "I just want it." It took [[patience|L3-0619]], but she began saving money in a [[jar|L3-0448]] with a [[label|L3-0474]] that said "Trip." Four months later, she had enough to visit her grandmother in Tainan. "What a [[pity|L3-0644]] I didn't learn this sooner," she said. "A cup is nice, but time with Grandma is far more [[precious|L3-0666]]."
zh: Lisa 以前一拿到零用錢，就會把每一分錢都花光。購物中心裡的可愛杯子、一袋花生糖、一支印著俏皮貓咪的筆——她樣樣都想要。每到月底，她的錢就花完了，所以常常只好把和朋友的計畫往後延。
最近，她們班正在學習和金錢有關的課題。在一項關於購物習慣的調查中，大多數學生表示，他們常常買下其實並不需要的東西。於是老師做了一張海報，上面寫著一條簡單的規則：買任何東西之前，先停十秒鐘問問自己：「我是需要它，還是只是想要它？」他還補充說：「你們很可能一個星期內就會把這些東西大多忘掉。」
Lisa 覺得這條規則很傻，但她實際試了以後，答案通常是「我只是想要」。這需要耐心，不過她開始把錢存進一個貼著「旅行」標籤的罐子裡。四個月後，她存夠了錢，去台南看外婆。她說：「真可惜我沒早點學會這件事。杯子雖然不錯，但和外婆相處的時光珍貴多了。」

questions.stem: What often happened to Lisa at the end of each month before she learned the rule?
options: She had to give her friends back their money.
She lost her pocket money at the mall.
She had no money left and had to put off plans with friends.
She saved her money in a jar.
questions.explain: 第一段說每到月底她的錢就花完了，常常只好把和朋友的計畫延後，故選 (C)。(D) 存錢進罐子是她學會規則「之後」才做的事，時間順序不對。
questions.evidence: By the end of each month, her money was gone, so she often had to postpone plans with friends.

questions.stem: What did the teacher's rule ask students to do?
options: Stop for ten seconds and think about whether they really need something
Buy only things that cost less than ten dollars
Take a poll before they go shopping
Put their money into a jar every week
questions.explain: 第二段海報上的規則是：買東西前先停十秒，問自己是「需要」還是「想要」，故選 (A)。(C) 做調查是全班的活動，並不是規則的內容。
questions.evidence: before you buy anything, pause for ten seconds and ask yourself, "Do I need this, or do I just want it?"

questions.stem: The word "precious" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: precious 指「珍貴的」。Lisa 拿杯子和陪外婆的時光比較，認為後者更有價值，與 valuable 最接近，故選 (D)。(A) cheap 意思是「便宜的」，正好相反。
questions.evidence: A cup is nice, but time with Grandma is far more precious.

questions.stem: What can we infer about Lisa from the passage?
options: She still buys everything she sees at the mall.
She has learned to value time with family more than things.
She does not like her teacher's ideas at all.
She wants to open a shop in Tainan.
questions.explain: Lisa 把省下的錢拿去探望外婆，並說陪外婆的時光比杯子珍貴得多，可推知她學會重視與家人相處勝過買東西，故選 (B)。(C) 她雖然一開始覺得規則很傻，但後來照做並有收穫，不能說她完全不喜歡。
questions.evidence: A cup is nice, but time with Grandma is far more precious.

vocab.stem: Because of the heavy rain, the school sports day was ______ until next Friday.
vocab.explain: 因為大雨，運動會「延期」到下週五，be postponed until... 是常見用法，故選 postponed。peeled（剝皮）、patted（輕拍）、paved（鋪路）都無法用在活動日期上。

vocab.stem: Learning to play the piano well takes years of practice and ______.
vocab.explain: 把鋼琴彈好需要多年的練習和「耐心」，故選 patience。pottery（陶器）、porcelain（瓷器）是物品，poverty（貧窮）也不是學琴需要的條件，語意不通。

title: Summers in a Fishing Village
paragraphs: Every summer, Ben stays with his grandfather in a small fishing village on Taiwan's east coast. He wakes up to the [[roar|L3-0735]] of the waves. Before the sun's first [[rays|L3-0697]] appear, Grandpa's boat is already out at sea, passing the old [[lighthouse|L3-0492]].

Grandpa once worked in an office in Taipei, but at forty he [[quit|L3-0690]] his job and came home to fish. "My [[salary|L3-0753]] was higher back then," he says, "but the sea makes me happy." Ben helps carry [[sacks|L3-0751]] of fish to the [[regional|L3-0708]] market, a [[lively|L3-0497]] place full of cooks from nearby towns. Some fish are so fresh that people eat them [[raw|L3-0696]]. Grandpa keeps his fish on ice, since fish that are not kept cold soon become [[rotten|L3-0743]].

This year, a [[rumor|L3-0748]] went around that there were fewer fish near the coast. "We must not catch the young ones," Grandpa told Ben as he put small fish back into the water. Ben used a [[recorder|L3-0705]] to save Grandpa's stories. Listening to them later [[reminded|L3-0717]] him that the sea gives us a lot, but we must take care of it. Still, Grandpa is [[optimistic|L3-0588]]: "If we fish wisely, the sea will be here for your children."
zh: 每年夏天，Ben 都會到台灣東海岸一個小小的漁村，住在爺爺家。他每天早上都在海浪的怒吼聲中醒來。在第一道陽光出現之前，爺爺的船早已出海，經過那座老燈塔。
爺爺以前在台北的辦公室上班，但他四十歲時辭掉工作，回到家鄉捕魚。他說：「那時候我的薪水比較高，但大海讓我快樂。」Ben 會幫忙把一袋袋的魚扛到地區性的市場，那是個熱鬧的地方，擠滿了來自鄰近城鎮的廚師。有些魚新鮮到大家直接生吃。爺爺會把魚放在冰塊上，因為沒有冰著的魚很快就會腐壞。
今年流傳著一個傳言，說近海的魚變少了。「我們不能捕小魚。」爺爺一邊把小魚放回水裡，一邊這樣告訴 Ben。Ben 用錄音機把爺爺的故事錄下來。後來重聽這些故事時，他想起大海給了我們很多，但我們也必須好好照顧它。儘管如此，爺爺還是很樂觀：「只要我們用聰明的方式捕魚，大海就會一直在這裡，留給你的孩子。」

questions.stem: Why did Grandpa leave his job in Taipei?
options: His salary was too low to live on.
Fishing made him happier than his office job.
He wanted to open a market in the village.
Ben asked him to come home.
questions.explain: 爺爺說以前的薪水比較高，「但大海讓我快樂」，可知他是因為捕魚比上班快樂才辭職，故選 (B)。(A) 正好相反，他以前的薪水其實比較高。
questions.evidence: "My salary was higher back then," he says, "but the sea makes me happy."

questions.stem: According to the passage, why does Grandpa keep his fish on ice?
options: So that people can eat them raw at home
So that the fish look bigger at the market
Because cooks from nearby towns ask him to
Because fish that are not kept cold go bad quickly
questions.explain: 第二段說爺爺把魚放在冰上，「因為沒有冰著的魚很快就會腐壞」，故選 (D)。(A) 雖然文中提到有人生吃魚，但那不是爺爺用冰塊保存的理由。
questions.evidence: Grandpa keeps his fish on ice, since fish that are not kept cold soon become rotten.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3, what does "the young ones" refer to?
questions.explain: 爺爺說「不能捕 the young ones」的同時，把小魚放回水中，所以 the young ones 指的是還沒長大的小魚，故選 (A)。(C) 是被 young 誤導，文中並沒有說不能「抓」Ben 和朋友。
questions.evidence: "We must not catch the young ones," Grandpa told Ben as he put small fish back into the water.

questions.stem: What can we infer about Grandpa from the passage?
options: He believes there will never be any fish near the coast again.
He thinks fishing is an easy way to become rich.
He cares about protecting the sea for the future.
He does not want Ben to visit the village again.
questions.explain: 爺爺把小魚放回海裡，並說只要用聰明的方式捕魚，大海就能留給下一代，可推知他重視為未來保護海洋，故選 (C)。(A) 與文末「爺爺很樂觀」的描述矛盾。
questions.evidence: "If we fish wisely, the sea will be here for your children."

vocab.stem: My uncle ______ smoking last year, and now he feels much healthier.
vocab.explain: 叔叔去年「戒」菸，現在覺得健康多了，quit smoking 是固定用法，故選 quit。robbed（搶劫）、pronounced（發音）、reminded（提醒）都不能接 smoking 表達戒掉。

vocab.stem: This old song always ______ me of the summers I spent at the beach.
vocab.explain: 這首老歌總讓我「想起」在海邊度過的夏天，remind sb. of sth. 是固定搭配，故選 reminds。robs 雖然也可以接 of（rob sb. of sth. 奪走），但「歌奪走我的夏天」語意不通。

title: Grandma's Banana Trick
paragraphs: Have you ever bought green bananas and wished they would turn yellow faster? Mia's grandmother has a trick: put them in a paper bag with an apple. Mia thought this was just an old [[rumor|L3-0748]], so she decided to test it for her school science project.

She divided nine green bananas of about the same size into three groups. One group stayed on the kitchen table, one went into a closed paper bag, and one went into another bag with a [[ripe|L3-0733]] apple. She [[labeled|L3-0474]] each group and kept [[neat|L3-0568]] notes, taking photos every morning before school. Waiting took a lot of [[patience|L3-0619]].

The results were clear. After two days, the bananas in the bag with the apple had turned bright yellow. The ones in the other bag came next, while those on the table were still a little green. By the end of the week, one banana in the apple bag had even gone soft and brown—almost [[rotten|L3-0743]].

Why? Her teacher, Mr. Lee, explained that ripe fruit gives off a natural chemical called ethylene, which helps fruit become ripe. A paper bag keeps this chemical close to the bananas, and a ripe apple adds even more of it. On an open table, it simply [[floats|L3-0328]] away. In other words, the old trick was not a rumor at all; it was science.

Asked what she had learned, Mia [[paused|L3-0620]]. "I used to think [[scientists|L3-0767]] only worked in labs," she said. "Now I know that grandmothers can be scientists, too." The project [[reminded|L3-0717]] her that questions from daily life can lead to [[meaningful|L3-0525]] discoveries, and she is [[optimistic|L3-0588]] that she will find many more.
zh: 你是否曾買了青綠的香蕉，希望它們快點變黃？Mia 的奶奶有個妙招：把香蕉和一顆蘋果一起放進紙袋裡。Mia 以為這只是老一輩的傳言，所以決定在學校的科學專題中驗證看看。
她把九根大小差不多的青香蕉分成三組：一組留在廚房餐桌上，一組放進封好的紙袋裡，另一組則和一顆熟蘋果一起放進另一個紙袋。她為每一組貼上標籤，並做了整齊的筆記，每天早上上學前都拍照記錄。等待需要很大的耐心。
結果很明顯。兩天後，和蘋果放在一起的那袋香蕉已經變成鮮黃色。接著是另一個紙袋裡的香蕉，而放在餐桌上的那幾根還有點青綠。到了週末，蘋果袋裡甚至有一根香蕉變得又軟又褐，幾乎快爛了。
為什麼會這樣呢？她的李老師解釋說，成熟的水果會釋放一種叫做乙烯的天然化學物質，它會促使水果成熟。紙袋能把這種物質留在香蕉周圍，而熟蘋果又會再增加更多乙烯。如果放在開放的桌面上，它就會飄散掉。換句話說，這個老妙招根本不是傳言，而是科學。
被問到學到了什麼時，Mia 停頓了一下。她說：「我以前以為科學家只在實驗室裡工作，現在我知道，奶奶也可以是科學家。」這個專題讓她體會到，來自日常生活的問題也能帶來有意義的發現，而她也樂觀地相信，自己還會發現更多。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to take good photos of fruit for a science project
Why bananas are healthier than apples
How grandmothers in Taiwan cook bananas
How a student tested an old trick and found the science behind it
questions.explain: 文章從奶奶的妙招寫起，接著描述 Mia 分組實驗、記錄結果，再由老師解釋乙烯的原理，主軸是學生驗證老妙招並找出背後的科學，故選 (D)。(A) 拍照只是第二段記錄方法的細節。
questions.evidence: In other words, the old trick was not a rumor at all; it was science.

questions.stem: Which group of bananas turned yellow first?
options: The bananas on the kitchen table
The bananas in the bag with an apple
The bananas in the closed bag without an apple
All three groups turned yellow at the same time.
questions.explain: 第三段說兩天後，和蘋果放在一起的那袋香蕉已經變成鮮黃色，最快變黃，故選 (B)。(C) 只放在紙袋裡的香蕉是第二快，並非最先變黃。
questions.evidence: After two days, the bananas in the bag with the apple had turned bright yellow.

questions.stem: Why did the bananas on the table take the longest to turn yellow?
options: The chemical that helps fruit become ripe could float away in the open air.
There was too much light in the kitchen.
Mia did not take photos of them every day.
They were bigger than the other bananas.
questions.explain: 第四段說紙袋能把乙烯留在香蕉周圍，而放在開放桌面上，乙烯就會飄散掉，因此桌上的香蕉吸收到的乙烯最少、熟得最慢，故選 (A)。(D) 與文意不符，Mia 一開始就挑了大小差不多的香蕉。
questions.evidence: On an open table, it simply floats away.

questions.stem: In paragraph 4, what does "it" in "it simply floats away" refer to?
questions.explain: 前文一直在說乙烯這種化學物質會被紙袋留住，熟蘋果還會讓它變多，所以在開放桌面上「飄走」的 it 指的是乙烯，故選 (C)。(B) 蘋果是會釋放乙烯的水果，本身不會飄走。
questions.evidence: A paper bag keeps this chemical close to the bananas, and a ripe apple adds even more of it.

vocab.stem: Before you put the jars in the fridge, please ______ each one with today's date.
vocab.explain: 放進冰箱前，請在每個罐子「貼上標籤」寫上今天日期，label sth. with... 是常見用法，故選 label。mend（修補）、omit（省略）、multiply（乘）都和「寫上日期」無關。

vocab.stem: These mangoes are not ______ yet, so wait a few more days before you eat them.
vocab.explain: 芒果還沒「成熟」，所以要再等幾天才能吃，故選 ripe。loose（鬆的）、lively（活潑的）、neat（整齊的）都不能用來說明水果能不能吃。

title: A Week at the Animal Hospital
paragraphs: Mia, a [[senior|L3-0776]] in Tainan, has wanted to be an animal doctor since finding a hurt bird in her garden as a child. Her parents had doubts. "Why not choose something more [[sensible|L3-0777]], like working in a bank?" her father asked with a [[sigh|L3-0791]].

To find out if the job was right for her, Mia spent a week [[shadowing|L3-0781]] Dr. Chen at an animal hospital. It was harder than she expected. She helped [[scrub|L3-0772]] the floors, handed Dr. Chen [[scissors|L3-0768]] during an [[operation|L3-0585]], and calmed a young [[shepherd|L3-0784]] dog that was afraid of needles. Free time was [[scarce|L3-0760]]; between visits, she could only take a quick [[sip|L3-0799]] of tea. Still, she was moved by Dr. Chen's [[patience|L3-0619]] with every animal.

On her last day, an old man brought in his sick cat. When Dr. Chen told him the cat would be fine, he thanked her again and again with [[sincere|L3-0797]] joy. The moment [[reminded|L3-0717]] Mia of the little bird, and she knew this was the work she wanted to do. Now she is studying hard for a [[scholarship|L3-0765]], and her parents have changed their minds. "A job you love," her mother said, "may be the most sensible choice of all."
zh: Mia 是台南的一名高三生。自從小時候在家裡院子發現一隻受傷的小鳥，她就一直想成為獸醫。不過，她的父母心存疑慮。「何不選個比較實際的工作，像是去銀行上班？」爸爸嘆了口氣問道。
為了弄清楚這份工作適不適合自己，Mia 花了一星期到一家動物醫院跟著陳醫師見習。這比她預期的還要辛苦。她幫忙刷洗地板，在手術中把剪刀遞給陳醫師，還安撫一隻怕打針的小牧羊犬。空閒時間少得可憐，看診之間她只能匆匆啜一口茶。儘管如此，陳醫師對每一隻動物的耐心讓她很感動。
見習的最後一天，一位老先生帶著生病的貓來看診。當陳醫師告訴他貓咪會沒事時，他帶著真誠的喜悅一再道謝。那一刻讓 Mia 想起了那隻小鳥，她知道這就是她想做的工作。現在她正努力讀書爭取獎學金，而她的父母也改變了想法。媽媽說：「做一份自己熱愛的工作，或許才是最明智的選擇。」

questions.stem: Why did Mia's father want her to think about another job at first?
options: He thought working in a bank was a more sensible choice.
He wanted her to become a teacher.
He thought she was not good at science.
questions.explain: 第一段爸爸嘆氣說「何不選個比較實際的工作，像是去銀行上班？」，可見他認為銀行工作比較穩當，故選 (A)。(B)、(C)、(D) 文中都沒有提到。
questions.evidence: "Why not choose something more sensible, like working in a bank?" her father asked with a sigh.

questions.stem: Which of the following did Mia NOT do at the animal hospital?
options: She gave a cat a shot by herself.
questions.explain: 第二段列出 Mia 做的事：刷地板、遞剪刀、安撫怕打針的小狗，並沒有說她自己替貓打針，故選 (C)。題目問的是「沒有」做的事，(A)、(B)、(D) 文中都有提到。
questions.evidence: She helped scrub the floors, handed Dr. Chen scissors during an operation, and calmed a young shepherd dog that was afraid of needles.

questions.stem: In paragraph 2, the word "shadowing" is closest in meaning to ______.
options: hiding from someone in the dark
following someone at work to learn about the job
questions.explain: Mia 是為了了解這份工作是否適合自己，才到醫院一整週跟在陳醫師身邊做事，所以 shadowing 在此指「跟在某人身邊見習」，故選 (B)。(A) 是 shadow「影子」的聯想，但文中不是躲起來的意思。
questions.evidence: To find out if the job was right for her, Mia spent a week shadowing Dr. Chen at an animal hospital.

questions.stem: What can we infer from the last paragraph?
options: Mia has decided to work in a bank.
The old man's cat could not be saved.
Dr. Chen asked Mia to stop studying.
Mia's week at the hospital made her dream even stronger.
questions.explain: 最後一天的經歷讓 Mia 確定「這就是她想做的工作」，她現在努力爭取獎學金，可推知這次見習讓她的夢想更堅定，故選 (D)。(B) 與文意相反，陳醫師說貓咪會沒事。
questions.evidence: The moment reminded Mia of the little bird, and she knew this was the work she wanted to do.

vocab.stem: During the long dry season, water became ______, so people had to use it carefully.
vocab.explain: 漫長的乾季裡水變得「稀少」，所以大家必須節約用水，故選 scarce。sincere（真誠的）、senior（年長的）、sensible（明智的）都不能用來形容水量。

vocab.stem: Thanks to a ______ from the university, Ben does not have to pay for his studies.
vocab.explain: 多虧大學提供的「獎學金」，Ben 不必支付學費，故選 scholarship。shepherd（牧羊人）、saucer（茶碟）、scarf（圍巾）都無法讓人免繳學費。

title: The Green Lady of New York
paragraphs: For more than a hundred years, visitors to New York have [[stared|L3-0836]] up at a tall green lady holding a torch high in the air. The [[Statue|L3-0838]] of [[Liberty|L3-0489]], a gift from the people of France to the United States, was opened to the public in 1886.

Building it was not easy. A [[skillful|L3-0803]] artist from France designed her face and body, but such a tall figure also had to stay [[stable|L3-0832]] in strong sea winds. Gustave Eiffel, who later built the Eiffel [[Tower|L3-0921]] in Paris, designed the iron [[structure|L3-0856]] inside. It holds the statue [[steady|L3-0839]] while letting its thin metal skin move a little in the wind. The statue was later shipped [[overseas|L3-0598]] in hundreds of pieces.
Here is a surprise: the lady was not always green. Her skin is made of copper, which first shone like a new [[penny|L3-0627]]. Over many years, air and sea water slowly turned it green.

Today, the park [[staff|L3-0834]] welcomes visitors from all over the world. Those who climb up to her head must take narrow, [[steep|L3-0842]] stairs, and many say their legs feel [[stiff|L3-0844]] the next day. If you visit New York [[someday|L3-0814]], don't [[skip|L3-0805]] the climb. The view is worth it.
zh: 一百多年來，到紐約的遊客總會抬頭凝視一位高舉火炬的綠色高大女士。自由女神像是法國人民送給美國的禮物，於 1886 年開放給大眾參觀。
建造這座雕像並不容易。一位技藝精湛的法國藝術家設計了她的臉和身體，但這麼高的雕像還必須在強烈的海風中保持穩固。後來在巴黎建造艾菲爾鐵塔的古斯塔夫・艾菲爾，設計了雕像內部的鐵製結構。這個結構讓雕像穩穩站立，同時讓外層薄薄的金屬外皮能隨風稍微移動。完成的雕像後來被分成好幾百塊，用船運送到海外。
說個讓人意外的事：這位女士並不是一直都是綠色的。她的外皮是銅做的，起初就像一枚新的一分錢硬幣那樣閃閃發亮。經過多年，空氣和海水慢慢讓它變成了綠色。
如今，公園的工作人員迎接來自世界各地的遊客。想爬到她頭部的人必須走又窄又陡的樓梯，許多人說隔天腿都變得僵硬痠痛。如果你有一天去紐約，可別略過這段攀爬，因為那裡的景色值得一看。

questions.stem: According to the passage, who gave the Statue of Liberty to the United States?
questions.explain: 第一段寫明自由女神像是「法國人民送給美國的禮物」，故選 (D)。(B) 艾菲爾只負責設計雕像內部的鐵製結構，並不是送禮的人。
questions.evidence: The Statue of Liberty, a gift from the people of France to the United States, was opened to the public in 1886.

questions.stem: Why did the statue need an iron structure inside?
options: To keep it steady in strong sea winds
To make its skin turn green
To help visitors reach the torch
To make it lighter for the trip overseas
questions.explain: 第二段說這麼高的雕像必須在強烈海風中保持穩固，而內部的鐵製結構能讓雕像穩穩站立，故選 (A)。(B) 雕像變綠是空氣和海水造成的，與內部結構無關。
questions.evidence: It holds the statue steady while letting its thin metal skin move a little in the wind.

questions.stem: The word "stiff" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: hard to move and a little painful
questions.explain: 爬完又窄又陡的樓梯後，隔天腿會「僵硬、不靈活」，stiff 在此指肌肉痠痛、難以活動，故選 (C)。(B) 意思是「輕快的」，正好與爬樓梯後的疲累相反。
questions.evidence: Those who climb up to her head must take narrow, steep stairs, and many say their legs feel stiff the next day.

questions.stem: What can we infer from paragraph 3?
options: The statue was painted green in France.
When the statue was new, it was a shiny brown color.
The statue will turn white in the future.
People in New York did not like the statue's color.
questions.explain: 第三段說雕像的銅外皮起初「像一枚新的一分錢硬幣那樣閃亮」，新的銅幣是亮亮的紅褐色，所以可推知雕像剛完成時並不是綠色，而是閃亮的褐色，故選 (B)。(A) 錯誤，綠色是多年來空氣和海水造成的，不是漆上去的。
